sentences.zh: 張澍，字介侯，武威人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shu, styled Jiehou, was a native of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shu, whose style name was Jiehou, came from Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 父應舉，有孝行。

translations.literal: His father Yingju was noted for filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yingju was renowned for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，澍年十八，成進士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Jiaqing reign, Shu at age eighteen passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1799, at the age of eighteen, Shu passed the highest civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 是科得人最盛，澍選庶吉士，文詞博麗。

translations.literal: That examination cohort was the most distinguished; Shu was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, his literary compositions broad and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: That year's examination produced an exceptionally strong cohort; Shu was chosen for the Hanlin Academy, and his writing was learned and elegant.

sentences.zh: 散館改知縣，初令玉屏，以病歸。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the Hanlin, he was changed to county magistrate; first appointed to Yuping, he returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After completing his Hanlin training he was assigned as a county magistrate, first to Yuping, but soon returned home due to illness.

sentences.zh: 敘防河勞，選屏山，攝興文，丁父艱。

translations.literal: His service in river defense was recorded; he was selected for Pingshan, acted as magistrate of Xingwen, and entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: Credit for his work on flood control earned him appointment to Pingshan; he also served temporarily as magistrate of Xingwen before entering mourning upon his father's death.

sentences.zh: 再起，知永新。

translations.literal: Recalled to office, he served as magistrate of Yongxin.
translations.idiomatic: Called back to service, he became magistrate of Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 署臨江通判，坐徵解緩，罷官。

translations.literal: He acted as subprefect of Linjiang; for slow tax remittance he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as acting subprefect of Linjiang, he was removed from office for delays in forwarding collected taxes.

sentences.zh: 開復，補瀘溪，復以憂去。

translations.literal: Restored to office, he was assigned to Luxi, then again left on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Reinstated, he was posted to Luxi, but once more left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 澍性亢直，所至輒有聲。

translations.literal: Shu was by nature lofty and upright; wherever he went he quickly gained a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was forthright and unyielding by temperament, and wherever he served he soon made a name for himself.

sentences.zh: 在黔時，巡撫初彭齡過縣，澍杖其僕之索金者。

translations.literal: While in Guizhou, when Governor Chu Pengling passed through the county, Shu had beaten a servant who was demanding money.
translations.idiomatic: In Guizhou, when Governor Chu Pengling passed through his county, Shu had a servant flogged for extorting money.

sentences.zh: 座主蔣攸銛督四川，甫下車，舉劾屬吏，風采嚴峻。

translations.literal: His patron Jiang Youshen supervised Sichuan; as soon as he took office he impeached subordinate officials, his bearing stern and severe.
translations.idiomatic: His examination patron Jiang Youshen became governor-general of Sichuan and, the moment he assumed office, began impeaching subordinates with stern and formidable authority.

sentences.zh: 澍上書論其循情市恩，黜陟不當，以此官不遂。

translations.literal: Shu submitted a memorial arguing that Jiang showed favoritism to curry goodwill and that promotions and dismissals were improper; for this his official career did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized the throne charging that Jiang traded in favoritism and made improper appointments and removals; because of this his own career never advanced.

sentences.zh: 務博覽經史，皆有纂著。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to wide reading of the classics and histories, and on all had compiled works.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics and histories and produced compilations on each field he studied.

sentences.zh: 遊跡半天下，詩文益富。

translations.literal: His travels covered half the empire, and his poetry and prose grew ever richer.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled across much of the empire, and his poetry and prose grew ever more abundant.

sentences.zh: 留心關、隴文獻，蒐輯刊刻之。

translations.literal: He attended to documents of the Guan and Long regions, collecting and publishing them.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted attention to the literary heritage of the Guan and Long regions, gathering and printing its texts.

sentences.zh: 纂五涼舊聞、三古人苑、續黔書、秦音、蜀典，而姓氏五書尤為絕學。

translations.literal: He compiled Old Reports of the Five Liang, Garden of the Three Ancients, Continued Records of Guizhou, Qin Dialect, and Shu Institutions, while his five books on surnames were especially supreme learning.
translations.idiomatic: Among his compilations were Old Reports of the Five Liang, Garden of the Three Ancients, Continued Records of Guizhou, Qin Dialect, and Shu Institutions; his five works on surnames were regarded as scholarship of the highest order.

sentences.zh: 自著詩文外，又有詩小序翼、說文引經考證。

translations.literal: Apart from his own poetry and prose, he also had Wings to the Small Prefaces of the Odes and Textual Verification of the Shuowen jiezi's Citations of the Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Besides his own literary writings, he also authored Wings to the Small Prefaces of the Odes and Textual Verification of Classical Citations in the Shuowen jiezi.

sentences.zh: 同時甘肅有與之同名者，曰邢澍，字​​雨民，階州人也。

translations.literal: At the same time in Gansu there was another of the same given name, called Xing Shu, styled Yumin, a native of Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary Gansu had another scholar also named Shu: Xing Shu, styled Yumin, from Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 兩人學派亦略相近。

translations.literal: The scholarly schools of the two men were also roughly similar.
translations.idiomatic: The two men's scholarly orientations were also much alike.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十五年進士，官至南安知府。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year of Qianlong, a jinshi, he rose in office to prefect of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year of Qianlong, a jinshi degree-holder, he eventually served as prefect of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 好古博聞，孫星衍輯寰宇訪碑錄，多資於澍。

translations.literal: Fond of antiquity and broad in learning, when Sun Xingyan compiled his Record of Stele Visits Throughout the Realm he drew heavily on Shu.
translations.idiomatic: A lover of antiquity with wide learning, he supplied much of the material for Sun Xingyan's Record of Stele Visits Throughout the Realm.

sentences.zh: 著有關右經籍考、兩漢希姓錄、金石文字辨異、守雅堂集。

translations.literal: His works include Examination of Classics of the Guanxi Region, Record of Rare Surnames of the Two Han, Differentiation of Inscriptions in Metal and Stone, and the Shouya Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Examination of Classics of the Guanxi Region, Record of Rare Surnames of the Two Han, Differentiation of Inscriptions in Metal and Stone, and the Shouya Hall Collection.

sentences.zh: 莫與儔，字猶人，獨山州人。

translations.literal: Mo Yuchou, styled Youren, was a native of Dushan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Yuchou, whose style name was Youren, came from Dushan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少有志操，兄歿，持期服，不與試，

translations.literal: In youth he had resolve and principle; when his elder brother died he observed the full year of mourning and did not take examinations.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed strong moral purpose; when his elder brother died he observed the full year of mourning and refused to sit for examinations.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，朱珪、阮元總裁會試，所拔取多樸學知名士，與儔亦以是年成進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, Zhu Gui and Ruan Yuan presided over the metropolitan examination; those they selected were mostly renowned scholars of plain learning, and Yuchou also in that year became a jinshi and was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, when Zhu Gui and Ruan Yuan presided over the metropolitan examination, they favored many well-known scholars of solid classical learning; Yuchou passed that year as well and was selected for the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 散館，改令鹽源縣。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the Hanlin, he was changed to magistrate of Yanyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: After completing his Hanlin training he was appointed magistrate of Yanyuan County.

sentences.zh: 俗，富民買田好擇取無稅者，貧民往往鬻產存賦，久輒逃亡。

translations.literal: By custom, when wealthy men bought land they preferred plots without tax liability; poor men often sold their property yet still owed tax, and after long periods would flee.
translations.idiomatic: Local custom favored wealthy buyers who chose untaxed land, while poor households often sold their fields yet still owed tax assessments and, in time, fled as refugees.

sentences.zh: 與儔責賦富人，而貰其隱佔罪。

translations.literal: Yuchou held wealthy men responsible for the tax burden and fined them for concealed occupation of land.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchou made wealthy landowners bear the tax obligations and fined them for concealed landholding.

sentences.zh: 又上言河西寧遠子稅所府隸橫徵病民，得裁去。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that the sub-tax office of Ningyuan in Hexi, subordinate to the prefecture, levied oppressively and harmed the people; the levy was cut back.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that the Ningyuan sub-tax office in Hexi, under prefectural control, was levying oppressive surcharges that harmed the people; the abuses were abolished.

sentences.zh: 木里喇嗎左所​​有山產銀銅，布政使符縣開礦，與儔持不可，以為礦山實土官經堂所據，奸民所呈地圖距經堂遠，實無礦，開廠聚眾，滋擾夷境，貪小利，賈大釁，事誠不便。

translations.literal: In the Muli Lama Left Office there were mountains producing silver and copper; the provincial treasurer ordered the county to open mines. Yuchou held this impermissible, arguing that the mine mountains were in fact held by the native chieftain's scripture hall; the map presented by scheming men was far from the scripture hall and in truth had no ore; opening works and gathering crowds would breed disturbance in the Yi frontier; to covet small profit and invite great strife was truly inexpedient.
translations.idiomatic: The Muli Lama Left Office had mountains rich in silver and copper, and the provincial treasurer ordered the county to open mines there. Yuchou objected, showing that the mountains actually belonged to the native chieftain's scripture hall, that the map submitted by scheming men lay far from it and showed no real ore, and that opening mines and gathering workers would disturb the Yi frontier—trading small gain for great trouble was plainly unwise.

sentences.zh: 大吏檄與儔覆勘，至則礦山果在經堂右。

translations.literal: The high officials ordered Yuchou to reinspect; on arrival the mine mountains were indeed to the right of the scripture hall.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials ordered Yuchou to reinspect the site, and he found the mountains were indeed just to the right of the scripture hall.

sentences.zh: 其眾嚴兵以待，既瞻與儔貌，聆其溫語，皆解甲羅拜。

translations.literal: The crowd stood in arms awaiting him; once they beheld Yuchou's appearance and heard his gentle words, all laid aside armor and bowed in ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen had armed themselves to meet him, but once they saw Yuchou's bearing and heard his gentle words, they laid down their weapons and bowed before him in ranks.

sentences.zh: 縣令至，土司例有供餽，盡卻之，又懸諸禁。

translations.literal: When a magistrate arrived, the native chieftain by custom made offerings of provisions; he refused them all and posted prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a magistrate arrived, the native chieftain customarily sent provisions as gifts; he refused them all and posted prohibitions against the practice.

sentences.zh: 比還，老幼遮道獻酒，填咽不得前。

translations.literal: When he returned, old and young blocked the road offering wine, filling it so he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, young and old blocked the road to offer wine until the way was so crowded he could not pass.

sentences.zh: 舉治行卓異，以父憂去。

translations.literal: He was recommended for outstanding administration, then left office on his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for outstanding administration, he then left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 母老，遂請終養。

translations.literal: His mother was aged, and he therefore requested lifelong care for her.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was elderly, and he petitioned to remain at home and care for her for life.

sentences.zh: 久之，被吏部檄復起，自請改教授，選遵義。

translations.literal: After long time he was summoned by the Board of Civil Appointments to return; he himself requested transfer to instructor and was selected for Zunyi.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval the Board of Civil Appointments recalled him to service; he asked instead to become an instructor and was appointed at Zunyi.

sentences.zh: 士人聞其至，爭請受業。

translations.literal: When scholars heard of his arrival, they vied to request instruction under him.
translations.idiomatic: When scholars learned he had arrived, they competed to study under him.

sentences.zh: 學舍如蜂房，猶不足，僦居半城市。

translations.literal: The school quarters were like beehives yet still insufficient; he rented lodgings over half the city.
translations.idiomatic: The school buildings were packed like beehives yet still could not hold everyone, and he rented rooms across half the city.

sentences.zh: 旦暮進諸生而詔之：「學以盡其下焉者而已，上焉者聽其自至可也。

translations.literal: Morning and evening he summoned the students and instructed them: "Study is only to exhaust the lower level; the higher level may be left to come of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening he gathered his students and told them: "Learning means mastering the fundamentals; the highest attainments may be left to arrive on their own.

sentences.zh: 程、朱氏之論，窮神達化，不越灑埽應對日用之常。

translations.literal: The doctrines of the Cheng and Zhu schools, in plumbing spirit and penetrating transformation, do not go beyond the everyday constants of sweeping, responding, and daily conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The teachings of the Cheng and Zhu schools, for all their talk of plumbing spirit and penetrating transformation, do not go beyond the everyday acts of sweeping floors and answering one's duties.

sentences.zh: 至六藝故訓，則國朝專經大師，實邁近古。」

translations.literal: As for the old exegesis of the Six Arts, the masters of specialized classics in our dynasty truly surpass recent antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: In the classical exegesis of the Six Arts, the Qing masters of specialized learning truly surpass the scholars of recent centuries."

sentences.zh: 其稱江、閻、惠、陳、段、王父子，未嘗隔三宿不言，聽者如旱苗之得膏雨。

translations.literal: In speaking of Jiang, Yan, Hui, Chen, Duan, and the Wang father and son, he never went three nights without mentioning them; listeners were like drought-stricken seedlings receiving nourishing rain.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of Jiang, Yan, Hui, Chen, Duan, and the Wang father and son so often that scarcely three days passed without their names on his lips, and his listeners were like parched seedlings revived by rain.

sentences.zh: 其後門人鄭珍及子友芝遂通許、鄭之學，為西南大師。

translations.literal: Thereafter his disciples Zheng Zhen and his son Youzhi mastered the learning of Xu and Zheng and became great masters of the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Later his disciples Zheng Zhen and his son Youzhi mastered the scholarship of the Xu and Zheng schools and became the leading scholars of the southwest.

sentences.zh: 與儔著二南近說，詩文散佚。

translations.literal: Yuchou authored Recent Explanations of the Two Souths; his poetry and prose are scattered and lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchou wrote Recent Explanations of the Two Souths; his poetry and prose have mostly been lost.

sentences.zh: 友芝記其言行為過庭碎錄。

translations.literal: Youzhi recorded his words and conduct in Miscellaneous Records from the Courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi recorded his father's teachings in Miscellaneous Records from the Courtyard.

sentences.zh: 友芝，字子偲。

translations.literal: Youzhi, styled Zisi.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi, whose style name was Zisi.

sentences.zh: 家世傳業，通會漢、宋。

translations.literal: His family for generations transmitted the profession; he united Han and Song learning.
translations.idiomatic: He came from a family of scholars and reconciled Han-dynasty philology with Song Neo-Confucianism.

sentences.zh: 工詩。

translations.literal: He was skilled in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He was an accomplished poet.

sentences.zh: 真行篆隸書不類唐以後人，世爭寶貴。

translations.literal: His regular, running, seal, and clerical scripts did not resemble post-Tang men; the world vied to treasure them.
translations.idiomatic: His regular, running, seal, and clerical scripts bore none of the manner of post-Tang calligraphers, and collectors prized them highly.

sentences.zh: 友芝亦樂易近人，癯貌玉立，而介特內含。

translations.literal: Youzhi was also easy and approachable, lean in appearance standing like jade, yet with firm integrity within.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi was affable and approachable, spare and upright as jade in bearing, yet inwardly possessed of unyielding integrity.

sentences.zh: 道光十一年舉人，在京師遠跡權貴。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Daoguang, a provincial graduate, in the capital he kept far from the tracks of the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Daoguang, a provincial graduate, he kept his distance from powerful patrons while in the capital.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼、曾國藩皆其舊好，留居幕府，評騭書史外，榮利泊如也。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi and Zeng Guofan were both his old friends; he stayed in their staffs, and apart from appraising books and histories he was indifferent to glory and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi and Zeng Guofan were old friends; he served in their staffs appraising books and histories, yet remained utterly indifferent to rank and gain.

sentences.zh: 咸豐時，嘗選取縣令，棄去。

translations.literal: In the Xianfeng period he was once selected for county magistrate but declined.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng reign he was once selected for a county magistracy but refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 至是中外大臣密疏薦其學行，有詔徵至，复謝不就。

translations.literal: At this time ministers at court and in the provinces secretly memorialized recommending his learning and conduct; an edict summoned him, but again he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: By then ministers at court and in the provinces had privately recommended his scholarship and character; the throne summoned him, but once again he declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 著黔詩紀略、遵義府志、聲韻考略、郘庭詩鈔、宋元舊本經眼錄、樗繭譜注、唐本說文木部箋異。

translations.literal: His works include Outline of Guizhou Poetry, Gazetteer of Zunyi Prefecture, Brief Study of Phonology, Luoting Poetry Drafts, Record of Song and Yuan Old Editions Seen, Commentary on the Silkworm Treatise, and Notes on Variants in the Wood Radical of the Tang Shuowen.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Outline of Guizhou Poetry, Gazetteer of Zunyi Prefecture, Brief Study of Phonology, Luoting Poetry Drafts, Record of Song and Yuan Old Editions Seen, Commentary on the Silkworm Treatise, and Notes on Variants in the Wood Radical of the Tang Shuowen.

sentences.zh: 陸繼輅，字祁孫，陽湖人。

translations.literal: Lu Jilu, styled Qisun, was a native of Yanghu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jilu, whose style name was Qisun, came from Yanghu.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，生母林嚴督之，非其人，禁勿與遊。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, his birth mother Lin strictly supervised him; if a companion was not the right sort, she forbade association.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in childhood, he was raised under the strict discipline of his mother Lin, who forbade him to associate with anyone she judged unworthy.

sentences.zh: 甫成童，出應試，得識丁履恆，歸告母，母察其賢，始令與結。

translations.literal: Just upon reaching youth he went out to take examinations, met Ding Lüheng, returned and told his mother; his mother perceived Ding's worth and only then allowed them to form a bond.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he came of age he went to take examinations, met Ding Lüheng, and told his mother on returning home; she judged Ding worthy and only then allowed them to become friends.

sentences.zh: 其後益交莊曾詒、張琦、惲敬、洪飴孫輩，學日進。

translations.literal: Thereafter he increasingly associated with Zhuang Zengyi, Zhang Qi, Yun Jing, Hong Yisun and others, and his learning advanced daily.
translations.idiomatic: He later befriended Zhuang Zengyi, Zhang Qi, Yun Jing, Hong Yisun, and others, and his scholarship steadily improved.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年舉人，選合肥訓導。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing he became a provincial graduate and was selected as director of studies at Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: In 1800 he passed the provincial examination and was appointed director of studies at Hefei.

sentences.zh: 以修安徽省志敘勞，遷貴溪令，三年引疾歸。

translations.literal: For compiling the Anhui provincial gazetteer his service was recorded; he was transferred to magistrate of Guixi, and after three years cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Credit for compiling the Anhui provincial gazetteer earned him appointment as magistrate of Guixi; after three years he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 繼輅儀幹秀削，聲清如唳鶴。

translations.literal: Jilu's bearing was slender and refined, his voice clear as a crying crane.
translations.idiomatic: Jilu was slender and refined in bearing, with a voice as clear as a crane's cry.

sentences.zh: 不以塵務經心，惟肆力於詩。

translations.literal: He did not let worldly affairs occupy his mind, but devoted his strength solely to poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He paid no heed to worldly affairs and devoted himself entirely to poetry.

sentences.zh: 清溫多風，如其人也。

translations.literal: Clear, warm, and full of spirit—like the man himself.
translations.idiomatic: His verse was clear, gentle, and spirited—like the man himself.

sentences.zh: 常州自張惠言、惲敬以古​​文名，繼輅與董士錫同時並起，世遂推為陽湖派，與桐城相抗。

translations.literal: From Changzhou, since Zhang Huiyan and Yun Jing were famed for ancient-style prose, Jilu and Dong Shixi rose together at the same time; the age therefore promoted them as the Yanghu school, rivaling Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhang Huiyan and Yun Jing had made Changzhou famous for ancient-style prose, Jilu and Dong Shixi rose together in the same generation, and the age hailed them as leaders of the Yanghu school to rival Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 然繼輅選七家古文，以為惠言、敬受文法於錢伯坰，伯坰親業劉大櫆之門；

translations.literal: Yet Jilu selected ancient prose of seven masters, holding that Huiyan and Jing received literary methods from Qian Bokun, and Bokun personally studied under Liu Dakui's gate;
translations.idiomatic: Yet in his anthology of seven masters of ancient prose, Jilu held that Huiyan and Jing learned their craft from Qian Bokun, who had studied directly under Liu Dakui;

sentences.zh: 蓋其淵源同出唐、宋大家，以上窺史、漢，桐城、陽湖，皆未嘗自標異也。

translations.literal: for their sources alike issued from the great masters of Tang and Song, looking upward to probe the Histories and Han; neither Tongcheng nor Yanghu had ever marked themselves as different.
translations.idiomatic: for their lineage alike reached back through the great Tang and Song masters toward the Histories and Han; neither Tongcheng nor Yanghu had truly set themselves apart.

sentences.zh: 繼輅著崇百藥齋集、合肥學舍札記。

translations.literal: Jilu authored the Chongbaiyao Studio Collection and Notes from the Hefei Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Jilu wrote the Chongbaiyao Studio Collection and Notes from the Hefei Academy.

sentences.zh: 從子耀遹，字劭文。

translations.literal: His nephew's son Yao Yu, styled Shaowen.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew's son Yao Yu, whose style name was Shaowen.

sentences.zh: 縣學生。

translations.literal: A county school student.
translations.idiomatic: He was a county school student.

sentences.zh: 工為詩，喜金石文字，與繼輅齊名。

translations.literal: Skilled in poetry, fond of inscriptions on metal and stone, he was equal in fame to Jilu.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at poetry and loved epigraphy, and was as renowned as Jilu himself.

sentences.zh: 其為人韜斂精采，而遇事侃侃無所撓。

translations.literal: In conduct he concealed his brilliance, yet when affairs arose he spoke forthrightly and was swayed by nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He was reserved in manner, yet when matters arose he spoke boldly and yielded to no pressure.

sentences.zh: 遊公卿間，尤長尺牘。

translations.literal: Traveling among high ministers, he was especially adept at letters.
translations.idiomatic: Moving among high officials, he was especially skilled at formal correspondence.

sentences.zh: 嘗客陝西巡撫幕，教匪反滑縣，那彥成過長安，聞耀遹名，即請見，為陳機宜數十事，因囑具草以聞，多施行。

translations.literal: He once served in the staff of the Shaanxi governor; when sect rebels rose in Huaxian, Na Yancheng passed through Chang'an, heard Yao Yu's fame, immediately requested an audience, and Yao set forth dozens of strategic points; he was told to draft a memorial, and many measures were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He once served on the staff of the Shaanxi governor. When sect rebels rose in Huaxian, Na Yancheng passed through Chang'an, heard of Yao Yu's reputation, and summoned him at once; Yao laid out dozens of strategic recommendations, drafted a memorial at his request, and many of the proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 道光初，舉孝廉方正，選阜寧教諭，卒。

translations.literal: Early in Daoguang he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt and Rectified, selected as instructor of Funing, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daoguang reign he was recommended as a Filial and Incorrupt scholar, appointed instructor at Funing, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 有雙白燕堂集、金石續編。

translations.literal: He left the Shuangbaiyan Hall Collection and Continuation of Metal and Stone Inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Shuangbaiyan Hall Collection and Continuation of Metal and Stone Inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 繼輅所鈔七家文者，大櫆、惠言、敬外，則方苞、姚鼐、朱仕琇、彭績也。

translations.literal: Of the seven masters' prose that Jilu copied, apart from Dakui, Huiyan, and Jing were Fang Bao, Yao Nai, Zhu Shixiu, and Peng Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The seven masters of ancient prose in Jilu's anthology, besides Dakui, Huiyan, and Jing, were Fang Bao, Yao Nai, Zhu Shixiu, and Peng Ji.

sentences.zh: 績，字秋士，長洲人。

translations.literal: Ji, styled Qiushi, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ji, whose style name was Qiushi, came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 品詣孤峻。

translations.literal: His character and attainment were solitary and severe.
translations.idiomatic: His character was austere and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 乾隆末，窮而客死。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianlong, in poverty he died as a guest far from home.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Qianlong reign he died in poverty far from home.

sentences.zh: 無子，年四十四。

translations.literal: He had no son; he was forty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son and was forty-four years old.

sentences.zh: 族子紹升曰：「人之吊先生者，悲其窮。

translations.literal: His clansman Shaosheng said: "Those who mourn the Master grieve his poverty.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Shaosheng said: "Those who came to mourn the Master lamented his poverty.

sentences.zh: 吾獨謂先生竹柏之性，有節有文采，其英亦元結、孟郊之匹，未見其窮也。」

translations.literal: I alone say the Master had the nature of bamboo and cypress, with joints and literary splendor; his spirit was a match for Yuan Jie and Meng Jiao—I do not see his poverty."
translations.idiomatic: I alone hold that the Master had the nature of bamboo and cypress—firm in integrity and rich in literary grace—and that his spirit rivaled Yuan Jie and Meng Jiao; I do not see him as poor at all."

sentences.zh: 有秋士遺集。

translations.literal: There is the Posthumous Collection of Qiushi.
translations.idiomatic: His Posthumous Collection of Qiushi survives.

sentences.zh: 餘六人皆自有傳。

translations.literal: The remaining six men each have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: The other six each have biographies of their own.

sentences.zh: 洪頤煊，字旌賢，臨海人。

translations.literal: Hong Yixuan, styled Jingxian, was a native of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Yixuan, whose style name was Jingxian, came from Linhai.

sentences.zh: 少時自力於學，與兄坤煊、弟震煊讀書僧寮，夜就佛鐙講誦不輟。

translations.literal: In youth he exerted himself in study; with elder brother Kunxuan and younger brother Zhenxuan he read in a monks' lodge, and at night by the Buddha lamp lectured and recited without cease.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he applied himself to learning; with his elder brother Kunxuan and younger brother Zhenxuan he studied in a monastery, lecturing and reciting by the Buddha lamp far into the night.

sentences.zh: 學使阮元招頤煊、震煊就學行省，名日起。

translations.literal: Education commissioner Ruan Yuan invited Yixuan and Zhenxuan to study at the provincial seat, and their fame rose daily.
translations.idiomatic: Education Commissioner Ruan Yuan invited Yixuan and Zhenxuan to study at the provincial capital, and their reputations grew daily.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年，充選拔貢生。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaqing he served as a selected tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: In 1801 he qualified as a selected tribute student.

sentences.zh: 入貲為州判，權知新興縣事。

translations.literal: He purchased office as assistant prefect and acted as magistrate of Xinxing County.
translations.idiomatic: He purchased the post of assistant prefect and served as acting magistrate of Xinxing County.

sentences.zh: 適阮元督粵，知頤煊學優非吏才，延致幕府，相與諮諏經史。

translations.literal: It happened that Ruan Yuan supervised Guangdong; knowing Yixuan's learning was superior but he was no man of official talent, he invited him to his staff to consult together on the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yuan was then governor-general of Guangdong; recognizing that Yixuan was a fine scholar but no administrator, he brought him onto his staff to discuss the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 後卒於家。

translations.literal: Later he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at home.

sentences.zh: 性喜聚書，廣購嶺南舊本至三萬餘卷，碑版彝器多世所罕覯。

translations.literal: By nature fond of collecting books, he widely purchased old editions from Lingnan to more than thirty thousand volumes; stele and ritual vessels were mostly what the age rarely saw.
translations.idiomatic: He loved collecting books and amassed more than thirty thousand volumes of old Lingnan editions, along with stele rubbings and ritual bronzes rarely seen in his day.

sentences.zh: 著禮經宮室答問、孔子三朝記、管子義證、漢志水道疏證、讀書叢錄、台州札記、筠軒詩文集。

translations.literal: His works include Answers on Palace Chambers in the Book of Rites, Record of Confucius's Three Audiences, Evidential Commentary on the Guanzi, Exegesis of Waterways in the Han Bibliographic Treatise, Miscellany from Reading, Taizhou Notes, and the Yunxuan Poetry and Prose Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Answers on Palace Chambers in the Book of Rites, Record of Confucius's Three Audiences, Evidential Commentary on the Guanzi, Exegesis of Waterways in the Han Bibliographic Treatise, Miscellany from Reading, Taizhou Notes, and the Yunxuan Poetry and Prose Collection.

sentences.zh: 坤煊，字載厚。

translations.literal: Kunxuan, styled Zaihou.
translations.idiomatic: Kunxuan, whose style name was Zaihou.

sentences.zh: 乾隆末，以拔貢生舉鄉試，題名後十餘日卒。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianlong, as a selected tribute student he passed the provincial examination; a little more than ten days after being listed he died.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Qianlong reign he passed the provincial examination as a selected tribute student and died little more than ten days after his name was posted.

sentences.zh: 震煊，字百里。

translations.literal: Zhenxuan, styled Baili.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenxuan, whose style name was Baili.

sentences.zh: 精選學，詩才敏贍。

translations.literal: He excelled in selected learning; his poetic talent was quick and abundant.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in classical scholarship, and his poetic talent was quick and prolific.

sentences.zh: 阮元修經籍篡詁、十三經校勘記皆任其役。

translations.literal: When Ruan Yuan compiled the Collected Glosses on the Classics and the Collation Notes on the Thirteen Classics, he entrusted the work to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yuan entrusted him with work on the Collected Glosses on the Classics and the Collation Notes on the Thirteen Classics.

sentences.zh: 後頤煊十二年充選拔貢生。

translations.literal: Twelve years after Yixuan, he served as a selected tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve years after his brother Yixuan, he qualified as a selected tribute student.

sentences.zh: 既廷試，貧不克歸，遂以客死。

translations.literal: After the palace examination, too poor to return home, he died as a guest far away.
translations.idiomatic: After the palace examination he was too poor to return home and died far from his native place.

sentences.zh: 著夏小正疏義。

translations.literal: He authored Exegesis of the Xia Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Exegesis of the Xia Calendar.

sentences.zh: 鄧顯鶴，字子立，新化人。

translations.literal: Deng Xianhe, styled Zili, was a native of Xinhua.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Xianhe, whose style name was Zili, came from Xinhua.

sentences.zh: 少與同里歐陽紹洛以詩相勵，遊客四方，所至傾動。

translations.literal: In youth with fellow townsman Ouyang Shaoluo he encouraged each other in poetry; traveling as a guest in all directions, wherever he went he stirred admiration.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he and his fellow townsman Ouyang Shaoluo spurred each other on in poetry; traveling widely, he won admiration wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶九年舉人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiaqing he became a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1804 he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 厭薄仕進，一以篡著為事，系楚南文獻者三十年，學者稱之曰湘皋先生。

translations.literal: Disdaining advancement through office, he devoted himself entirely to compilation; for thirty years he was tied to the documents of south Chu, and scholars called him Master Xianggao.
translations.idiomatic: Disdaining official careerism, he devoted himself entirely to scholarly compilation; for thirty years he preserved the literary heritage of southern Hunan, and scholars called him Master Xianggao.

sentences.zh: 內行修，事兄白首無間，撫其子勤於己子。

translations.literal: His inner conduct was cultivated; in serving his elder brother he was without estrangement to white hair; in raising his brother's son he was as diligent as with his own.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright in private life, remained devoted to his elder brother to the end of their days, and raised his nephew as diligently as his own sons.

sentences.zh: 尤篤於師友風義。

translations.literal: He was especially devoted to the moral obligations of teachers and friends.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially steadfast in loyalty to teachers and friends.

sentences.zh: 嘗以為洞庭以南，服嶺以北，屈原、賈誼傷心之地也，歷代通人志士相望，​​而文字湮鬱不宣。

translations.literal: He once held that south of Dongting and north of the Five Ridges was the land where Qu Yuan and Jia Yi had grieved; through the ages men of broad learning and aspiring scholars succeeded one another, yet writings were buried in obscurity and not brought forth.
translations.idiomatic: He held that the region south of Dongting Lake and north of the Five Ridges was the land of Qu Yuan and Jia Yi's sorrow, where learned men and loyal scholars had succeeded one another through the ages, yet whose writings remained buried and unknown.

sentences.zh: 乃從事搜討，每得貞烈遺行於殘簡斷冊中，為之驚喜狂拜，汲汲彰顯，若大譴隨其後。

translations.literal: He therefore undertook search and collation; whenever he obtained the surviving deeds of the chaste and steadfast in broken slips and torn registers, he would in surprise and joy bow wildly, urgently making them manifest, as if great punishment followed close behind.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore searched the archives, and whenever he found records of loyal martyrs in damaged manuscripts, he would rejoice and bow in reverence, rushing to publish them as though great blame would follow if he delayed.

sentences.zh: 凡所著有資江耆舊集、沅湘耆舊集、楚寶增輯考異、武岡志、寶慶志、朱子五忠祠傳略及續傳、明季湖南殉節傳略。

translations.literal: Among his works are Collections of Elders of the Zijiang, Collections of Elders of the Yuan and Xiang, Supplemental Collation and Variants of the Chu Treasure, Gazetteers of Wugang and Baojing, Brief Biographies of the Five Loyal Temple of Zhu Xi and its continuation, and Brief Biographies of Martyrs of Hunan in the Late Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Collections of Elders of the Zijiang, Collections of Elders of the Yuan and Xiang, Supplemental Collation and Variants of the Chu Treasure, gazetteers of Wugang and Baojing, Brief Biographies of the Five Loyal Temple of Zhu Xi and its continuation, and Brief Biographies of Martyrs of Hunan in the Late Ming.

sentences.zh: 又易述、毛詩表、南村草堂詩文集，共數百卷。

translations.literal: He also had Expositions on the Changes, Tables of the Mao Odes, and the Nancun Thatched Hall Poetry and Prose Collection, totaling several hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Expositions on the Changes, Tables of the Mao Odes, and the Nancun Thatched Hall Poetry and Prose Collection, totaling several hundred volumes.

sentences.zh: 晚授寧鄉訓導。

translations.literal: Late in life he was appointed director of studies at Ningxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he was appointed director of studies at Ningxiang.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 同時萬希槐，字蔚亭，黃岡人。

translations.literal: At the same time Wan Xihuai, styled Weiting, was a native of Huanggang.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary with him was Wan Xihuai, whose style name was Weiting, from Huanggang.

sentences.zh: 以廩膳生官南漳訓導。

translations.literal: As a granary-stipend student he became director of studies at Nanzhang.
translations.idiomatic: As a granary-stipend student he was appointed director of studies at Nanzhang.

sentences.zh: 通經史百家言，著十三經證異。

translations.literal: He mastered the classics, histories, and the hundred schools; he authored Evidential Variants of the Thirteen Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the classics, histories, and the hundred schools, and wrote Evidential Variants of the Thirteen Classics.

sentences.zh: 困學紀聞集證，陳嵩慶推為王氏功臣。

translations.literal: His Collected Evidences to Notes from Difficult Study was praised by Chen Songqing as a meritorious servant of Wang Yinglin.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Songqing hailed his Collected Evidences to Notes from Difficult Study as an indispensable contribution to Wang Yinglin's scholarship.

sentences.zh: 周濟，字保緒，荊溪人。

translations.literal: Zhou Ji, styled Baoxu, was a native of Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ji, whose style name was Baoxu, came from Jingxi.

sentences.zh: 好讀史，喜觀古將帥兵略，騎射擊刺藝絕精。

translations.literal: He loved reading history and delighted in studying ancient generals' military strategies; in horsemanship, archery, and thrusting arts he was supremely skilled.
translations.idiomatic: He loved history and studied ancient generals' military strategies; he was supremely skilled in horsemanship, archery, and swordplay.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年進士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiaqing, a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Jiaqing, he was a jinshi degree-holder.

sentences.zh: 或謂之曰：「對策語幸無過激。」

translations.literal: Someone said to him: "In the policy essay, pray do not speak too boldly."
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned him: "In your policy essay, try not to be too outspoken."

sentences.zh: 濟曰：「始進，敢欺君乎！」

translations.literal: Ji said: "At my first advancement, how dare I deceive the ruler!"
translations.idiomatic: Ji replied: "At my first audience with the throne, how could I dare deceive my sovereign!"

sentences.zh: 及廷對，縱言天下事，字逾恆格。

translations.literal: When he faced the court in audience, he spoke freely on affairs of the realm, exceeding the usual word limit.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace audience he spoke freely on affairs of the realm, exceeding the prescribed length.

sentences.zh: 以三甲歸班選知縣，改就淮安府學教授。

translations.literal: As third-rank jinshi he returned to the roster and was selected as county magistrate, but changed to become professor of the Huai'an Prefecture school.
translations.idiomatic: Placed in the third rank of jinshi graduates, he was selected as a county magistrate but instead took the post of professor at the Huai'an Prefecture school.

sentences.zh: 上丁釋奠，禮畢，知府王轂就殿門外升輿，濟趨前阻之，知府不懌去，濟遂引疾歸。

translations.literal: On the upper ding day of the sacrifice to Confucius, when the rites were finished, Prefect Wang Gu stepped outside the hall to mount his carriage; Ji hurried forward to stop him; the prefect left displeased, and Ji then cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At the spring sacrifice to Confucius, when the rites were finished, Prefect Wang Gu stepped outside the hall to mount his carriage; Ji rushed forward to stop him. The prefect left in displeasure, and Ji resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 是秋冒賑事發，自轂以下吏皆得罪，濟以先去免。

translations.literal: That autumn a case of embezzling relief funds broke out; from Gu downward all officials were punished, but Ji escaped because he had left first.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn a scandal over embezzled relief funds broke out, and officials from Wang Gu downward were all punished; Ji was spared because he had already resigned.

sentences.zh: 淮南北鹽梟充斥，總督孫玉庭知濟能，以防撫事屬之。

translations.literal: North and south of the Huai, salt smugglers filled the land; Governor-General Sun Yuting knew Ji's ability and entrusted him with defense and pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Salt smugglers infested the Huai region; Governor-General Sun Yuting, recognizing Ji's ability, entrusted him with defense and pacification.

sentences.zh: 濟集營弁，勒以兵法，奸民皆斂跡。

translations.literal: Ji gathered camp officers and disciplined them with military law; scheming people all restrained their tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Ji assembled military officers and disciplined them according to military law, and the lawless all fell silent.

sentences.zh: 已而歎曰：「鹽務不理其本，徒緝私，私不可勝緝也。」

translations.literal: Soon he sighed and said: "Salt administration does not treat the root; merely suppressing smuggling—smuggling cannot be exhausted by suppression."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he sighed and said: "Salt administration ignores the root of the problem; merely suppressing smuggling can never end it."

sentences.zh: 因謝去。

translations.literal: He therefore resigned and left.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore resigned.

sentences.zh: 濟與李兆洛、張琦、包世臣訂交。

translations.literal: Ji formed friendships with Li Zhaoluo, Zhang Qi, and Bao Shichen.
translations.idiomatic: Ji formed close friendships with Li Zhaoluo, Zhang Qi, and Bao Shichen.

sentences.zh: 當是時，數吳中士有裨世用者，必首及世臣、濟兩人。

translations.literal: At that time, when counting Wu-region scholars useful to the age, Shichen and Ji were always named first.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, whenever scholars of the Wu region useful to public affairs were counted, Shichen and Ji were always named first.

sentences.zh: 濟雖以才自喜，一日盡屏豪習，閉門撰述，成晉略八十卷，例精辭潔，於攻取防守地勢多發明論贊中，非徒考訂已也。

translations.literal: Although Ji prided himself on talent, one day he completely put aside extravagant habits, closed his door to write, and completed eighty juan of Outline of Jin, with refined categories and clean diction; on terrain for attack, defense, and garrison he made many original expositions in his discussions—not mere collation.
translations.idiomatic: Though proud of his talents, Ji one day cast off his extravagant habits, shut his door to write, and completed eighty volumes of Outline of Jin, with refined organization and clean prose; in his discussions he offered original insights on terrain for attack and defense, going far beyond mere collation.

sentences.zh: 晚復任淮安教授，遴秀童教以樂舞，禮成，觀者盈千。

translations.literal: Late in life he again served as Huai'an professor, selected talented youths to teach music and dance; when the rites were completed, observers filled the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he again served as professor at Huai'an, selecting talented youths to teach ritual music and dance; when the ceremony was completed, more than a thousand people watched.

sentences.zh: 周天爵移督湖廣，邀濟偕行。

translations.literal: Zhou Tianjue was transferred to supervise Huguang and invited Ji to travel with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Tianjue was transferred to governor-general of Huguang, he invited Ji to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 道卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: He died on the road at age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the journey at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 陳鶴，字鶴齡，元和人。

translations.literal: Chen He, styled Heling, was a native of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Chen He, whose style name was Heling, came from Yuanhe.

sentences.zh: 操行修潔，亦精史學。

translations.literal: His conduct was cultivated and pure; he was also expert in historical studies.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and refined in conduct and also excelled in historical studies.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年進士，以主事分工部，出無車馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, a jinshi, as a director he served in the Works Bureau; when going out he had no carriage or horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiaqing, a jinshi, he served as a director in the Ministry of Works and went about on foot without carriage or horses.

sentences.zh: 與棲霞牟昌裕、​​陽山鄭士超有「工部三君子」之目。

translations.literal: With Qixia Mou Changyu and Yangshan Zheng Shichao he was known as one of the "Three Gentlemen of the Works Bureau."
translations.idiomatic: With Mou Changyu of Qixia and Zheng Shichao of Yangshan he was known as one of the "Three Gentlemen of the Works Bureau."

sentences.zh: 熟於明代​​事，輯明紀六十卷。

translations.literal: Well versed in Ming affairs, he compiled sixty juan of Ming Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Well versed in Ming history, he compiled sixty volumes of Ming Annals.

sentences.zh: 未成，卒。

translations.literal: Before completion he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died before the work was finished.

sentences.zh: 後八卷其孫克家續成之。

translations.literal: The last eight juan were continued to completion by his grandson Kejia.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Kejia completed the final eight volumes.

sentences.zh: 克家，道光末舉人。

translations.literal: Kejia, a provincial graduate at the end of Daoguang.
translations.idiomatic: Kejia passed the provincial examination late in the Daoguang reign.

sentences.zh: 官中書。

translations.literal: He served as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a secretarial officer in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後參張國梁軍事，殉難，贈知府銜。

translations.literal: Later he joined Zhang Guoliang's military affairs, died a martyr, and was posthumously granted the rank of prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Zhang Guoliang's staff, died in service, and was posthumously granted the rank of prefect.

sentences.zh: 徐松，字星伯，大興人。

translations.literal: Xu Song, styled Xingbo, was a native of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Song, whose style name was Xingbo, came from Daxing.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the tenth year of Jiaqing, he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1805 and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 簡湖南學政，坐事戍伊犁。

translations.literal: Selected as education commissioner of Hunan, for an offense he was banished to garrison duty at Yili.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed education commissioner of Hunan, he was later banished to Yili for an offense.

sentences.zh: 松留心文獻，既出關，置開方小冊，隨所至圖其山川曲折，成西域​​水道記，擬水經；

translations.literal: Song attended to documents; once beyond the pass he kept a square pocket notebook, mapping the twists of mountains and rivers wherever he went, and completed Record of Western Region Waterways, modeled on the Water Classic;
translations.idiomatic: Song devoted himself to documentary research; beyond the frontier he carried a pocket notebook, mapping the courses of mountains and rivers wherever he traveled, and completed Record of Western Region Waterways, modeled on the Water Classic;

sentences.zh: 復自為釋，以比道元之注。

translations.literal: He also wrote his own commentary, to compare with Li Daoyuan's notes.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote his own commentary, intended to rival Li Daoyuan's annotations.

sentences.zh: 又以新疆入版圖數十年，視同畿甸，而未有專書，乃纂述成編，於建置、控扼、錢糧、兵籍，言之尤詳。

translations.literal: Moreover, since Xinjiang had entered the map for several decades and was regarded like the capital region yet had no specialized book, he compiled and completed a work, speaking especially in detail on establishment, strategic control, revenue grain, and military registers.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xinjiang had been part of the empire for decades and was treated like the capital region yet lacked a dedicated study, he compiled a comprehensive work with detailed treatment of administration, strategic control, revenue, and military registers.

sentences.zh: 將軍松筠奏進其書，賜名新疆事略，特旨赦還，御製序付武英殿刊行。

translations.literal: General Songyun memorialized and presented his book; it was granted the title Brief Account of Xinjiang Affairs; by special edict he was pardoned and returned; an imperial preface was composed and entrusted to the Wuying Hall for printing.
translations.idiomatic: General Songyun presented his book to the throne; it was given the title Brief Account of Xinjiang Affairs; by special edict Xu was pardoned and recalled; the emperor wrote a preface and ordered its publication by the imperial printing office.

sentences.zh: 道光改元，起內閣中書，洊擢郎中，補御史，出知榆林府。

translations.literal: At the change of reign to Daoguang he was recalled as secretary of the Grand Secretariat, repeatedly promoted to director, appointed censor, and sent out as prefect of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daoguang reign he was recalled as a Grand Secretariat secretary, promoted to director, appointed censor, and then sent out as prefect of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 他所著有新斠注地理志集釋、漢書西域傳補注、唐兩京城坊考、唐登科記考、新疆賦共數十卷。

translations.literal: His other works include Collected Explanations of the Geography Monograph, Supplementary Notes to the Account of the Western Regions in the Han History, Examination of the Two Capitals' Wards in Tang, Examination of Tang Examination Records, and Rhapsody on Xinjiang, totaling several tens of juan.
translations.idiomatic: His other works include Collected Explanations of the Geography Monograph, Supplementary Notes to the Account of the Western Regions in the Han History, Examination of the Two Capitals' Wards in Tang, Examination of Tang Examination Records, and Rhapsody on Xinjiang, totaling several dozen volumes.

sentences.zh: 松喜延譽後進。

translations.literal: Song delighted in extending reputation to younger scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Song delighted in promoting younger scholars.

sentences.zh: 其客有沈垚者，字子惇，烏程人。

translations.literal: Among his guests was Shen Yao, styled Zidun, a native of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Among his protégés was Shen Yao, whose style name was Zidun, from Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 優貢生。

translations.literal: An outstanding tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: He was an outstanding tribute student.

sentences.zh: 性沉默，足不越關塞，好指畫絕域山川。

translations.literal: By nature silent, his feet never crossed passes and barriers; he loved to trace out mountains and rivers of remote regions.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet by nature, he never traveled beyond the frontier himself, yet loved to chart the mountains and rivers of distant lands.

sentences.zh: 初為何凌漢、陳用光所賞拔。

translations.literal: At first he was appreciated and promoted by He Linghan and Chen Yongguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was first recognized and promoted by He Linghan and Chen Yongguang.

sentences.zh: 入京師，館於松。

translations.literal: Entering the capital, he lodged with Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he lodged in Xu's household.

sentences.zh: 松稱其地學之精。

translations.literal: Song praised the refinement of his geographical studies.
translations.idiomatic: Xu praised the excellence of his geographical scholarship.

sentences.zh: 歙程恩澤嘗讀西遊記，擬為文疏通其說。

translations.literal: She County's Cheng Enze once read Journey to the West and planned to write an essay clarifying its doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Enze of She County once read Journey to the West and planned to write an essay explaining its geography.

sentences.zh: 及見垚所撰西遊記金山以東釋，歎曰：「遐荒萬里在目前矣！」

translations.literal: When he saw Yao's Explanation of Journey to the West East of Jinshan, he sighed and said: "Ten thousand li of remote wilderness lie before one's eyes!"
translations.idiomatic: When he saw Yao's Explanation of Journey to the West East of Jinshan, he exclaimed: "Ten thousand li of distant wilderness lie spread before one's eyes!"

sentences.zh: 遂閣筆。

translations.literal: He then closed his brush.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid down his brush and wrote no more.

sentences.zh: 垚客死，張穆裒其遺著，為落颿樓藁。

translations.literal: Yao died as a guest; Zhang Mu gathered his surviving writings into Drafts of the Falling-Sail Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Yao died far from home; Zhang Mu collected his surviving writings as Drafts of the Falling-Sail Tower.

sentences.zh: 陳潮，字東之，泰興人。

translations.literal: Chen Chao, styled Dongzhi, was a native of Taixing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Chao, whose style name was Dongzhi, came from Taixing.

sentences.zh: 通經，工小篆，又擅周髀之學。

translations.literal: He mastered the classics, was skilled in small seal script, and was also expert in Zhou Bi studies.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the classics, excelled at small seal script, and was also expert in mathematical astronomy.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜登高台窺星象，不寐。

translations.literal: He once climbed a high terrace at night to observe the stars and did not sleep.
translations.idiomatic: He once spent a sleepless night on a high terrace observing the stars.

sentences.zh: 遊京師，亦卒於松寓。

translations.literal: Traveling to the capital, he also died in Song's lodging.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled to the capital and also died in Xu's household.

sentences.zh: 李圖，字少伯，掖縣人。

translations.literal: Li Tu, styled Shaobo, was a native of Yexian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tu, whose style name was Shaobo, came from Yexian.

sentences.zh: 以拔貢生官直隸無極縣知縣，謝病歸。

translations.literal: As a selected tribute student he served as magistrate of Wuji County in Zhili, then resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: As a selected tribute student he served as magistrate of Wuji County in Zhili, then resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 圖讀書十行俱下，天才卓越。

translations.literal: Tu read ten lines at once; his natural talent was outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Tu could read ten lines at a glance; his natural talent was extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 工詩古文詞，力屏近世浮靡之習。

translations.literal: Skilled in poetry and ancient-style prose, he vigorously rejected recent frivolous fashions.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at poetry and ancient-style prose and firmly rejected the frivolous fashions of his day.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「文非司馬子長，詩非蘇、李，不足為師法也。」

translations.literal: He once said: "For prose, if not Sima Qian; for poetry, if not Su and Li—insufficient as models."
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "In prose, nothing but Sima Qian is fit to be a model; in poetry, nothing but Su Shi and Li Bai."

sentences.zh: 徐松為濟南濼源書院山長，見圖詩，歎曰：「三百年來無此作矣！」

translations.literal: Xu Song was head of the Luoyuan Academy in Jinan; seeing Tu's poetry, he sighed: "In three hundred years there has been nothing like this!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Song, as head of the Luoyuan Academy in Jinan, read Tu's poetry and exclaimed: "In three hundred years there has been nothing like this!"

sentences.zh: 著有鴻桷齋詩文集。

translations.literal: He authored the Hongjue Studio Poetry and Prose Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His Hongjue Studio Poetry and Prose Collection survives.

sentences.zh: 山左稱詩者，王士禎、趙執信以後，以圖為巨擘云。

translations.literal: Among poets famed in Shandong, after Wang Shizhen and Zhao Zhixin, Tu was called a great master.
translations.idiomatic: Among Shandong poets, after Wang Shizhen and Zhao Zhixin, Tu was regarded as the leading figure.

sentences.zh: 李兆洛，字申耆，陽湖人。

translations.literal: Li Zhaoluo, styled Shenqi, was a native of Yanghu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhaoluo, whose style name was Shenqi, came from Yanghu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiaqing, a jinshi, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Jiaqing, a jinshi degree-holder, he was selected for the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 改令鳳臺，俗獷悍多盜，地接蒙城、阜陽，遠者至百八十里，官或終任不一至。

translations.literal: Changed to magistrate of Fengtai; the customs were fierce and bold with many bandits; the territory bordered Mengcheng and Fuyang, distant places reaching one hundred eighty li, and officials might complete a term without visiting once.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Fengtai, where the people were fierce and banditry common; the county bordered Mengcheng and Fuyang, with outlying districts as far as one hundred eighty li away, so that magistrates sometimes never visited them during an entire term.

sentences.zh: 兆洛親行縣，辨其里落繁耗、地畝廣袤饒瘠，次第經理之。

translations.literal: Zhaoluo personally traveled the county, distinguishing the prosperity and decline of hamlets and villages, the breadth and length and fertility and barrenness of fields, and put them in order step by step.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoluo traveled the county himself, assessing each hamlet's prosperity, mapping field sizes and soil quality, and putting local administration in order.

sentences.zh: 焦岡湖，漢芍陂也，濱淮，易為災。

translations.literal: Jiaogang Lake was the Han Quepi; bordering the Huai, it easily became a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaogang Lake was the ancient Quepi Reservoir; lying along the Huai River, it was prone to flooding.

sentences.zh: 乃增堤防，設溝閘，歲以屢豐。

translations.literal: He therefore increased dikes and defenses, set up ditches and sluice gates, and year after year harvests were abundant.
translations.idiomatic: He strengthened the dikes, built canals and sluice gates, and harvests became consistently abundant.

sentences.zh: 擇耆老勸民孝謹，優敘之。

translations.literal: He selected elders to urge the people toward filial piety and prudence and gave them preferential recognition.
translations.idiomatic: He chose respected elders to encourage filial conduct and prudent living among the people and honored them publicly.

sentences.zh: 於僻遠設義學，為求良師。

translations.literal: In remote places he established charity schools and sought good teachers.
translations.idiomatic: In remote districts he established charity schools and recruited able teachers.

sentences.zh: 其捕盜，尤為人所喜稱。

translations.literal: His capture of bandits was especially praised by people.
translations.idiomatic: His success in capturing bandits was especially praised.

sentences.zh: 嘗騎率健勇出不意得其魁，因察而撫之。

translations.literal: He once rode leading stalwart braves, taking the ringleader by surprise, then investigated and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: He once led mounted braves in a surprise raid that captured a bandit chief, then investigated the case and won the people's trust.

sentences.zh: 兆洛嘗曰：「鳳、潁、泗民氣可用，揀集五千人，方行天下有餘矣。

translations.literal: Zhaoluo once said: "The martial spirit of the people of Feng, Ying, and Si can be used; selecting five thousand men would be more than enough to pacify the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoluo once said: "The fighting spirit of the people along the Feng, Ying, and Si rivers could be harnessed; five thousand well-chosen men would be more than enough to pacify the empire.

sentences.zh: 然唯其豪能使之，官帥至千里外，必客兵勢勝足相鈐制乃可。」

translations.literal: Yet only local strongmen could deploy them; if officials went a thousand li away, they must have guest troops whose strength was superior and sufficient to restrain them."
translations.idiomatic: Yet only local strongmen could command them effectively; officials operating a thousand li from home needed outside troops strong enough to keep such forces in check."

sentences.zh: 兆洛在縣七年，以父憂去，遂不出。

translations.literal: Zhaoluo served in the county seven years, left on his father's mourning, and thereafter did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoluo served seven years as magistrate, left to mourn his father, and never returned to office.

sentences.zh: 主講江陰書院幾二十年，以實學課士，其治經學、音韻、訓詁，訂輿圖，考天官歷術及習古文辭者輩出。

translations.literal: As head lecturer of the Jiangyin Academy for nearly twenty years, he taught scholars with practical learning; those who mastered classical studies, phonology, and exegesis, revised geographical maps, investigated celestial offices and calendrical arts, and practiced ancient-style prose emerged in succession.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly twenty years he headed the Jiangyin Academy, teaching practical scholarship; his students who mastered classical studies, phonology, exegesis, cartography, astronomy, and ancient-style prose emerged in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 如江陰承培元、宋景昌、繆尚誥、六承如等，皆其選也。

translations.literal: Such as Jiangyin's Cheng Peiyuan, Song Jingchang, Mou Shanggao, Liu Chengru, and others—all were his selections.
translations.idiomatic: Among them were Cheng Peiyuan, Song Jingchang, Mou Shanggao, and Liu Chengru of Jiangyin—all his chosen disciples.

sentences.zh: 兆洛短身碩腹，豹顱剛目，望之若不可近，而接人和易，未嘗疾言遽色。

translations.literal: Zhaoluo was short in stature with a large belly, leopard head and firm eyes; viewed from afar he seemed unapproachable, yet in receiving people he was gentle and easy, never speaking harshly or showing sudden anger.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoluo was short and stout, with a leonine head and piercing eyes; he seemed unapproachable at first glance, yet in person he was gentle and never spoke harshly or showed sudden anger.

sentences.zh: 資卹故舊窮乏無不至。

translations.literal: In providing funds and relief to old friends and the impoverished, there was nothing to which he did not extend himself.
translations.idiomatic: He spared no effort in aiding old friends and relieving the poor.

sentences.zh: 藏書逾五萬卷，皆手加丹鉛，尤嗜輿地學。

translations.literal: His collected books exceeded fifty thousand juan, all personally marked with red and lead annotations; he especially delighted in geography.
translations.idiomatic: His library held more than fifty thousand volumes, each annotated in his own hand; he was especially devoted to historical geography.

sentences.zh: 其論文欲合駢散為一，病當世治古文者知宗唐、宋不知宗兩漢，因輯駢體文鈔。

translations.literal: In his discourse on literature he wished to unite parallel and free prose into one; he lamented that those of the age who cultivated ancient-style prose knew how to take the Tang and Song as masters but not how to take the two Han as masters, and therefore compiled the Anthology of Parallel Prose.
translations.idiomatic: In literary theory he sought to unite parallel and free prose; criticizing contemporaries who revered Tang and Song models but neglected the two Han, he compiled the Anthology of Parallel Prose.

sentences.zh: 其序略云：「自秦迄隋，其體遞變，而文無異名。

translations.literal: His preface in summary says: "From Qin through Sui, the forms changed in succession, yet literature had no separate names.
translations.idiomatic: His preface states in brief: "From the Qin through the Sui, literary forms evolved step by step, yet prose had no distinct labels.

sentences.zh: 自唐以來，始有古文之目，而目六朝之文為駢體。

translations.literal: From the Tang onward there first arose the category of ancient-style prose, while the literature of the Six Dynasties was labeled parallel style.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tang on, the term "ancient-style prose" appeared, and writings of the Six Dynasties were called parallel prose.

sentences.zh: 為其學者，亦自以為與古文殊路。

translations.literal: Those who practiced the latter learning also considered themselves on a different path from ancient-style prose.
translations.idiomatic: Students of parallel prose likewise regarded themselves as following a path wholly separate from ancient-style writing.

sentences.zh: 夫氣有厚薄，天為之也；

translations.literal: Now, qi has thins and thicks—Heaven makes this so;
translations.idiomatic: Vital force may be robust or attenuated—Heaven determines that;

sentences.zh: 學有純駁，人為之也；

translations.literal: learning has purity and admixture—men make this so;
translations.idiomatic: scholarship may be pure or mixed—human effort determines that;

sentences.zh: 體格有遷變，人與天參焉者也；

translations.literal: literary form has shifts and changes—men and Heaven share in this;
translations.idiomatic: literary style shifts and changes—human and heavenly factors share in that;

sentences.zh: 義理無殊途，天人合焉者也。

translations.literal: moral principle has no divergent paths—Heaven and man unite in this.
translations.idiomatic: moral principle admits no separate paths—Heaven and humanity meet in that.

sentences.zh: 得其厚薄純雜之故，則於其體格之變，可以知世焉；

translations.literal: When one grasps the reasons for thinness and thickness, purity and admixture, then from changes in literary form one may know the age;
translations.idiomatic: Once one understands why force is strong or weak and learning pure or mixed, one can read the age in changing literary forms;

sentences.zh: 於其義理之無殊，可以知文焉。

translations.literal: from the absence of divergence in moral principle one may know literature.
translations.idiomatic: from the unity of moral principle one can understand literature itself.

sentences.zh: 文之體至六代而其變盡，夫沿其流極而溯之以至乎其源，則其所出者一也。」

translations.literal: The forms of literature reached the Six Dynasties and their changes were exhausted; following the stream to its utmost and tracing back to the source, what issues forth is one."
translations.idiomatic: Literary forms ran their course by the Six Dynasties; follow the current to its limit and trace back to the source, and what emerges is one."

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 其自著曰養一齋集。

translations.literal: His own writings are called the Yangyi Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His own collected works are entitled the Yangyi Studio Collection.

sentences.zh: 所輯有皇朝文典、大清一統輿地全圖、鳳臺縣志、地理韻編。

translations.literal: What he compiled includes the Anthology of Our Dynasty's Literature, the Complete Atlas of the Great Qing Unified Realm, the Fengtai County Gazetteer, and the Rhymed Geography Compendium.
translations.idiomatic: His compilations include the Anthology of Our Dynasty's Literature, the Complete Atlas of the Great Qing Unified Realm, the Fengtai County Gazetteer, and the Rhymed Geography Compendium.

sentences.zh: 培元，字守丹。

translations.literal: Peiyuan, courtesy name Shoudan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Peiyuan, courtesy name Shoudan.

sentences.zh: 優貢生。

translations.literal: A senior tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: He was a senior tribute student.

sentences.zh: 著說文引經證例、籀雅、經滯揭櫫。

translations.literal: He wrote Shuowen Citations from the Classics as Proof, Zhouya, and Exposing Obscurities in the Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Shuowen Citations from the Classics as Proof, Zhouya, and Exposing Obscurities in the Classics.

sentences.zh: 景昌，字冕之。

translations.literal: Jingchang, courtesy name Mianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jingchang, courtesy name Mianzhi.

sentences.zh: 縣學生。

translations.literal: A county school student.
translations.idiomatic: He was a county school student.

sentences.zh: 著星緯測量諸篇。

translations.literal: He wrote various treatises on measuring stars and constellations.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote various essays on measuring stars and constellations.

sentences.zh: 尚誥，字芷卿。

translations.literal: Shanggao, courtesy name Zhiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Shanggao, courtesy name Zhiqing.

sentences.zh: 舉人。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a provincial graduate (juren).

sentences.zh: 著古韻譜、雙聲譜、經星考。

translations.literal: He wrote Ancient Rhymes Tables, Initial-Consonant Tables, and Inquiry into Classic Stars.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Ancient Rhymes Tables, Initial-Consonant Tables, and Inquiry into Classic Stars.

sentences.zh: 承如及族人嚴，皆貢生。

translations.literal: Chengru and his clansman Yan were both tribute students.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chengru and his clansman Yan were both tribute students.

sentences.zh: 兆洛訂輿地圖，六氏兩生所手繪也。

translations.literal: The geographical atlas Zhaoluo revised was hand-drawn by the two disciples of the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: The geographical atlas that Zhaoluo revised was hand-drawn by Liu Chengru and his fellow student.

sentences.zh: 錢儀吉，字衎石，嘉興人，尚書陳群曾孫。

translations.literal: Qian Yiji, courtesy name Kanshi, was a native of Jiaxing and great-grandson of Minister Chen Qun.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Yiji, courtesy name Kanshi, was from Jiaxing and a great-grandson of Minister Chen Qun.

sentences.zh: 父福胙，侍讀學士。

translations.literal: His father Fuzuo was an academician reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian Fuzuo served as an academician reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 儀吉生有五色文禽翔其室，故初名逵吉，後易焉。

translations.literal: When Yiji was born a five-colored patterned bird flew in his chamber; hence his original name was Kuiji, later changed.
translations.idiomatic: At Yiji's birth a five-colored patterned bird flew into the room, so he was first named Kuiji and later renamed.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiaqing he became a metropolitan graduate and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the Jiaqing reign (1808) he passed the metropolitan examination and was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 改戶部主事，累遷至工科給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and was promoted in succession to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and rose in succession to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 皆能舉其職，因公罷歸。

translations.literal: In each post he could fulfill his duties; dismissed on account of an official matter, he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he discharged his duties well; after being dismissed over an official matter, he went home.

sentences.zh: 儀吉治經，先求古訓，博考眾說，一折衷本文大義，不持漢、宋門戶。

translations.literal: Yiji studied the classics by first seeking ancient glosses, broadly examining the theories of many, and uniformly weighing them against the great meaning of the original text, not adhering to Han or Song factional gates.
translations.idiomatic: Yiji approached the classics by seeking ancient glosses first, surveying many commentators, and reconciling them with the text's main sense—without taking sides in the Han versus Song schools.

sentences.zh: 嘗著經典證文、說文雅厭。

translations.literal: He once wrote Evidence from the Classics and Shuowen Elegance Disposed.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Evidence from the Classics and Shuowen Elegance Disposed.

sentences.zh: 雅厭者，以十九篇之次，寫九百四部之文，而以經籍傳注推廣之。

translations.literal: Elegance Disposed follows the order of the nineteen sections, transcribes the nine hundred and four category texts, and extends them through canonical works and commentarial traditions.
translations.idiomatic: Elegance Disposed follows the nineteen sections of the Shuowen, sets out its nine hundred and four categories, and expands them with citations from classics and commentaries.

sentences.zh: 其讀史，補晉兵志、朔閏諸表，撰三國晉南北朝會要，體例視徐天麟有所出入，不限斷以本書。

translations.literal: In reading history he supplemented the Jin military monograph and tables on new and intercalary months, and wrote Essentials of the Three Kingdoms, Jin, and Northern and Southern Dynasties; the format compared with Xu Tianlin's had some divergences and did not limit judgments to the original book.
translations.idiomatic: In historical studies he supplemented the Jin military monograph and calendrical tables, and compiled Essentials of the Three Kingdoms, Jin, and Northern and Southern Dynasties—its format partly diverged from Xu Tianlin's and did not bind conclusions to a single source text.

sentences.zh: 又彷宋杜大珪名臣琬琰碑傳集，得清臣工文儒等八百餘人，輯錄之為碑傳集。

translations.literal: Again, following the Song Du Dagui's Collection of Steles and Biographies of Eminent Ministers, he obtained more than eight hundred Qing officials, literary craftsmen, Confucian scholars, and the like, and compiled them into a Collection of Stele Biographies.
translations.idiomatic: He also modeled himself on the Song Du Dagui's Collection of Steles and Biographies of Eminent Ministers, gathered more than eight hundred Qing statesmen, writers, and scholars, and compiled them into his Collection of Stele Biographies.

sentences.zh: 後卒於大梁書院，年六十八。

translations.literal: Later he died at Daliang Academy at age sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at Daliang Academy at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 從弟泰吉，字警石。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Taiji, courtesy name Jingshi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Qian Taiji, courtesy name Jingshi.

sentences.zh: 少孤，執喪盡哀禮。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he observed mourning to the fullest extent of filial rites.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he observed mourning with the fullest filial propriety.

sentences.zh: 與儀吉以學行相磨，遠近盛稱「嘉興二石」。

translations.literal: With Yiji he polished each other in learning and conduct; near and far they were greatly praised as "the two Stones of Jiaxing."
translations.idiomatic: He and Yiji sharpened each other in scholarship and conduct; people far and near acclaimed them as "the two Stones of Jiaxing."

sentences.zh: 為詩文原本情性，讀其辭，知其於孝友最深也。

translations.literal: In composing poetry and prose he took genuine disposition as his root; reading his words one knows his depth in filial piety and brotherly love.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose sprang from true feeling; read his language and one sees how deeply filial piety and brotherly affection shaped him.

sentences.zh: 以廩貢生得海寧州學訓導。

translations.literal: As a stipendiary tribute student he obtained the post of educational instructor at Haining Prefectural School.
translations.idiomatic: As a stipendiary tribute student he was appointed educational instructor at the Haining prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 居間務讀書，自經史百氏下逮唐、宋以來詩文集，靡不博校。

translations.literal: In intervals he devoted himself to reading; from classics, histories, and the hundred schools down to Tang and Song poetry and prose collections, nothing escaped broad collation.
translations.idiomatic: In his spare time he read constantly, collating everything from the classics, histories, and masters down to Tang and Song belles-lettres.

sentences.zh: 以其學語諸生，諸生之賢且文者大附。

translations.literal: He imparted his learning to the students, and the worthy and literary among them greatly attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: He taught his learning to the students, and the able and literary among them flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 嘗修學宮，以費所羨修海昌備志。

translations.literal: He once repaired the school temple, and with surplus funds compiled the Haichang Supplementary Gazetteer.
translations.idiomatic: He once renovated the school temple and used leftover funds to compile the Haichang Supplementary Gazetteer.

sentences.zh: 既又得民間節孝行者千餘事為旌之，曰：「吾職也。」

translations.literal: Having also obtained more than a thousand cases of chastity and filial conduct among the people, he had them commended, saying: "This is my duty."
translations.idiomatic: He also collected more than a thousand local cases of chastity and filial devotion and had them officially commended, saying, "This is my duty.

sentences.zh: 再三請，必得乃已。

translations.literal: Repeated requests had to be made three times before he would cease only when he obtained agreement.
translations.idiomatic: He had to ask repeatedly, three times over, and would desist only when his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 為訓導幾三十年，不以枝官自放曠。

translations.literal: As educational instructor for nearly thirty years, he did not treat a minor post as license for self-indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly thirty years as an educational instructor he never treated a minor post as an excuse for slackness.

sentences.zh: 粵寇陷浙，往依曾國藩，卒於安慶。

translations.literal: When Cantonese rebels took Zhejiang he went to rely on Zeng Guofan and died at Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel forces overran Zhejiang he joined Zeng Guofan and died at Anqing.

sentences.zh: 著曝書雜誌、甘泉鄉人稿。

translations.literal: He wrote Baoshu Miscellany and Drafts of a Ganquan Villager.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Baoshu Miscellany and Drafts of a Ganquan Villager.

sentences.zh: 儀吉子寶惠，泰吉子炳森，皆能世其學。

translations.literal: Yiji's son Baohui and Taiji's son Bingsen could both inherit their fathers' learning.
translations.idiomatic: Yiji's son Baohui and Taiji's son Bingsen both carried on their fathers' scholarship.

sentences.zh: 包世臣，字慎伯，涇縣人。

translations.literal: Bao Shichen, courtesy name Shenbo, was a native of Jing County.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Shichen, courtesy name Shenbo, was from Jing County.

sentences.zh: 少工詞章，有經濟大略，喜言兵。

translations.literal: In youth he excelled at regulated composition; he had a broad grasp of statecraft and delighted in discussing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he excelled at literary composition, had a broad vision of statecraft, and loved to discourse on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年舉人，大挑以知縣發江西。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiaqing he became a provincial graduate; in the grand selection he was assigned as magistrate to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Jiaqing (1808) he passed the provincial examination; in the grand selection he was assigned a magistracy in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 一權新喻，被劾去。

translations.literal: Once he served as acting magistrate of Xinyu and was impeached and removed.
translations.idiomatic: He briefly served as acting magistrate of Xinyu, was impeached, and left office.

sentences.zh: 复隨明亮徵川、楚，發奇謀不見用，遂歸，卜居金陵。

translations.literal: Again he followed Mingliang on the campaign in Sichuan and Huguang; his ingenious stratagems went unused, so he returned and took up residence in Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Mingliang on campaigns in Sichuan and Huguang; his bold plans were not adopted, so he returned and settled in Jinling.

sentences.zh: 世臣精悍有口辯，以布衣遨遊公卿間。

translations.literal: Shichen was keen and forceful with a ready tongue, and as a commoner wandered among high ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Shichen was sharp-witted and eloquent, and as a commoner moved freely among high officials.

sentences.zh: 東南大吏，每遇兵、荒、河、漕、鹽諸鉅政。

translations.literal: The great officials of the southeast, whenever they encountered major policies on military affairs, famine relief, rivers, grain transport, or salt,
translations.idiomatic: Whenever southeastern governors faced major issues of war, famine relief, rivers, grain transport, or salt,

sentences.zh: 無不屈節諮詢，世臣亦慷慨言之。
