translations.literal: all without exception bowed to consult him, and Shichen also spoke out boldly.
translations.idiomatic: they all humbled themselves to seek his counsel, and Shichen answered with equal forthrightness.

sentences.zh: 初，海盜蔡牽犯上海，鎮道迎世臣閱沿海島嶼。

translations.literal: At first the pirate Cai Qian raided Shanghai; the military governor and circuit intendant welcomed Shichen to inspect the coastal islands.
translations.idiomatic: When the pirate Cai Qian attacked Shanghai, the regional commander and circuit intendant invited Shichen to survey the coastal islands.

sentences.zh: 見黃浦停泊商船千艘，遂建海運可救漕弊之議。

translations.literal: Seeing a thousand merchant vessels moored at Huangpu, he then proposed that sea transport could remedy abuses in the tribute-grain system.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing a thousand merchant ships at anchor on the Huangpu, he proposed that sea transport could cure the abuses of the grain-tribute system.

sentences.zh: 遊袁浦，值河事亟，箸策河四略。

translations.literal: Traveling to Yuanpu when river works were urgent, he wrote the Four Strategies for Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to Yuanpu during a river crisis he drafted the Four Strategies for Rivers.

sentences.zh: 是時鹽法以兩淮為大，私梟充斥，議者爭言緝私。

translations.literal: At that time the salt laws took the two Huai circuits as primary; private smugglers filled the land, and debaters vied in speaking of suppressing smuggling.
translations.idiomatic: Salt policy then centered on the two Huai circuits; smugglers were everywhere, and officials competed in proposals to crack down on illicit trade.

sentences.zh: 世臣擬多裁鹽官，惟留運司主錢糧，場大使督灶戶，不分畛域，仿現行鐵硝之例，聽商販領本地官印照，赴場繳課買鹽。

translations.literal: Shichen proposed drastically cutting salt officials, retaining only the transport commissioner to manage revenue and grain, with field supervisors overseeing saltern households; without territorial divisions, following the present iron-and-saltpeter model, merchants would obtain local official licenses, go to the salterns to pay duties and buy salt.
translations.idiomatic: Shichen proposed slashing salt bureaucracy, leaving only the transport commissioner in charge of revenue while field supervisors oversaw saltern households; abolishing rigid zones and following the iron-and-saltpeter model, merchants would carry local official licenses to the salterns, pay duties, and buy salt.

sentences.zh: 州縣具詳，運司存核，則場官不能乾沒正課；

translations.literal: When prefectures and counties submitted detailed reports and the transport commissioner kept them on file for verification, then field officials could not embezzle the regular tax;
translations.idiomatic: With counties filing reports and the transport commissioner keeping records for audit, field officials could not skim the regular tax;

sentences.zh: 而轉輸迅速，則鹽價必銳減；

translations.literal: and with rapid transport, salt prices would necessarily fall sharply;
translations.idiomatic: and with faster distribution, salt prices would drop sharply;

sentences.zh: 私鹽皆輸官課，課入必倍。

translations.literal: illicit salt would all be turned into official revenue, and tax receipts would necessarily double.
translations.idiomatic: smuggled salt would flow into official coffers, doubling revenue.

sentences.zh: 以之津貼辦公，並增翰、詹、科、道廉俸，為計甚便。

translations.literal: Using this to subsidize official expenses and also to increase the stipends of Hanlin, expositorate, censorate, and secretariat officials would be a very convenient plan.
translations.idiomatic: The surplus could subsidize government costs and raise stipends for Hanlin, expositorate, censorate, and secretariat officials—a highly practical scheme.

sentences.zh: 其論西北水利曰：「今國家南漕四百萬石，中歲腴田二百萬畝所產也。

translations.literal: His discussion of northwestern water conservancy says: "Today the state transports four million shi of southern grain tribute—what fertile fields of two million mu in a middling year produce.
translations.idiomatic: On northwestern irrigation he wrote: "The empire now ships four million shi of southern grain tribute—about what two million mu of good farmland yield in an average year.

sentences.zh: 有田四百萬畝，歲入與佃半之，遂當全漕。

translations.literal: With fields of four million mu, if annual revenue were shared half with tenants, it would equal the entire tribute transport.
translations.idiomatic: With four million mu under cultivation, splitting the harvest half with tenants would match the full tribute quota.

sentences.zh: 先減運十之一，糶其穀及運資置官屯，遞減至十年，則漕可罷，賦可寬。

translations.literal: First reduce transport by one-tenth, sell the grain and transport costs to establish official military colonies, and reduce in succession over ten years—then tribute transport could be abolished and land tax eased.
translations.idiomatic: Cut transport by a tenth at first, sell grain and freight to fund official colonies, and phase reductions over ten years—then the tribute fleet could end and land taxes lighten.

sentences.zh: 以其盈餘量加賦餉，而官可廉，兵可練。

translations.literal: With the surplus measured out to increase pay and rations, officials could be incorrupt and troops could be trained.
translations.idiomatic: Apply the surplus to pay and provisions, and officials could serve honestly while troops were properly drilled.

sentences.zh: 不然，漕東南以贍西北，浮收勒折，日增一日，竭民力，積眾怒。

translations.literal: Otherwise, using southeastern transport to sustain the northwest, with inflated collection and forced deductions increasing day by day, exhausts the people's strength and accumulates popular anger.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, feeding the northwest from southeastern transport—with extortionate levies and squeezes growing daily—will drain the people and stockpile resentment.

sentences.zh: 東南大患，終必在此。」

translations.literal: The great calamity of the southeast will in the end lie here."
translations.idiomatic: The southeast's gravest disaster will ultimately stem from this."

sentences.zh: 世臣能為大言。

translations.literal: Shichen could utter grand pronouncements.
translations.idiomatic: Shichen was given to bold, sweeping statements.

sentences.zh: 其論書法尤精，行草隸書，皆為世所珍貴。

translations.literal: His discourse on calligraphy was especially refined; his running, cursive, and clerical scripts were all treasured by the age.
translations.idiomatic: His theory of calligraphy was especially subtle; his running, cursive, and clerical scripts were prized throughout his day.

sentences.zh: 著有小倦遊閣文集，別編為安吳四種。

translations.literal: His writings include the Collected Works of the Little Weary-of-Travel Pavilion, separately compiled as the Four Works of Anwu.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Collected Works of the Little Weary-of-Travel Pavilion, also issued separately as the Four Works of Anwu.

sentences.zh: 齊彥槐，字梅麓，婺源人。

translations.literal: Qi Yanhuai, courtesy name Meilu, was a native of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Yanhuai, courtesy name Meilu, was from Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年召試舉人，明年成進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiaqing he was summoned to the palace examination as a provincial graduate; the next year he became a metropolitan graduate and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Jiaqing (1808) he was called to the palace examination as a juren; the following year he passed the metropolitan examination and entered the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 散館，授金匱令。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the academy he was appointed magistrate of Jinquan.
translations.idiomatic: After completing his Hanlin term he was appointed magistrate of Jinquan.

sentences.zh: 毀淫祠，歲旱，勤賑務。

translations.literal: He destroyed illicit shrines; in years of drought he diligently managed relief.
translations.idiomatic: He demolished improper shrines and, in drought years, worked tirelessly at famine relief.

sentences.zh: 擢蘇州府同知，陳海運策，巡撫召詰之，條舉以對，巡撫不能難，終以更張寢其事。

translations.literal: Promoted to vice-prefect of Suzhou, he submitted a sea-transport plan; the governor summoned and questioned him, and he answered point by point—the governor could not refute him, yet in the end shelved the proposal for fear of sweeping change.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice-prefect of Suzhou, he presented a sea-transport plan; the governor interrogated him, but though he answered every objection and the governor could not defeat his arguments, the scheme was finally dropped for fear of radical change.

sentences.zh: 後十餘年，改行海運，仍仿其法焉。

translations.literal: More than ten years later, when sea transport was adopted, his method was still followed.
translations.idiomatic: More than a decade later, when sea transport was instituted, officials still followed his approach.

sentences.zh: 嘗制渾天儀、中星儀，並各為之說，及龍尾、恆升二車，便民運水。

translations.literal: He once made an armillary sphere and a meridian instrument, each with its own exposition, as well as the Dragon-Tail and Constant-Rising water wheels to benefit the people in transporting water.
translations.idiomatic: He built an armillary sphere and a meridian instrument, each with an explanatory treatise, and also the Dragon-Tail and Constant-Rising water wheels to help people lift water.

sentences.zh: 又著北極星緯度分錶、海運南漕叢議、梅麓詩文集。

translations.literal: He also wrote Tables of Polar Star Latitudes, Discussions on Sea Transport and Southern Grain Tribute, and the Meilu Poetry and Prose Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Tables of Polar Star Latitudes, Discussions on Sea Transport and Southern Grain Tribute, and the Meilu Poetry and Prose Collection.

sentences.zh: 姚椿，字春木，婁縣人。

translations.literal: Yao Chun, courtesy name Chunmu, was a native of Lou County.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chun, courtesy name Chunmu, was from Lou County.

sentences.zh: 父令儀，四川布政使，又屢參戎幕。

translations.literal: His father Lingyi was Sichuan provincial treasurer and repeatedly joined military staffs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yao Lingyi served as Sichuan provincial treasurer and often served on military staffs.

sentences.zh: 椿高才博學，幼隨父遊歷諸行省，洞知閭閻疾苦，慨然欲效用於世。

translations.literal: Chun was gifted and broadly learned; in childhood he followed his father in traveling the provinces and thoroughly knew the hardships of common households, and with emotion wished to serve the world.
translations.idiomatic: Chun was brilliant and widely read; as a boy he traveled with his father through the provinces, learned firsthand the people's hardships, and resolved to put his talents to public use.

sentences.zh: 以國子監生試京兆，日與洪亮吉、楊芳燦、張問陶輩文酒高會，才名大起。

translations.literal: As a National University student he took the capital examination; daily he joined Hong Liangji, Yang Fangcan, Zhang Wentao, and the like in literary gatherings and wine feasts, and his literary fame rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: As a National University student he sat for the capital examinations, meeting daily with Hong Liangji, Yang Fangcan, Zhang Wentao, and others for literary salons—and his reputation soared.

sentences.zh: 顧試輒不遇。

translations.literal: Yet whenever he tested he was unsuccessful.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he repeatedly failed the examinations.

sentences.zh: 既，又受學於姚鼐，退而發宋賢書讀之，屏棄夙習​​，壹意求道，泊如也。

translations.literal: Afterward he also received instruction from Yao Nai; retiring, he opened the books of Song worthies and read them, abandoning former habits and with single intent seeking the Way, tranquil as could be.
translations.idiomatic: Later he studied under Yao Nai, turned to Song Neo-Confucian writings, set aside old habits, and pursued the Way with single-minded calm.

sentences.zh: 嘗得寶應朱澤澐遺著，歎曰：「此真為程、朱之學者！」

translations.literal: He once obtained the posthumous writings of Zhu Zeyun of Baoying and sighed: "This is a true student of the Cheng and Zhu school!"
translations.idiomatic: He once came upon the posthumous works of Baoying's Zhu Zeyun and exclaimed, "Here is a genuine follower of Cheng and Zhu!

sentences.zh: 親詣其墓拜之，申私淑之禮。

translations.literal: He personally went to his tomb to bow, observing the rites of private admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He visited Zhu's grave to pay his respects, observing the rites due a scholar one admires from afar.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，舉孝廉方正，不就。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daoguang (1821) he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt but declined office.

sentences.zh: 主書院講席，以實學勵諸生。

translations.literal: He held the chair of an academy and with practical learning encouraged the students.
translations.idiomatic: He headed an academy lectureship and urged students toward practical learning.

sentences.zh: 其論文必舉桐城所稱，曰：「好學深思，心知其意。」

translations.literal: In his discourse on literature he always cited what the Tongcheng school praised, saying: "Love learning and think deeply; let the heart know the meaning."
translations.idiomatic: In discussing literature he always invoked the Tongcheng school's motto: "Love learning and think deeply until the heart grasps the meaning."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「文之用有四：曰明道，曰記事，曰考古有得，曰言詞深美。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Literature has four uses: to illuminate the Way, to record events, to present gains from antiquarian study, and to express words of depth and beauty."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Writing serves four ends: to illuminate the Way, to record events, to convey sound antiquarian findings, and to utter language of depth and beauty."

sentences.zh: 其錄清代人文八十餘卷，一本此旨。

translations.literal: His compilation of Qing literary figures in more than eighty volumes wholly follows this aim.
translations.idiomatic: His compilation of Qing literary figures, more than eighty volumes in all, wholly embodies this principle.

sentences.zh: 著有通藝閣錄、晚學齋文錄。

translations.literal: He authored Records of the Tongyi Pavilion and Literary Records of the Wanxue Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Records of the Tongyi Pavilion and Literary Records of the Wanxue Studio.

sentences.zh: 顧廣譽，字維康，平湖人。

translations.literal: Gu Guangyu, styled Weikang, was a native of Pinghu.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Guangyu, styled Weikang, was from Pinghu.

sentences.zh: 優貢生，舉咸豐元年孝廉方正。

translations.literal: A senior tribute student; in the first year of Xianfeng he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: A senior tribute student, he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt in the first year of Xianfeng (1851).

sentences.zh: 寇亂，未廷試。

translations.literal: Rebellion broke out; he never took the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiping rebellion intervened, and he never sat for the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 廣譽慕其鄉張履祥、陸隴其之為人，刻意厲行。

translations.literal: Guangyu admired the conduct of his fellow townsman Zhang Lüxiang and Lu Longqi and deliberately cultivated strict practice.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyu admired the moral example of his fellow townsman Zhang Lüxiang and Lu Longqi and strove to emulate their rigorous conduct.

sentences.zh: 其治經一依程端禮讀書分年日程遺法。

translations.literal: In studying the classics he wholly followed the legacy method of Cheng Duanli's Annual Reading Schedule.
translations.idiomatic: In his classical studies he followed Cheng Duanli's Annual Reading Schedule in every respect.

sentences.zh: 著學詩詳說，用力至勤。

translations.literal: He wrote Detailed Explanations of Learning the Odes, to which he devoted tireless effort.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Detailed Explanations of Learning the Odes, laboring over it with exceptional diligence.

sentences.zh: 又憫晚近喪祭禮廢，恩紀衰薄，婚娶僭侈逾度，乃變通古禮，酌時俗之宜，成四禮榷疑八卷。

translations.literal: He also lamented that in recent times mourning and sacrificial rites had fallen into disuse, bonds of grace had thinned, and weddings and funerals were extravagantly beyond measure; he therefore adapted ancient rites to suit contemporary custom and produced Eight Fascicles on Resolving Doubts in the Four Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He also lamented that mourning and sacrificial rites had fallen into neglect, familial bonds had weakened, and weddings and funerals had grown extravagantly excessive; adapting ancient ritual to present custom, he produced his eight-fascicle Resolving Doubts in the Four Rites.

sentences.zh: 姚椿推為一時宗匠。

translations.literal: Yao Chun acclaimed him as a master of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chun hailed him as the leading authority of his generation.

sentences.zh: 有悔過齋文稿。

translations.literal: He left Drafts from the Studio of Repentance.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings survive as Drafts from the Studio of Repentance.

sentences.zh: 卒於上海龍門書院。

translations.literal: He died at the Longmen Academy in Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the Longmen Academy in Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 張鑑，字春冶，歸安人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jian, styled Chunye, was a native of Gui'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian, styled Chunye, was from Gui'an.

sentences.zh: 巡撫阮元築詁經精舍西湖，鑑及同里楊鳳苞、施國祁肄業其中，皆知名。

translations.literal: When Governor Ruan Yuan built the Classics Research Academy on West Lake, Jian together with fellow townsman Yang Fengbao and Shi Guoqi studied there—all became well known.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor Ruan Yuan founded the Classics Research Academy on West Lake, Jian studied there alongside fellow townsman Yang Fengbao and Shi Guoqi; all three won renown.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，副榜貢生。

translations.literal: Early in Jiaqing he became a tribute student from the second examination list.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiaqing reign he became a tribute student from the second examination list.

sentences.zh: 元剿海寇，賑兩浙水災，一資鑑贊畫。

translations.literal: When Ruan suppressed sea pirates and relieved flood disaster in the two Zhes, he relied wholly on Jian for planning.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruan suppressed coastal pirates and relieved flooding in Zhejiang, he relied entirely on Jian for strategic counsel.

sentences.zh: 時方議海運，鑑力主之。

translations.literal: At the time maritime transport was under debate; Jian strongly advocated it.
translations.idiomatic: Maritime grain transport was then under debate, and Jian was its strongest advocate.

sentences.zh: 以為河運雖安，費鉅；

translations.literal: He held that although canal transport was secure, its cost was enormous;
translations.idiomatic: Canal transport was secure, he argued, but ruinously expensive;

sentences.zh: 海運費省，得其人熟習海道，未嘗不安。

translations.literal: maritime transport saved expense; with the right men skilled in sea routes, it was never unsafe.
translations.idiomatic: maritime transport saved money, and with experienced navigators it was no less safe.

sentences.zh: 乃著海運芻言，凡料淺佔風之法，定盤望星之規，放洋泊舟之處，考之甚悉，侍郎英和亟稱其書。

translations.literal: He then wrote Sketches on Maritime Transport, examining in great detail methods for gauging shallows and reading winds, rules for fixing compass and sighting stars, and places for setting sail and anchoring; Vice Minister Ying He repeatedly praised the work.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Sketches on Maritime Transport, treating in exhaustive detail methods for sounding shallows and reading winds, rules for compass and star sighting, and places for putting to sea and anchoring; Vice Minister Ying He repeatedly praised the book.

sentences.zh: 道光四年，河決高家堰，漕運阻。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang the Yellow River breached at Gaojiayan and grain transport was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daoguang (1824) the Yellow River burst at Gaojiayan, blocking the grain transport route.

sentences.zh: 英和遂奏行海運，多采用鑑說。

translations.literal: Ying He thereupon memorialized to implement maritime transport, largely adopting Jian's proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Ying He then memorialized to implement maritime transport, drawing heavily on Jian's proposals.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十三。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 著十五經叢說、西夏紀事本末、眉山詩案廣證。

translations.literal: He authored Collected Notes on the Fifteen Classics, Comprehensive Account of Western Xia Affairs, and Expanded Evidence on the Meishan Poetry Case.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Collected Notes on the Fifteen Classics, Comprehensive Account of Western Xia Affairs, and Expanded Evidence on the Meishan Poetry Case.

sentences.zh: 鳳苞，字傅九。

translations.literal: Fengbao, styled Fujiu.
translations.idiomatic: Fengbao, styled Fujiu.

sentences.zh: 元編經籍篡詁，鳳苞與分纂。

translations.literal: When Ruan compiled the Exegesis of Classics and Histories, Fengbao participated in the editing.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruan compiled the Exegesis of Classics and Histories, Fengbao served as one of its editors.

sentences.zh: 熟明季事，嘗為南疆逸史跋十二篇，傳於時。

translations.literal: Thoroughly versed in late Ming affairs, he once wrote twelve colophons for the Unofficial History of the Southern Court, which circulated in his day.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply versed in late Ming history, he wrote twelve colophons for the Unofficial History of the Southern Court, which circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 晚館郡城陳氏，其書室為鄭元慶魚計亭，人以為元慶復生云。

translations.literal: In his later years he lodged with the Chen family in the prefectural city; his study was Zheng Yuanqing's Yuji Pavilion—people said Yuanqing had been reborn.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he lodged with the Chen family in the prefectural city; his study was Zheng Yuanqing's Yuji Pavilion, and people said Yuanqing had been reborn in him.

sentences.zh: 國祁，字非熊。

translations.literal: Guoqi, styled Feixiong.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqi, styled Feixiong.

sentences.zh: 與鳳苞皆廩膳生。

translations.literal: He and Fengbao were both stipend students.
translations.idiomatic: He and Fengbao were both government stipend students.

sentences.zh: 國祁病金史蕪雜，積二十餘年，成金史詳校。

translations.literal: Guoqi found the History of Jin chaotic; over more than twenty years he produced a Detailed Collation of the History of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the History of Jin hopelessly disordered, Guoqi labored more than twenty years to produce a Detailed Collation of the History of Jin.

sentences.zh: 以其帙繁，乃列舉條目為金源劄記。

translations.literal: Because the work was voluminous, he listed entries separately as Notes on the Jin Source.
translations.idiomatic: Because the work grew too large, he listed its entries separately as Notes on the Jin Source.

sentences.zh: 又作元遺山集箋、金源雜事詩。

translations.literal: He also wrote Commentary on Yuan Haoshan's Collected Works and Miscellaneous Poems on Jin Origins.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote a commentary on Yuan Haoshan's collected works and Miscellaneous Poems on Jin Origins.

sentences.zh: 國祁工詩文，善填詞。

translations.literal: Guoqi was skilled at poetry and prose and adept at composing lyric song.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqi excelled at poetry and prose and was adept at composing lyric verse.

sentences.zh: 家貧，為人主計市肆中。

translations.literal: Poor at home, he kept accounts for others in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Poor at home, he earned his living keeping accounts in a shop.

sentences.zh: 有一樓，顏曰吉貝居，著書其中，毀於火，著述多燼。

translations.literal: He had a tower called Jibei Studio where he wrote; it was destroyed by fire and most of his writings perished.
translations.idiomatic: He had a study called Jibei Studio where he wrote; it burned down, and most of his writings were lost in the flames.

sentences.zh: 黃易，字小松，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Huang Yi, styled Xiaosong, was a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yi, styled Xiaosong, was from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 父樹穀，以孝聞，工隸書，博通金石。

translations.literal: His father Shugu was renowned for filial piety, excelled at clerical script, and was broadly versed in bronzes and stones.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shugu was famed for filial piety, excelled at clerical script, and was widely versed in bronzes and stone inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 易承先業，於吉金樂石，寢食依之，遂以名家。

translations.literal: Yi inherited the family pursuit; with ancient bronzes and inscribed stones he lived and ate among them until he became a leading name.
translations.idiomatic: Yi inherited this pursuit; bronzes and inscribed stones were his daily companions, and he became a leading name in the field.

sentences.zh: 官山東運河同知，勤於職事。

translations.literal: He served as assistant prefect of the Grand Canal in Shandong and was diligent in office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as assistant prefect of the Grand Canal in Shandong and was diligent in his duties.

sentences.zh: 嘗得武班碑及武梁祠堂石室畫像於嘉祥，乃即其地起武氏祠堂，砌石祠內。

translations.literal: He once obtained the Wu Ban stele and stone-chamber pictorial reliefs of the Wu Liang Shrine at Jiaxiang; he thereupon erected the Wu Family Shrine on the spot and set the stones within.
translations.idiomatic: He once obtained the Wu Ban stele and the pictorial stone reliefs of the Wu Liang shrine chamber at Jiaxiang; he then erected the Wu family shrine on the spot and installed the stones within it.

sentences.zh: 又出家藏精拓雙鉤鋟木。

translations.literal: He also issued fine rubbings from his collection in double-outline woodblock prints.
translations.idiomatic: He also published fine rubbings from his collection as double-outline woodblock prints.

sentences.zh: 凡四方好古之士得奇文古刻，皆就易是正，以是所蓄甲於一時。

translations.literal: Whenever antiquarians throughout the realm obtained rare inscriptions or ancient carvings, they brought them to Yi for correction; thus his collection ranked first of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever antiquarians across the empire obtained rare inscriptions or ancient carvings, they brought them to Yi for authentication; his collection thus ranked foremost of the age.

sentences.zh: 自乾、嘉以來，漢學盛行，群經古訓無可蒐輯，則旁及金石，嗜之成癖，亦一時風尚然也。

translations.literal: Since the Qianlong and Jiaqing reigns Han Learning had flourished; when ancient glosses to the classics could no longer be gathered, scholars turned to bronzes and stones until obsession with them became a fashion of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Qianlong and Jiaqing reigns Han Learning had flourished; when little remained to be gleaned from ancient commentaries on the classics, scholars turned to bronzes and stone inscriptions until collecting them became a craze—a fashion characteristic of the age.

sentences.zh: 瞿中溶，字木夫，嘉定人。

translations.literal: Qu Zhongrong, styled Mufu, was a native of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Zhongrong, styled Mufu, was from Jiading.

sentences.zh: 為錢大昕女夫。

translations.literal: He was Qian Daxin's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son-in-law of Qian Daxin.

sentences.zh: 尤邃金石之學。

translations.literal: He was especially deep in the study of bronzes and stones.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially accomplished in the study of bronzes and stone inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 官湖南布政司理問，蒐奇訪僻於人跡罕至之境，所獲益多。

translations.literal: He served as director of punishments under the Hunan provincial administration; he sought rarities in remote places seldom visited and gained all the more.
translations.idiomatic: As director of punishments under the Hunan provincial administration, he sought rarities in remote places few had visited and acquired all the more.

sentences.zh: 著有孔廟從祀弟子辨證、漢魏蜀石經考異辨正、說文地名考異、古泉山館彝器圖錄、錢志補正集、古官印考證、古鏡圖錄、續漢金石文編，凡二十餘種。

translations.literal: He authored Verification of Disciples Worshipped in the Confucian Temple, Corrections to Studies of Stone Classics of Han, Wei, and Shu, Textual Variants in Place Names in the Shuowen, Illustrated Record of Ritual Bronzes from the Guquan Mountain Lodge, Supplementary Corrections to the Numismatic Treatise, Verification of Ancient Official Seals, Illustrated Record of Ancient Mirrors, and Continued Compilation of Han Stone Inscriptions—more than twenty works in all.
translations.idiomatic: His more than twenty works include Verification of Disciples Worshipped in the Confucian Temple, Corrections to Studies of the Han, Wei, and Shu Stone Classics, Textual Variants in Place Names in the Shuowen, Illustrated Record of Ritual Bronzes from the Guquan Mountain Lodge, Supplementary Corrections to the Numismatic Treatise, Verification of Ancient Official Seals, Illustrated Record of Ancient Mirrors, and Continued Compilation of Han Stone Inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 張廷濟，字叔未，嘉興人。

translations.literal: Zhang Tingji, styled Shuwei, was a native of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingji, styled Shuwei, was from Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing he placed first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiaqing (1798) he placed first in the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 應禮部試輒躓，遂歸隱，以圖書金石自娛。

translations.literal: Whenever he took the Ministry of Rites examination he stumbled; he then retired into seclusion and amused himself with books and bronzes and stones.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly failed the metropolitan examination and withdrew into private life, devoting himself to books and antiquities.

sentences.zh: 建清儀閣，藏庋古器，名被大江南北。

translations.literal: He built the Qingyi Pavilion to store ancient objects; his fame spread north and south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Qingyi Pavilion to house his antiquities, and his reputation spread throughout the Yangtze valley.

sentences.zh: 沈濤，字西雝。

translations.literal: Shen Tao, styled Xiyong.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tao, styled Xiyong.

sentences.zh: 與廷濟同邑。

translations.literal: He was from the same district as Tingji.
translations.idiomatic: He was from the same district as Tingji.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十五年舉人。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Jiaqing he became a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He received his provincial degree in the fifteenth year of Jiaqing (1810).

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，署江西鹽法道。

translations.literal: Early in Xianfeng he served as acting Jiangxi salt commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign he served as acting Jiangxi salt commissioner.

sentences.zh: 粵賊攻南昌，隨巡撫張芾城守。

translations.literal: When the Cantonese rebels attacked Nanchang, he followed Governor Zhang Fei in defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taiping rebels attacked Nanchang, he joined Governor Zhang Fei in defending the city.

sentences.zh: 圍解，授興泉永道，未到官，卒。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted he was appointed intendant of Xing-Quan-Yong Circuit but died before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege was lifted he was appointed intendant of the Xing-Quan-Yong circuit but died before assuming office.

sentences.zh: 濤尚考訂之學，喜金石，著《常山貞石志》、《說文古本考》。

translations.literal: Tao favored textual verification, delighted in bronzes and stones, and authored Records of Inscribed Stones of Changshan and Investigation of Ancient Editions of the Shuowen.
translations.idiomatic: Tao favored textual verification and antiquities; his works include Records of Inscribed Stones of Changshan and Investigation of Ancient Editions of the Shuowen.

sentences.zh: 陸增祥，字星農，太倉人。

translations.literal: Lu Zengxiang, styled Xingnong, was a native of Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zengxiang, styled Xingnong, was from Taicang.

sentences.zh: 道光三十年一甲一名進士，授修撰，至辰永沅靖道。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Daoguang he placed first in the first rank of the jinshi examination, was appointed Compiler, and rose to intendant of the Chen-Yuan-Yong-Jing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Daoguang (1850) he placed first in the jinshi examination, was appointed Hanlin Compiler, and rose to intendant of the Chen-Yuan-Yong-Jing circuit.

sentences.zh: 踵王昶金石萃編成金石補正百二十卷，凡三千五百餘通。

translations.literal: Following Wang Chang's Collected Stone Inscriptions, he completed Supplementary Corrections to Stone Inscriptions in 120 fascicles, comprising more than thirty-five hundred inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: Following Wang Chang's Collected Stone Inscriptions, he compiled Supplementary Corrections to Stone Inscriptions in 120 fascicles, recording more than thirty-five hundred inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 又著磚錄一卷。

translations.literal: He also wrote one fascicle of Records of Bricks.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote a one-fascicle Records of Bricks.

sentences.zh: 其訂正金石款識名物，何紹基服其精。

translations.literal: In correcting inscriptions and identifying objects on bronzes and stones, He Shaoji acknowledged his mastery.
translations.idiomatic: He Shaoji acknowledged his mastery in correcting inscriptions and identifying objects on bronzes and stone tablets.

sentences.zh: 董祐誠，字方立，陽湖人。

translations.literal: Dong Youcheng, styled Fangli, was a native of Yanghu.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Youcheng, styled Fangli, was from Yanghu.

sentences.zh: 生五歲，曉九九數。

translations.literal: At age five he understood the multiplication table.
translations.idiomatic: At five he had mastered the multiplication table.

sentences.zh: 稍長，善屬文。

translations.literal: When somewhat older he was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he proved adept at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 遊陝西，成​​華山神廟賦，一時傳誦。

translations.literal: Traveling in Shaanxi, he composed a Rhapsody on the Huashan Spirit Temple, which was widely recited for a time.
translations.idiomatic: On a journey to Shaanxi he composed a Rhapsody on the Huashan Spirit Temple, which was widely recited at the time.

sentences.zh: 其學於典章、禮儀、輿地、名物皆肆力探索，而尤精曆算，盡通諸家法。

translations.literal: In his learning he explored with full effort institutions, ritual, geography, and material culture, and was especially expert in calendrical calculation, thoroughly mastering the methods of all schools.
translations.idiomatic: He explored institutions, ritual, geography, and material culture with equal vigor, but excelled above all in calendrical astronomy, mastering every major method.

sentences.zh: 特善深沉之思，書之鉤棘難讀者，一覽輒通曉。

translations.literal: He was especially good at profound thought; writings tangled and hard to read he understood at a single glance.
translations.idiomatic: He had a gift for penetrating thought; abstruse and knotty texts he grasped at a single reading.

sentences.zh: 復能出新意，闡曲隱，補罅漏。

translations.literal: He could also produce fresh ideas, elucidate what was obscure, and repair gaps.
translations.idiomatic: He could also advance fresh insights, clarify what was obscure, and repair lacunae in received learning.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十三年舉人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Jiaqing he became a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He received his provincial degree in the twenty-third year of Jiaqing (1818).

sentences.zh: 越五年卒，年三十三。

translations.literal: Five years later he died at the age of thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later he died, aged thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 祐誠讀諸史曆志，因著三統衍補。

translations.literal: Youcheng read the calendrical treatises in the various histories and thereupon wrote Supplement to the Triple Concordance Calculations.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the calendrical treatises in the standard histories, Youcheng wrote his Supplement to the Triple Concordance Calculations.

sentences.zh: 復取三統以次迄明大統、萬年、回回各術，擬撰五十三家歷術，屬稿未成，其兄基誠取已成五種附水經註圖說刊之。

translations.literal: He further took from the Triple Concordance down through the Ming Great Concordance, Ten-Thousand-Year, and Islamic methods, planning to compile fifty-three schools of calendrical technique; the draft was unfinished, and his elder brother Jicheng published the five completed parts appended to the Illustrated Commentary on the Water Classic.
translations.idiomatic: He planned a comprehensive treatise on fifty-three calendrical systems from the Triple Concordance through the Ming Great Concordance, Ten-Thousand-Year, and Islamic methods, but left the work unfinished; his elder brother Jicheng published the five completed parts as an appendix to the Illustrated Commentary on the Water Classic.

sentences.zh: 其所著算學，有割圜連比例術圖解、斜弧三邊求角補術、堆垛求積術若干種。

translations.literal: Among his mathematical writings were Illustrated Explanation of the Method of Continuous Proportion for Circle Division, Supplementary Method for Finding Angles from Three Oblique Arcs, and several methods for finding volumes by stacking.
translations.idiomatic: His mathematical works include Illustrated Explanation of Continuous Proportion for Circle Division, Supplementary Method for Finding Angles from Three Oblique Arcs, and several treatises on volume calculation by stacking.

sentences.zh: 基誠，字子詵。

translations.literal: Jicheng, styled Zishen.
translations.idiomatic: Jicheng, styled Zishen.

sentences.zh: 進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi.

sentences.zh: 由刑部郎中出知開封府。

translations.literal: From director in the Ministry of Punishments he went out to serve as prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as a director in the Ministry of Punishments, he was appointed prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 工詞章，與祐誠文合刊曰多華館駢體文。

translations.literal: Skilled at regulated verse, he and Youcheng's writings were jointly published as Parallel Prose of the Duohua Studio.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at belles-lettres, his writings and Youcheng's were published together as Parallel Prose of the Duohua Studio.

sentences.zh: 方履籛，字彥聞，大興人。

translations.literal: Fang Lüqian, styled Yanwen, was a native of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Lüqian, styled Yanwen, was from Daxing.

sentences.zh: 與祐誠同年舉人，為令閩中。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the same year as Youcheng, he served as magistrate in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate in the same year as Youcheng, he served as a magistrate in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 初試吏署永定，裡豪胡鳳兆掘族人父棺，並殺其子，名捕不得。

translations.literal: On his first assignment as an acting official in Yongding, local bully Hu Fengzhao dug up a clansman's father's coffin and also killed his son; though sought by name he could not be captured.
translations.idiomatic: On his first posting as an acting official in Yongding, a local bully named Hu Fengzhao exhumed a clansman's father's coffin and murdered his son; despite an all-points search he could not be caught.

sentences.zh: 履籛至，為書諭之，鳳兆自首，遂論如法。

translations.literal: When Lüqian arrived he wrote a letter instructing him; Fengzhao surrendered himself and was sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When Lüqian arrived he wrote Fengzhao a letter of admonition; Fengzhao turned himself in and was sentenced according to law.

sentences.zh: 調閩縣，會旱，禱兩烈日中，體豐碩，中暑卒。

translations.literal: Transferred to Min County, he encountered drought; praying for rain under the blazing sun, his body being stout, he died of heatstroke.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Min County during a drought, he prayed for rain in the blazing heat; his stout frame succumbed to sunstroke and he died.

sentences.zh: 履籛亦以駢文著稱。

translations.literal: Lüqian was also famed for parallel prose.
translations.idiomatic: Lüqian was also renowned for his parallel prose.

sentences.zh: 尤嗜金石文字，所積幾萬種，有伊闕石刻錄、富蘅齋碑目、河內縣志、萬善花室集。

translations.literal: He was especially fond of inscribed bronzes and stones; his collection numbered nearly ten thousand items. He authored Records of Yique Stone Inscriptions, Catalogue of Steles from the Fuheng Studio, Gazetteer of Henei County, and Collected Writings from the Wanshan Flower Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially devoted to inscribed bronzes and stones, amassing nearly ten thousand specimens. His works include Records of Yique Stone Inscriptions, Catalogue of Steles from the Fuheng Studio, Gazetteer of Henei County, and Collected Writings from the Wanshan Flower Studio.

sentences.zh: 周儀暐，字伯恬，陽湖人。

translations.literal: Zhou Yiwei, styled Botian, was a native of Yanghu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yiwei, styled Botian, was from Yanghu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初舉人，宣城訓導。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate early in Jiaqing, he served as instructor at Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate early in Jiaqing, he served as instructor at Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 擢知山陽縣，調鳳翔。

translations.literal: He was promoted to magistrate of Shanyang County and transferred to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to magistrate of Shanyang County and later transferred to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 能詩。

translations.literal: He could write poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He was a capable poet.

sentences.zh: 有夫椒山館集。

translations.literal: He left Collected Poems of the Fufu Mountain Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: His collected poems survive as the Fufu Mountain Lodge Collection.

sentences.zh: 其後又有吳頡鴻，字嘉之。

translations.literal: Afterward there were also Wu Jiehong, styled Jiazhi;
translations.idiomatic: Later figures include Wu Jiehong, styled Jiazhi;

sentences.zh: 道光中進士，官代州知州；

translations.literal: a jinshi in the Daoguang reign who served as prefect of Daizhou;
translations.idiomatic: a Daoguang-era jinshi who served as prefect of Daizhou;

sentences.zh: 莊縉度，字眉叔。

translations.literal: Zhuang Jindu, styled Meishu;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Jindu, styled Meishu;

sentences.zh: 進士，戶部主事；

translations.literal: jinshi, secretary in the Ministry of Revenue;
translations.idiomatic: a jinshi and secretary in the Ministry of Revenue;

sentences.zh: 趙申嘉，字芸酉；

translations.literal: Zhao Shenjia, styled Yunyou;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shenjia, styled Yunyou;

sentences.zh: 陸容，字蓉卿；

translations.literal: Lu Rong, styled Rongqing;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Rong, styled Rongqing;

sentences.zh: 徐廷華，字子楞；

translations.literal: Xu Tinghua, styled Zileng;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Tinghua, styled Zileng;

sentences.zh: 汪士進，字逸雲；

translations.literal: Wang Shijin, styled Yiyun;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shijin, styled Yiyun;

sentences.zh: 周儀顥，字叔程，舉人，即儀暐弟也。

translations.literal: Zhou Yigao, styled Shucheng, a provincial graduate and younger brother of Yiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yigao, styled Shucheng, a provincial graduate and the younger brother of Yiwei.

sentences.zh: 號「毗陵後七子」，其名位亞於前七子。

translations.literal: They were styled the "Seven Later Masters of Piling," their fame and standing below the earlier seven masters.
translations.idiomatic: They were known as the "Seven Later Masters of Piling," ranking below the earlier seven masters in fame and standing.

sentences.zh: 俞正燮，字理初，黟縣人。

translations.literal: Yu Zhengxie, styled Lichu, was a native of Yi County.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhengxie, styled Lichu, was from Yi County.

sentences.zh: 性彊記，經目不忘。

translations.literal: By nature he had a powerful memory and forgot nothing he read.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed a prodigious memory and forgot nothing he read.

sentences.zh: 年二十餘，北走兗州謁孫星衍。

translations.literal: In his twenties he traveled north to Yanzhou to visit Sun Xingyan.
translations.idiomatic: In his twenties he traveled north to Yanzhou to visit Sun Xingyan.

sentences.zh: 時星衍為伏生建立博士，复訪求左氏後裔。

translations.literal: At the time Xingyan was establishing the doctorate for Fu Sheng and also seeking descendants of the Zuo clan.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xingyan was establishing the doctorate for Fu Sheng and also seeking descendants of the Zuo clan.

sentences.zh: 正燮因作邱明子孫姓氏論、左山考，星衍多據以折衷群議，由是名大起。

translations.literal: Zhengxie thereupon wrote On the Surname and Clan of Qiu Ming's Descendants and Examination of Mount Zuo; Xingyan relied heavily on these to reconcile competing views, and Zhengxie's fame rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengxie wrote On the Surname and Clan of Qiu Ming's Descendants and Examination of Mount Zuo; Xingyan drew heavily on them to reconcile scholarly debates, and Zhengxie's fame rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 道光元年舉人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he became a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He received his provincial degree in the first year of Daoguang (1821).

sentences.zh: 明年，阮元主會試，士相謂曰：「理初入彀矣！」

translations.literal: The next year Ruan Yuan presided over the metropolitan examination, and scholars said to one another: "Lichu has passed the threshold!"
translations.idiomatic: The following year Ruan Yuan presided over the metropolitan examination, and scholars said to one another, "Lichu is sure to pass!

sentences.zh: 後竟落第。

translations.literal: Yet in the end he failed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end he failed.

sentences.zh: 其經策淹博，為他考官所乙，元未之見也。

translations.literal: His examination essays on the classics were encyclopedic; another examiner marked him down, and Yuan never saw them.
translations.idiomatic: His classical examination essays were encyclopedic, but another examiner marked him down and Yuan never saw them.

sentences.zh: 房考王藻嘗引為恨。

translations.literal: Examiner Wang Zao often cited this as a regret.
translations.idiomatic: Examiner Wang Zao often cited this as a lasting regret.

sentences.zh: 正燮讀書，置巨冊數十，分題疏記，積歲月乃排比為文，斷以己意。

translations.literal: In reading, Zhengxie set out several dozen large volumes, annotating topics separately; only after months and years did he arrange them into essays, judging with his own views.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengxie read with enormous folio volumes at hand, annotating by topic; only after months and years did he arrange his notes into essays, judging matters by his own lights.

sentences.zh: 藻為刻十五卷，名曰癸巳類稿，又有存稿十五卷，山西楊氏​​刻之。

translations.literal: Zao printed fifteen fascicles entitled Guisi Miscellany, and there were also fifteen fascicles of surviving drafts printed by the Yang family of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zao printed fifteen fascicles as the Guisi Miscellany, and fifteen fascicles of surviving drafts were later printed by the Yang family of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 弟正禧，亦舉人。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhengxi was also a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhengxi was also a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 多義行，文學與正燮齊名。

translations.literal: Rich in righteous conduct, his literary learning ranked with Zhengxie's.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned for righteous conduct, his literary learning ranked with Zhengxie's.

sentences.zh: 趙紹祖，字琴士，涇縣人。

translations.literal: Zhao Shaozu, styled Qinshi, was a native of Jing County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shaozu, styled Qinshi, was from Jing County.

sentences.zh: 年十二，受知學使朱筠，補諸生。

translations.literal: At twelve he won recognition from Educational Commissioner Zhu Yun and was enrolled as a student.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he won recognition from Educational Commissioner Zhu Yun and was enrolled as a student.

sentences.zh: 筠授以說文，曰：「讀此日無過十字。

translations.literal: Yun taught him the Shuowen, saying: "In reading this, do not exceed ten characters a day.
translations.idiomatic: Yun taught him the Shuowen, saying, "Read no more than ten characters of this text a day.

sentences.zh: 讀注疏，亦無過十葉。

translations.literal: In reading commentaries, likewise do not exceed ten pages.
translations.idiomatic: In reading commentaries, likewise read no more than ten pages a day.

sentences.zh: 必精造乃已。」

translations.literal: You must master it thoroughly before stopping."
translations.idiomatic: You must master each passage thoroughly before moving on."

sentences.zh: 紹祖熟於史事，嘗應布政使陶澍聘，修安徽省志，詳贍有法。

translations.literal: Shaozu was thoroughly versed in historical matters; he once accepted appointment from Provincial Commissioner Tao Shu to compile the gazetteer of Anhui, which was detailed, comprehensive, and well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozu was thoroughly versed in historical matters; he accepted appointment from Provincial Commissioner Tao Shu to compile the gazetteer of Anhui, producing a work that was detailed, comprehensive, and well ordered.

sentences.zh: 道光初，年七十，舉孝廉方正。

translations.literal: Early in Daoguang, at age seventy, he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daoguang, at age seventy, he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 又十二年，卒。

translations.literal: Twelve years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve years later he died.

sentences.zh: 注有通鑑注商、新舊唐書互證、金石跋、安徽金石記、涇川金石記、金石文正續鈔。

translations.literal: His commentaries include Notes on the Zizhi Tongjian, Mutual Verification of the Old and New Books of Tang, Colophons on Bronzes and Stones, Records of Anhui Stone Inscriptions, Records of Jingchuan Stone Inscriptions, and Continued Transcription of Correct Stone Inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Notes on the Zizhi Tongjian, Mutual Verification of the Old and New Books of Tang, Colophons on Bronzes and Stones, Records of Anhui Stone Inscriptions, Records of Jingchuan Stone Inscriptions, and Continued Transcription of Correct Stone Inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 汪文台，字士南。

translations.literal: Wang Wentai, styled Shinan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wentai, styled Shinan.

sentences.zh: 與正燮同縣，相善。

translations.literal: From the same county as Zhengxie, they were on friendly terms.
translations.idiomatic: He was from the same county as Zhengxie and they were close friends.

sentences.zh: 宗漢儒，以論語邢疏疏略，因取證古義，博採子史箋傳，依韓嬰詩傳例作論語外傳。

translations.literal: Upholding Han Learning, he found Xing Shu's commentary on the Analects too brief; he therefore gathered evidence of ancient meaning from masters, histories, and commentaries and, following the model of Han Ying's Commentary on the Odes, wrote the Outer Tradition of the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: An adherent of Han Learning, he found Xing Shu's commentary on the Analects too brief; gathering evidence of ancient meaning from masters, histories, and commentaries, he wrote the Outer Tradition of the Analects following the model of Han Ying's Commentary on the Odes.

sentences.zh: 見阮元十三經註疏校勘記，謂有益於後學，然成於眾手，時有駮文，別為表識，作校勘記識語，寄示阮元，元服其精博，禮聘之。

translations.literal: Seeing Ruan Yuan's Collation Notes to the Thirteen Classics with Commentary, he said they benefited later students yet, being the work of many hands, sometimes contained errors; he separately tabulated them and wrote Identifying Notes to the Collation Notes, sending them to Ruan Yuan, who acknowledged their mastery and courteously engaged him.
translations.idiomatic: Reading Ruan Yuan's Collation Notes to the Thirteen Classics with Commentary, he judged them beneficial to later students yet, being the work of many hands, sometimes erroneous; he tabulated his corrections in Identifying Notes to the Collation Notes and sent them to Yuan, who acknowledged their mastery and courteously engaged him.

sentences.zh: 又嘗纂輯七家後漢書、淮南子校勘記及脞稿，皆行於世。

translations.literal: He also once compiled the Seven Versions of the History of the Later Han, Collation Notes to the Huainanzi, and Miscellaneous Drafts, all of which circulated.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled the Seven Versions of the History of the Later Han, Collation Notes to the Huainanzi, and Miscellaneous Drafts, all of which circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 道光二十四年，卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang he died at the age of forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang (1844) he died at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 湯球，字伯玕，亦黟人。

translations.literal: Tang Qiu, styled Bohang, was also from Yi County.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Qiu, styled Bohang, was also from Yi County.

sentences.zh: 少耽經史，從正燮、文台遊，傳其考據之學。

translations.literal: In youth devoted to the classics and histories, he associated with Zhengxie and Wentai and inherited their evidential scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he devoted himself to the classics and histories, studied with Zhengxie and Wentai, and inherited their evidential scholarship.

sentences.zh: 通曆算星緯，恥以藝名。

translations.literal: He mastered calendrical calculation and astronomical constants yet was ashamed to be known for technical skill.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered calendrical calculation and astronomical constants yet was ashamed to be known merely for technical skill.

sentences.zh: 嘗輯鄭康成逸書九種、劉熙孟子注、劉珍等東觀漢記、皇甫謐帝王世紀、譙周古史考、傅子、伏侯古今注。

translations.literal: He once compiled nine lost works of Zheng Xuan, Liu Xi's commentary on the Mencius, the Eastern Han Records of Liu Zhen and others, Huangfu Mi's Annals of Emperors and Kings, Qiao Zhou's Investigation of Ancient History, the Master Fu, and the Ancient and Modern Notes of the Marquis of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled nine lost works of Zheng Xuan, Liu Xi's commentary on the Mencius, the Eastern Han Records of Liu Zhen and others, Huangfu Mi's Annals of Emperors and Kings, Qiao Zhou's Investigation of Ancient History, the Master Fu, and the Ancient and Modern Notes of the Marquis of Fu.

sentences.zh: 球讀史用力於晉書尤深，廣蒐載籍，補晉史之闕，成書數種。

translations.literal: Qiu devoted his historical reading especially to the History of Jin; widely searching records, he supplemented its lacunae in several works.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu devoted his historical reading especially to the History of Jin; searching widely through sources, he supplemented its lacunae in several works.

sentences.zh: 同治六年，舉孝廉方正。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tongzhi he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tongzhi (1867) he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 光緒七年，卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu he died at the age of seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Guangxu (1881) he died at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 潘德輿，字四農，山陽人。

translations.literal: Pan Deyu, styled Sinong, was a native of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Deyu, styled Sinong, was from Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 年五六歲，母病不食，亦不食。

translations.literal: At five or six, when his mother was ill and would not eat, he would not eat either.
translations.idiomatic: At five or six, when his mother was ill and would not eat, he refused food as well.

sentences.zh: 父咯血，刲臂肉和藥進，父察其色動，泣曰：「固知兒有是也！」

translations.literal: His father spat blood; he cut flesh from his arm, mixed it with medicine, and presented it. His father, seeing his complexion change, wept: "I knew my son would do this!"
translations.idiomatic: When his father spat blood, he cut flesh from his arm, mixed it with medicine, and presented it. Seeing his son's pallor, his father wept, "I knew my son would do this!

sentences.zh: 既孤，大母猶在堂，孝敬彌至。

translations.literal: After he was orphaned his grandmother still lived; his filial respect grew all the greater.
translations.idiomatic: After he was orphaned his grandmother still lived, and his filial devotion grew all the greater.

sentences.zh: 居喪一遵禮制，柴瘠劚然。

translations.literal: In mourning he followed ritual in every respect, becoming gaunt and haggard.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he followed ritual in every respect, growing gaunt and haggard.

sentences.zh: 著喪禮正俗文、祭儀，為家法。

translations.literal: He wrote Correcting Popular Errors in Mourning Rites and Sacrificial Rites as family law.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Correcting Popular Errors in Mourning Rites and Sacrificial Rites as family standards.

sentences.zh: 撫寡妹嗣子，教養盡二十年。

translations.literal: He raised his widowed sister's adopted son, educating and providing for him for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his widowed sister's adopted son, educating and providing for him for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 其他行多類此。

translations.literal: His other conduct was largely of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His other conduct was largely of this kind.

sentences.zh: 嘗以挽回世運，莫切於文章，文章之根本在忠孝，源在經術。

translations.literal: He once held that to turn the age's fortune, nothing was more urgent than literature, whose root lay in loyalty and filial piety and whose source lay in classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: He held that to turn the age's fortune, nothing was more urgent than literature, whose root lay in loyalty and filial piety and whose source lay in classical learning.

sentences.zh: 其說經，不袒漢、宋，力求古人微言大義。

translations.literal: In expounding the classics he favored neither Han nor Song but strove for the subtle words and great meaning of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: In expounding the classics he favored neither Han nor Song schools but strove for the subtle words and great meaning of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 其論治術，謂天下大病不外三言：曰「吏」、曰「例」、曰「利」。

translations.literal: In discussing governance he said the great ills of the empire could be summed in three words: "officials," "precedents," and "profit."
translations.idiomatic: In discussing governance he said the empire's great ills could be summed in three words: "officials," "precedents," and "profit."

sentences.zh: 世儒負匡濟大略，非雜縱橫，即陷功利，未有能破「利」字而成百年休養之治者。

translations.literal: Confucian scholars who bore grand plans for saving the age, if not entangled in coalition tactics, fell into utilitarianism; none could break the word "profit" and achieve a century of restorative rule.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars who bore grand plans for saving the age, if not entangled in factional tactics, fell into utilitarianism; none could break the hold of "profit" and achieve a century of restorative rule.

sentences.zh: 道光八年，舉江南鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Daoguang he placed first in the Jiangnan provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Daoguang (1828) he placed first in the Jiangnan provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 入都，座主侍郎鍾昌館德輿於家，語人曰：「四農乃吾師也。」

translations.literal: Entering the capital, his examiner Vice Minister Zhong Chang lodged Deyu in his home and told others: "Sinong is my teacher."
translations.idiomatic: In the capital his examiner Vice Minister Zhong Chang lodged Deyu in his home and told others, "Sinong is my teacher."

sentences.zh: 大挑以知縣分安徽，未到官卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: In the large selection he was assigned as magistrate to Anhui but died before taking office, at the age of fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the large selection he was assigned as magistrate to Anhui but died before taking office, aged fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 初，阮元總督漕運，招之，謝不往。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ruan Yuan was governor-general of grain transport, he invited him, but he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Ruan Yuan was governor-general of grain transport, he invited him, but Deyu declined.

sentences.zh: 後朱桂楨、周天爵皆號為名臣，折節原納交，德輿遠引避之，以為義無所居也，天爵喟然有望塵之嘆。

translations.literal: Later Zhu Guizhen and Zhou Tianjue, both famed as worthy ministers, humbled themselves to seek his acquaintance; Deyu kept his distance, holding that righteousness left no place for compromise—Tianjue sighed with admiration from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhu Guizhen and Zhou Tianjue, both famed as worthy ministers, humbled themselves to seek his acquaintance; Deyu kept his distance, holding that righteousness left no room for compromise—Tianjue sighed with admiration from afar.

sentences.zh: 其所與遊，若永豐郭儀霄、建寧張際亮、震澤張履、益陽湯鵬、歙徐寶善，皆一時之選。

translations.literal: Those with whom he associated—Guo Yixiao of Yongfeng, Zhang Jiliang of Jianning, Zhang Lü of Zhenze, Tang Peng of Yiyang, and Xu Baoshan of She—all were leading figures of the age.
translations.idiomatic: His associates—Guo Yixiao of Yongfeng, Zhang Jiliang of Jianning, Zhang Lü of Zhenze, Tang Peng of Yiyang, and Xu Baoshan of She—were all leading figures of the age.

sentences.zh: 德輿詩文精深博奧，有養一齋集。

translations.literal: Deyu's poetry and prose were profound, exhaustive, and vast; he left the Yangyi Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu's poetry and prose were profound and vast; his collected works survive as the Yangyi Studio Collection.

sentences.zh: 門人清河吳昆田，字云圃。

translations.literal: His student Wu Kuntian of Qinghe, styled Yunpu.
translations.idiomatic: His student Wu Kuntian of Qinghe, styled Yunpu.

sentences.zh: 舉人，刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate, he served as vice director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate, he served as vice director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 晚年家居，賊犯清河，團練防守，邑賴以安。

translations.literal: In his later years at home, when rebels invaded Qinghe he organized militia defense and the district was kept safe.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years at home, when rebels invaded Qinghe he organized militia defense and the district was kept safe.

sentences.zh: 著漱六軒集。

translations.literal: He authored Collected Writings of the Shuliu Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Collected Writings of the Shuliu Studio.

sentences.zh: 張維屏，字子樹，番禺人。

translations.literal: Zhang Weiping, styled Zishu, was a native of Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Weiping, styled Zishu, was from Panyu.

sentences.zh: 工詩，計偕入都，翁方綱賞異之。

translations.literal: Skilled at poetry, on traveling to the capital for the examination he won Weng Fanggang's high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at poetry, on traveling to the capital for the examination he won Weng Fanggang's high regard.

sentences.zh: 與黃培芳、譚敬昭稱「粵東三子」。

translations.literal: With Huang Peifang and Tan Jingzhao he was styled the "Three Masters of Guangdong."
translations.idiomatic: With Huang Peifang and Tan Jingzhao he was known as the "Three Masters of Guangdong."

sentences.zh: 道光二年進士，改官知縣，署黃梅。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the second year of Daoguang, he changed appointment to magistrate and served as acting magistrate of Huangmei.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the second year of Daoguang (1822), he changed appointment to magistrate and served as acting magistrate of Huangmei.

sentences.zh: 江水潰堤，乘小舟勘災，水急舟衝溜，掛樹免。

translations.literal: When the river breached its dike he took a small boat to survey the disaster; the current was swift and the boat was swept into the rapids, but it caught on a tree and he was saved.
translations.idiomatic: When the river breached its dike he took a small boat to survey the disaster; the current swept his boat into the rapids, but it caught on a tree and he was saved.

sentences.zh: 民為謠曰：「犯急湍，官救民，神救官。」

translations.literal: The people made a ballad: "Meeting the rapids, the official saves the people; the gods save the official."
translations.idiomatic: The people made up a ballad: "Meeting the rapids, the official saves the people; the gods save the official."

sentences.zh: 調補廣濟，公費一資漕折，民苦之，勢不可革，引疾去。

translations.literal: Transferred to Guangji, public funds all went to grain transport deductions, causing the people great hardship; the practice could not be reformed, and he resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Guangji, he found that public funds all went to grain transport deductions, causing the people great hardship; the practice could not be reformed, and he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 汪廷珍語人曰：「縣官不原收漕，世罕見也！」

translations.literal: Wang Tingzhen told others: "A magistrate who refuses to accept grain transport fees is rarely seen in this world!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingzhen told others, "A magistrate who refuses to accept grain transport fees is rarely seen in this world!"

sentences.zh: 丁艱服闋，原就閒，援例改郡丞，權南康。

translations.literal: After mourning and returning to service, he wished for a quiet post; by precedent he changed to assistant prefect and held acting charge of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning and returning to service, he sought a quiet post; by precedent he changed to assistant prefect and held acting charge of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 建太白、東坡祠廬山，暇則集諸生談藝，以風雅寓規勸焉。

translations.literal: He built shrines to Li Bai and Su Dongpo on Mount Lu; in leisure he gathered students to discuss literature, embedding admonition in refined expression.
translations.idiomatic: He built shrines to Li Bai and Su Dongpo on Mount Lu; in his leisure he gathered students to discuss literature, embedding admonition in refined expression.

sentences.zh: 未一載，复罷歸。

translations.literal: In less than a year he resigned again and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In less than a year he resigned again and returned home.

sentences.zh: 築聽松園，頹然不與世事，癖愛松，又號松心子。

translations.literal: He built the Listening to Pines Garden and withdrew indifferently from worldly affairs; doting on pines, he also styled himself Master Pineheart.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Listening to Pines Garden and withdrew from worldly affairs; doting on pines, he also styled himself Master Pineheart.

sentences.zh: 見松形奇古，輒下拜。

translations.literal: When he saw a pine of strange and ancient form he would bow before it.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw a pine of strange and ancient form he would bow before it.

sentences.zh: 精書法，朝鮮、小呂宋得其書，咸寶愛之。

translations.literal: Expert in calligraphy, Korea and the Sulu Islands treasured his writing.
translations.idiomatic: Expert in calligraphy, Korea and the Sulu Islands treasured his writing.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 有松心草堂集、國朝詩人徵略。

translations.literal: He left Collected Writings of the Pineheart Studio and Biographical Sketches of Qing Poets.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Collected Writings of the Pineheart Studio and Biographical Sketches of Qing Poets.

sentences.zh: 培芳，香山人。

translations.literal: Peifang was from Xiangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Peifang was from Xiangshan.

sentences.zh: 敬昭，字子晉，陽春人。

translations.literal: Jingzhao, styled Zijin, was from Yangchun.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao, styled Zijin, was from Yangchun.

sentences.zh: 順德黎簡者，以詩名海內，敬昭賦鵬鶴篇投之，簡嘆為異才。

translations.literal: Li Jian of Shunde was famed throughout the realm for poetry; Jingzhao sent him his Rhapsody on the Peng and the Crane, and Jian sighed that he was a prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jian of Shunde was famed throughout the realm for poetry; Jingzhao sent him his Rhapsody on the Peng and the Crane, and Jian exclaimed that he was a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十二年進士，官戶部主事。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the twenty-second year of Jiaqing, he served as secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the twenty-second year of Jiaqing (1817), he served as secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 著聽雲樓集。

translations.literal: He authored Collected Writings of the Listening to Clouds Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Collected Writings of the Listening to Clouds Studio.

sentences.zh: 同時廣東以學行名者，又有高要彭泰來，字子大。

translations.literal: At the same time in Guangdong, Gao Yao's Peng Tailai, styled Zida, was also famed for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time in Guangdong, Peng Tailai of Gaoyao, styled Zida, was also famed for learning and conduct.

sentences.zh: 生二十月，能即事誦古經，語無不切。

translations.literal: At twenty months he could recite the ancient classics on the spot, every word apt.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty months he could recite the ancient classics on the spot, every word apt.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十八年拔貢生。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jiaqing he became a selected tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Jiaqing (1813) he became a selected tribute student.

sentences.zh: 絕意進取，學使李棠階高其品，屏騶從徒步就見，詢以挽回風俗之道。

translations.literal: He utterly renounced advancement; Educational Commissioner Li Tangjie esteemed his character, dismissed his mounted escort, and walked on foot to visit him, asking how to restore popular morals.
translations.idiomatic: He utterly renounced official advancement; Educational Commissioner Li Tangjie esteemed his character, dismissed his mounted escort, and walked on foot to visit him, asking how to restore popular morals.

sentences.zh: 泰來為書數千言復之，棠階表其廬，下教高要令，歲時存問。

translations.literal: Tailai replied in a letter of several thousand words; Tangjie erected a placard at his dwelling and instructed the magistrate of Gaoyao to visit him with seasonal inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: Tailai replied in a letter of several thousand words; Tangjie erected a placard at his dwelling and instructed the magistrate of Gaoyao to visit him with seasonal inquiries.

sentences.zh: 自惠士奇禮下胡方後，此為再見焉。

translations.literal: Since Hui Shiqi honored Hu Fang, this was seen only a second time.
translations.idiomatic: Since Hui Shiqi honored Hu Fang, such deference had been seen only once before.

sentences.zh: 著端州金石略、昨夢齋、詩義堂各集。

translations.literal: He authored Records of Duanzhou Stone Inscriptions and collected works from the Zuomeng Studio and the Shiyitang.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Records of Duanzhou Stone Inscriptions and collected works from the Zuomeng Studio and the Shiyitang.

sentences.zh: 梅曾亮，字伯言，上元人。

translations.literal: Mei Cengliang, styled Boyan, was a native of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Cengliang, styled Boyan, was from Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 少時工駢文。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled at parallel prose.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was skilled at parallel prose.

sentences.zh: 姚鼐主講鍾山書院，曾亮與邑人管同俱出其門，兩人交最篤，同肆力古文，鼐稱之不容口，名大起。

translations.literal: Yao Nai lectured at the Zhongshan Academy; Cengliang and his fellow townsman Guan Tong both studied under him. The two were closest in friendship; together they devoted themselves to ancient-style prose. Nai praised them without cease and their fame rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Nai lectured at the Zhongshan Academy; Cengliang and his fellow townsman Guan Tong both studied under him. The two were closest in friendship and together devoted themselves to ancient-style prose; Nai praised them without cease and their fame rose greatly.

sentences.zh: 間以規曾亮，曾亮自喜，不為動也。

translations.literal: Tong sometimes admonished Cengliang, but Cengliang was pleased with himself and was not moved.
translations.idiomatic: Tong sometimes admonished Cengliang, but Cengliang was pleased with himself and would not be swayed.

sentences.zh: 久之，讀周、秦、太史公書，乃頗寤，一變舊習。

translations.literal: After a long while, reading the books of Zhou, Qin, and Grand Historian Sima, he awakened somewhat and changed his former habits entirely.
translations.idiomatic: After long reading in Zhou, Qin, and Sima Qian, he awakened somewhat and changed his former habits entirely.

sentences.zh: 義法本桐城，稍參以異己者之長，選聲練色，務窮極筆勢。

translations.literal: His principles of composition were rooted in Tongcheng but drew somewhat on the strengths of others; he chose sounds and refined colors, striving to exhaust every turn of the brush.
translations.idiomatic: His principles of composition were rooted in Tongcheng but drew on others' strengths; he chose sounds and refined colors, striving to exhaust every turn of the brush.

sentences.zh: 道光二年進士，用知縣，授例改戶部郎中。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the second year of Daoguang, he was appointed magistrate but by precedent changed to director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the second year of Daoguang (1822), he was appointed magistrate but by precedent changed to director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 居京師二十餘年，與宗稷辰、朱琦、龍啟瑞、王拯、邵懿辰輩游處，曾國藩亦起而應之。

translations.literal: He lived in the capital more than twenty years, associating with Zong Yichen, Zhu Qi, Long Qirui, Wang Zheng, Shao Yichen, and the like; Zeng Guofan also rose to answer his call.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in the capital more than twenty years, associating with Zong Yichen, Zhu Qi, Long Qirui, Wang Zheng, Shao Yichen, and others; Zeng Guofan also rose to answer his call.

sentences.zh: 京師治古文者，皆從梅氏問法。

translations.literal: Those in the capital who studied ancient-style prose all sought instruction from the Mei school.
translations.idiomatic: Those in the capital who studied ancient-style prose all sought instruction from Mei.

sentences.zh: 當是時，管同已前逝，曾亮最為大師；

translations.literal: At that time Guan Tong had already died; Cengliang was the greatest master;
translations.idiomatic: By then Guan Tong had already died, and Cengliang was the greatest master;

sentences.zh: 而國藩又從唐鑑、倭仁、吳廷棟講身心克治之學，其於文推挹姚氏尤至。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Guofan also studied the learning of self-cultivation with Tang Jian, Woren, and Wu Tingdong; in literature he esteemed the Yao school above all.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Guofan also studied self-cultivation under Tang Jian, Woren, and Wu Tingdong; in literature he esteemed the Yao school above all.

sentences.zh: 於是士大夫多喜言文術政治，乾、嘉考據之風稍稍衰矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon many scholar-officials delighted in discussing literary craft and statecraft, and the evidential scholarship of the Qianlong and Jiaqing reigns gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon many scholar-officials turned to literary craft and statecraft, and the evidential scholarship of the Qianlong and Jiaqing reigns gradually waned.

sentences.zh: 未幾，曾亮依河督楊以增。

translations.literal: Before long Cengliang entered the service of Grand Canal Governor Yang Yizeng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Cengliang entered the service of Grand Canal Governor Yang Yizeng.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 以增為刊其詩文，曰柏梘山房集。

translations.literal: Yizeng published his poetry and prose under the title Collected Writings of the Baizhi Mountain Studio.
translations.idiomatic: Yizeng published his collected works as the Baizhi Mountain Studio Collection.

sentences.zh: 同，字異之。

translations.literal: Tong, styled Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Tong, styled Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 少孤，母鄒以節孝聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, his mother Zou was renowned for chastity and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, his mother Zou was renowned for chastity and filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 同善屬文，有經世之志，稱姚門高足弟子。

translations.literal: Tong was skilled at literary composition and had the ambition to order the age; he was called a leading disciple of the Yao school.
translations.idiomatic: Tong excelled at literary composition and aspired to practical statecraft; he was acclaimed as a leading disciple of the Yao school.

sentences.zh: 嘗擬言風俗書、籌積貯書，為一時傳誦。

translations.literal: He once drafted books on customs and on hoarding grain reserves, which were widely recited in his day.
translations.idiomatic: He once drafted treatises on customs and on grain reserves that circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 道光五年，陳用光典試江南，同中式。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daoguang, Chen Yongguang presided over the Jiangnan examination and Tong passed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daoguang (1825), Chen Yongguang presided over the Jiangnan examination and Tong passed.

sentences.zh: 用光語人曰：「吾校兩江士，獨以得一異之自憙耳。」

translations.literal: Yongguang told others: "In examining scholars of the two Jiangs, I rejoice chiefly in having obtained one Yizhi."
translations.idiomatic: Yongguang told others, "In examining scholars of the two Jiangs, I rejoice chiefly in having found one Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 用光亦鼐弟子也。

translations.literal: Yongguang was also a disciple of Nai.
translations.idiomatic: Yongguang was also a disciple of Yao Nai.

sentences.zh: 同卒，年四十七，著因寄軒集。

translations.literal: Tong died at forty-seven and left the Yinjixuan Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Tong died at forty-seven; his collected works survive as the Yinjixuan Collection.

sentences.zh: 子嗣复，字小異。

translations.literal: His son Sifu, styled Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sifu, styled Xiaoyi.

sentences.zh: 能世其業，兼通算術。

translations.literal: He could inherit his father's craft and was also versed in mathematics.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's craft and was also versed in mathematics.

sentences.zh: 鼐門下著籍者眾，惟同傳法最早。

translations.literal: Many were enrolled under Nai's gate, but only Tong transmitted the method earliest.
translations.idiomatic: Many studied under Yao Nai, but only Tong transmitted his method earliest.

sentences.zh: 其於同里，則亟稱劉開之才。

translations.literal: Among his fellow townsman he most praised Liu Kai's talent.
translations.idiomatic: Among his fellow townsman he most praised Liu Kai's talent.

sentences.zh: 開，字明東。

translations.literal: Kai, styled Mingdong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kai, styled Mingdong.

sentences.zh: 以孤童牧牛，聞塾師誦書，竊聽之，盡記其語。

translations.literal: As an orphan he herded cattle; hearing the tutor recite in the school, he listened secretly and memorized all that was said.
translations.idiomatic: An orphan who herded cattle, he listened outside the schoolhouse, memorizing every word the tutor recited.

sentences.zh: 塾師留之學，而妻以女。

translations.literal: The tutor kept him to study and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The tutor took him in as a student and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 年十四，以文謁鼐，有國士之譽，盡授以文法。

translations.literal: At fourteen he presented a composition to Nai and won praise as a national talent; Nai taught him the full method of writing.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he presented a composition to Yao Nai and won praise as a national talent; Nai taught him his entire method of composition.

sentences.zh: 遊客公卿，才名動一時。

translations.literal: Traveling among guests of dukes and ministers, his literary fame shook the age.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling among the great households, his literary fame shook the age.

sentences.zh: 年四十，卒。

translations.literal: He died at forty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty.

sentences.zh: 著孟塗集。

translations.literal: He left the Mengtu Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works survive as the Mengtu Collection.

sentences.zh: 子繼，字少塗。

translations.literal: His son Ji, styled Shaotu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji, styled Shaotu.

sentences.zh: 有信義。

translations.literal: He had faith and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for faith and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 遍走貴勢求刻其父書，以此孟塗集益顯。

translations.literal: He went everywhere among the powerful seeking to have his father's book printed, and thereby the Mengtu Collection grew all the more famous.
translations.idiomatic: He went everywhere among the powerful seeking publication of his father's book, and thereby the Mengtu Collection grew all the more famous.

sentences.zh: 寶山毛岳生，字申甫。

translations.literal: Mao Yuesheng of Baoshan, styled Shenfu.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Yuesheng of Baoshan, styled Shenfu.

sentences.zh: 用難廕改文學生。

translations.literal: By privilege for hardship he changed status to literary student.
translations.idiomatic: By privilege for hardship he changed status to literary student.

sentences.zh: 孤貧，以孝聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor, he was renowned for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he was renowned for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 自力於學，未弱冠，賦白雁詩，得名。

translations.literal: He strove in learning on his own; before reaching manhood he composed a poem on the white goose and won fame.
translations.idiomatic: He strove in learning on his own; before reaching manhood he composed a poem on the white goose and won fame.

sentences.zh: 亦從鼐學古文，以鉤棘字句為工。

translations.literal: He also studied ancient-style prose under Nai, excelling in hooked and thorny diction.
translations.idiomatic: He also studied ancient-style prose under Yao Nai, excelling in intricate, forceful diction.

sentences.zh: 有休復居集。

translations.literal: He left the Xiufu Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works survive as the Xiufu Studio Collection.

sentences.zh: 湯鵬，字海秋，益陽人。

translations.literal: Tang Peng, styled Haiqiu, was a native of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Peng, styled Haiqiu, was from Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 道光二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the second year of Daoguang.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the second year of Daoguang (1822).

sentences.zh: 初喜為詩，自上古歌謠至三百篇、漢、魏、六朝、唐，無不形規而神絜之，有詩三千首。
