translations.idiomatic: Once assigned to supervise engineering, by precedent there were shares to distribute; Songwei alone refused, saying, "In what we take and give we must be careful ourselves and cannot drift with custom.

sentences.zh: 昔陳稽亭先生官部曹時，印結公項，且猶不取。

translations.literal: Formerly Master Chen Jiting, when an official in a ministry, would not even take public seal fees.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Master Chen Jiting, when an official in a ministry, would not even take public seal fees.

sentences.zh: 矧此實為廠商之賄賂乎？」

translations.literal: How much more is this in truth a bribe from factory merchants?"
translations.idiomatic: How much more is this in truth a bribe from factory merchants?"

sentences.zh: 二十一年，中日釁起，戰事多北洋大臣主之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Sino-Japanese hostilities arose; warfare was largely directed by the Beiyang minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year (1895) Sino-Japanese hostilities arose; warfare was largely directed by the Beiyang minister.

sentences.zh: 會翁同龢復入軍機，乃進言曰：「讀聖祖、高宗聖訓，凡事關軍務者，皆由中朝謀定後動。

translations.literal: When Weng Tonghe again entered the Grand Council, he advanced remonstrance, saying: "Reading the sacred instructions of the Kangxi and Qianlong emperors, all matters concerning military affairs were planned at court before action.
translations.idiomatic: When Weng Tonghe again entered the Grand Council, he remonstrated, saying, "Reading the sacred instructions of the Kangxi and Qianlong emperors, all military matters were planned at court before action.

sentences.zh: 今日戰局既成，非直隸一省事，豈能悉諉之北洋乎？」

translations.literal: Today the war situation has formed; can it all be delegated to Zhili alone?"
translations.idiomatic: Today the war has begun; can it all be delegated to Zhili alone?

sentences.zh: 及議和，頌蔚益為悲憤，嘗曰：「今之敗績，徒歸咎於師之不練、器之不利，猶非探本之論。

translations.literal: When peace was discussed Songwei was all the more grieved and indignant, once saying: "Today's defeats merely blame untrained troops and inferior weapons—still not probing the root.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was discussed Songwei was all the more grieved, once saying, "Today's defeats merely blame untrained troops and inferior weapons—still not probing the root.

sentences.zh: 頻年以來，盈廷習洩沓之風，宮中務遊觀之樂，直臣擯棄，賄賂公行，安有戰勝之望？

translations.literal: In recent years the court has grown accustomed to lax ways, the palace pursues pleasures of travel and spectacle, upright men are cast aside, and bribes run openly—how can there be hope of victory?
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the court has grown lax, the palace pursues travel and spectacle, upright men are cast aside, and bribes run openly—how can there be hope of victory?

sentences.zh: 此後償金既巨，民力益疲，恐大亂之不在外患而在內憂矣。」

translations.literal: Hereafter indemnity gold is already vast and the people's strength grows weaker; I fear great disorder will come not from foreign trouble but from internal anxiety."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter indemnities are vast and the people's strength grows weaker; I fear great disorder will come not from foreign invasion but from internal collapse.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he died.

sentences.zh: 著有寫禮庼文集、詩集、讀碑記、古書經眼錄各一卷，明史考證攟逸四十二卷。

translations.literal: His works include the Xieli Studio Prose Collection, poetry collection, Record of Reading Steles, and Record of Books Seen—all one fascicle each—and forty-two fascicles of Gathered Remnants of Textual Verification of the History of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Xieli Studio collections, Record of Reading Steles, Record of Books Seen, and forty-two fascicles of Gathered Remnants of Textual Verification of the History of Ming.

sentences.zh: 葉昌熾，字鞠裳，元和人。

translations.literal: Ye Changchi, styled Jushang, was a native of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Changchi, styled Jushang, was from Yuanhe.

sentences.zh: 光緒十六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the sixteenth year of Guangxu, he was selected as bachelor and appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the sixteenth year of Guangxu (1890), he was selected as bachelor and appointed Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 累至侍講，督甘肅學政，邊地樸陋，昌熾校閱盡職。

translations.literal: He rose to reader and served as educational commissioner of Gansu; the frontier was plain and crude, yet Changchi examined and corrected with full diligence.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to reader and served as educational commissioner of Gansu; though the frontier was plain and crude, Changchi examined candidates with full diligence.

sentences.zh: 以裁缺歸，著書終老。

translations.literal: When the post was abolished he returned home and wrote to the end of his life.
translations.idiomatic: When the post was abolished he returned home and wrote to the end of his life.

sentences.zh: 國變後五年，卒。

translations.literal: Five years after the dynastic change he died.
translations.idiomatic: Five years after the dynastic change he died.

sentences.zh: 著有藏書紀事詩六卷，語石十卷，邠州大佛寺題刻考二卷，均考訂精確。

translations.literal: His works include six fascicles of Poetry on Bibliophiles, ten fascicles of Discourse on Stone, and two fascicles of Examination of Inscriptions at the Dazhou Great Buddha Temple—all textually precise.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Poetry on Bibliophiles, Discourse on Stone, and Examination of Inscriptions at the Dazhou Great Buddha Temple—all textually precise.

sentences.zh: 管禮耕，字申季。

translations.literal: Guan Ligeng, styled Shenji.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Ligeng, styled Shenji.

sentences.zh: 歲貢生。

translations.literal: A tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: A tribute student.

sentences.zh: 父慶祺，從陳奐遊。

translations.literal: His father Qingqi studied with Chen Huan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qingqi studied with Chen Huan.

sentences.zh: 禮耕篤守家學，尤長訓詁。

translations.literal: Ligeng faithfully maintained family learning and was especially expert in glosses.
translations.idiomatic: Ligeng faithfully maintained family learning and was especially expert in glosses.

sentences.zh: 嘗言唐以正義立學官，漢、魏、六朝遺說，積久泰半闕不完。

translations.literal: He once said that since Tang times the Correct Meaning was established in the state academy, Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties survivals over long years were mostly incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: He once said that since Tang times the Correct Meaning was established in the state academy, Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties survivals had mostly been lost.

sentences.zh: 凡所考見，獨存釋文，而今本踳駮非其舊，思綜稽群籍為校證，未及半而卒。

translations.literal: Of what can be verified, only the Shiwen survives, yet today's edition is confused and not the original; he planned to collate all books for verification but died before half was done.
translations.idiomatic: Of what survives, only the Shiwen remains, yet today's edition is corrupt; he planned a comprehensive collation but died before half was done.

sentences.zh: 袁寶璜，字朅禹，元和人。

translations.literal: Yuan Baohuang, styled Jieyu, was a native of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Baohuang, styled Jieyu, was from Yuanhe.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十一年進士，官刑部主事。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the twenty-first year of Guangxu, he served as secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the twenty-first year of Guangxu (1895), he served as secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 通經、小學，兼及算術。

translations.literal: He was versed in the classics and philology and also in mathematics.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in the classics and philology and also in mathematics.

sentences.zh: 著書亦未成而卒。

translations.literal: His writings were also unfinished when he died.
translations.idiomatic: His writings were also unfinished when he died.

sentences.zh: 李慈銘，字愛伯，會稽人。

translations.literal: Li Ciming, styled Aibo, was a native of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ciming, styled Aibo, was from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 諸生，入貲為戶部郎中。

translations.literal: A student, he purchased office as director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate, he purchased office as director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 至都，即以詩文名於時。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital he was at once famed in his day for poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital he was at once famed for poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 大學士周祖培、尚書潘祖廕引為上客。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhou Zupei and Minister Pan Zuyin took him as a honored guest.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhou Zupei and Minister Pan Zuyin took him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，成進士，歸本班，改御史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he became a jinshi, returned to his original rank, and changed to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Guangxu (1880) he became a jinshi, returned to his original rank, and changed to censor.

sentences.zh: 時朝政日非，慈銘遇事建言，請臨雍，請整頓台綱。

translations.literal: At the time court affairs daily worsened; Ciming remonstrated on affairs, requesting the emperor lecture at the imperial school and requesting rectification of the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: As court affairs daily worsened, Ciming remonstrated, requesting the emperor lecture at the imperial school and requesting rectification of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 大臣則糾孫毓汶、孫楫，疆臣則糾德馨、沈秉成、裕寬，數上疏，均不報。

translations.literal: Among grand ministers he impeached Sun Yuweng and Sun Ji; among frontier officials De Xin, Shen Bingcheng, and Yu Kuan—several memorials, all unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: Among grand ministers he impeached Sun Yuweng and Sun Ji; among frontier officials De Xin, Shen Bingcheng, and Yu Kuan—several memorials, all unanswered.

sentences.zh: 慈銘鬱鬱而卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: Ciming died in depression at sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Ciming died in depression at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 慈銘為文沉博絕麗，詩尤工，自成一家。

translations.literal: Ciming's prose was deep, vast, and surpassingly beautiful; his poetry was especially skilled, forming a school of his own.
translations.idiomatic: Ciming's prose was deep, vast, and surpassingly beautiful; his poetry was especially skilled, forming a school of his own.

sentences.zh: 性狷介，又口多雌黃。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and aloof, and his mouth was full of criticism.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and aloof, and his tongue was sharp.

sentences.zh: 服其學者好之，憎其口者惡之。

translations.literal: Those who admired his learning liked him; those who hated his mouth detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who admired his learning liked him; those who resented his tongue detested him.

sentences.zh: 日有課記，每讀一書，必求其所蓄之深淺，致力之先後，而評騭之，務得其當，後進翕然大服。

translations.literal: He kept daily lesson notes; for every book read he sought the depth of what it stored and the order of effort, judging it and striving to be fair; younger scholars were greatly convinced.
translations.idiomatic: He kept daily lesson notes; for every book he judged the depth of its learning and the order of effort required; younger scholars were greatly convinced.

sentences.zh: 著有越縵堂文十卷，白華絳趺閣詩十卷、詞二卷，又日記數十冊。

translations.literal: His works include ten fascicles of Yuemantang prose, ten fascicles of Baihua Jiangqiu Studio poetry and two of lyric song, and several dozen volumes of diary.
translations.idiomatic: His works include ten fascicles of Yuemantang prose, ten fascicles of Baihua Jiangqiu Studio poetry and two of lyric song, and several dozen volumes of diary.

sentences.zh: 弟子著錄數百人，同邑陶方琦為最。

translations.literal: Recorded disciples numbered several hundred; his fellow townsman Tao Fangqi was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Recorded disciples numbered several hundred; his fellow townsman Tao Fangqi was foremost.

sentences.zh: 方琦，字子珍。

translations.literal: Fangqi, styled Zizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Fangqi, styled Zizhen.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the second year of Guangxu, he was selected as bachelor and appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the second year of Guangxu (1876), he was selected as bachelor and appointed Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 督學湖南。

translations.literal: He served as educational commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as educational commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 年四十，卒於京邸。

translations.literal: At forty he died in his Beijing lodging.
translations.idiomatic: At forty he died in his Beijing lodging.

sentences.zh: 方琦學有本末，汲汲於古，述造無間歲時。

translations.literal: Fangqi's learning had root and branch; eagerly pursuing antiquity, he wrote without idle years.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqi's learning had root and branch; eagerly pursuing antiquity, he wrote without idle years.

sentences.zh: 治易鄭注，詩魯故，爾雅漢注，又習大戴禮記。

translations.literal: He studied Zheng's commentary on the Changes, Lu tradition of the Odes, Han commentary on the Erya, and also practiced the Elder Dai's Record of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He studied Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Changes, the Lu tradition of the Odes, Han commentary on the Erya, and the Elder Dai's Record of Rites.

sentences.zh: 其治淮南王書，力以推究經訓，蒐採許注，拾補高誘。

translations.literal: In studying the Huainan King's book he strove to investigate classical glosses, gather Xu Shen's commentary, and supplement Gao You.
translations.idiomatic: In studying the Huainanzi he strove to investigate classical glosses, gather Xu Shen's commentary, and supplement Gao You.

sentences.zh: 再三屬草，矻矻十年，實事求是。

translations.literal: Drafting again and again, laboring ten years, he sought truth from facts.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting again and again over ten years, he sought truth from facts.

sentences.zh: 有淮南許注異同詁、許君年表、漢孳室文鈔、駢文、詩詞。

translations.literal: He had Collated Notes on Xu Shen's Huainan Commentary, Chronological Table of Master Xu, Han Zishi Studio Literary Transcription, parallel prose, and lyric poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Collated Notes on Xu Shen's Huainan Commentary, Chronological Table of Master Xu, Han Zishi Studio Literary Transcription, parallel prose, and lyric poetry.

sentences.zh: 譚廷獻，字仲修，仁和人。

translations.literal: Tan Tingxian, styled Zhongxiu, was a native of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Tingxian, styled Zhongxiu, was from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 同治六年舉人。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the sixth year of Tongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate in the sixth year of Tongzhi (1867).

sentences.zh: 少負志節，通知時事。

translations.literal: In youth he bore resolve and integrity and was well informed on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he bore resolve and integrity and was well informed on current affairs.

sentences.zh: 國家政制典禮，能講求其義。

translations.literal: State institutions and ritual propriety—he could investigate their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He could investigate the meaning of state institutions and ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 治經必求西漢諸儒微言大義，不屑屑章句。

translations.literal: In studying the classics he always sought the subtle words and great meaning of Western Han ruists, disdaining mere chapter-and-verse work.
translations.idiomatic: In studying the classics he sought the subtle words and great meaning of Western Han scholars, disdaining mere chapter-and-verse work.

sentences.zh: 讀書日有程課，凡所論箸，隱栝於所為日記。

translations.literal: In reading he had daily schedules; all he discussed and wrote was summarized in his diary.
translations.idiomatic: In reading he kept daily schedules; all he discussed and wrote was summarized in his diary.

sentences.zh: 文導源漢、魏，詩優柔善入，惻然動人。

translations.literal: His prose took Han and Wei as source; his poetry was gentle and moving, stirring pity.
translations.idiomatic: His prose took Han and Wei as source; his poetry was gentle and moving, stirring pity.

sentences.zh: 又工詞，與慈銘友善，相唱和。

translations.literal: He was also skilled at lyric song and was friendly with Ciming, exchanging compositions.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled at lyric song and exchanged compositions with Ciming.

sentences.zh: 官安徽，知歙、全椒、合肥、宿松諸縣。

translations.literal: He served in Anhui as magistrate of She, Quanjiao, Hefei, and Susong.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Anhui as magistrate of She, Quanjiao, Hefei, and Susong.

sentences.zh: 晚告歸，貧甚。

translations.literal: In his later years he requested leave and returned home, very poor.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he returned home, very poor.

sentences.zh: 張之洞延主經心書院，年餘謝歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhidong engaged him to head the Jingxin Academy; after a year he declined and returned, dying at home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhidong engaged him to head the Jingxin Academy; after a year he declined and died at home.

sentences.zh: 李稷勳，字姚琴，秀山人。

translations.literal: Li Jixun, styled Yaoqin, was a native of Xiushan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jixun, styled Yaoqin, was from Xiushan.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十四年二甲一名進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Second in the second rank in the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu, he changed to bachelor and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Second in the second rank in the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu (1898), he changed to bachelor and was appointed Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 充會試同考官，精衡鑑，重實學，頗得知名士。

translations.literal: He served as associate metropolitan examiner, precise in judgment, valuing practical learning, and obtained many famed scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He served as associate metropolitan examiner, precise in judgment, valuing practical learning, and obtained many famed scholars.

sentences.zh: 累官郵傳部參議，總川漢路事。

translations.literal: He rose to counselor in the Ministry of Posts and oversaw Sichuan-Hankou railway affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to counselor in the Ministry of Posts and oversaw Sichuan-Hankou railway affairs.

sentences.zh: 博學善古文，嘗受詩法於王闓運，而不囿師說。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and skilled at ancient prose, he once received poetic instruction from Wang Kaiyun yet was not confined by his teacher's doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and skilled at ancient prose, he studied poetry under Wang Kaiyun yet was not confined by his teacher's doctrine.

sentences.zh: 專步趨唐賢，意致深婉，得風人之遺。

translations.literal: He exclusively followed Tang masters; his meaning was deep and graceful, obtaining the legacy of the Wind.
translations.idiomatic: He exclusively followed Tang masters; his meaning was deep and graceful, obtaining the legacy of the Book of Songs.

sentences.zh: 慈銘嘗稱賞之。

translations.literal: Ciming once praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Ciming once praised him.

sentences.zh: 有甓盦詩錄四卷。

translations.literal: He had four fascicles of the Bie'an Poetry Record.
translations.idiomatic: His Bie'an Poetry Record runs to four fascicles.

sentences.zh: 張裕釗，字廉卿，武昌人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuzhao, styled Lianqing, was a native of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuzhao, styled Lianqing, was from Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 少時，塾師授以製舉業，意不樂。

translations.literal: In youth his tutor taught examination essays; he was unwilling.
translations.idiomatic: In youth his tutor taught examination essays; he was unwilling.

sentences.zh: 家獨有南豐集，時時竊讀之。

translations.literal: At home alone they had the Nanfeng Collection; he often stole time to read it.
translations.idiomatic: At home they had the Nanfeng Collection; he often stole time to read it.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年舉人，考授內閣中書。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the first year of Xianfeng, he was appointed Secretariat compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate in the first year of Xianfeng (1851), he was appointed Secretariat compiler.

sentences.zh: 曾國藩閱卷賞其文，既，來見，曰：「子豈嘗習子固文耶？」

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan, reading his paper, praised his writing; afterward, meeting him, said: "Have you studied Zeng Gong's prose?"
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan, reading his examination paper, praised his writing; meeting him afterward, said, "Have you studied Zeng Gong's prose?

sentences.zh: 裕釗私自喜。

translations.literal: Yuzhao secretly rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhao secretly rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 已而國藩益告以文事利病及唐、宋以來家法，學乃大進，寤前此所為猶凡近，馬遷、班固、相如、揚雄之書，無一日不誦習。

translations.literal: Afterward Guofan further told him the strengths and weaknesses of literary affairs and the family methods since Tang and Song; his learning greatly advanced, awakening that what he had done before was still commonplace; the books of Sima Qian, Ban Gu, Sima Xiangru, and Yang Xiong he recited not a day without practice.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan further instructed him in literary craft and family methods since Tang and Song; his learning advanced greatly, and he saw that his earlier work was still commonplace; he recited Sima Qian, Ban Gu, Sima Xiangru, and Yang Xiong daily without fail.

sentences.zh: 又精八法，由魏、晉、六朝以上窺漢隸，臨池之勤，亦未嘗一日輟。

translations.literal: He was also expert in the eight scripts; from Wei, Jin, and the Six Dynasties upward he peered into Han clerical script; diligence at the inkstone never ceased a day.
translations.idiomatic: He was also expert in calligraphy; from Wei, Jin, and the Six Dynasties upward he studied Han clerical script; diligence at the inkstone never ceased.

sentences.zh: 國藩既成大功，出其門者多通顯。

translations.literal: After Guofan achieved great merit, many who came from his gate attained high office.
translations.idiomatic: After Guofan achieved great merit, many who came from his gate attained high office.

sentences.zh: 裕釗相從數十年，獨以治文為事。

translations.literal: Yuzhao followed him several decades, devoting himself solely to writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhao followed him for decades, devoting himself solely to writing.

sentences.zh: 國藩為文，義法取桐城，益閎以漢賦之氣體，尤善裕釗之文。

translations.literal: Guofan's writing took principles of composition from Tongcheng, further broadened with the breath of Han fu, and he especially valued Yuzhao's writing.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan's writing took composition principles from Tongcheng, broadened with Han fu breath, and he especially valued Yuzhao's writing.

sentences.zh: 嘗言「吾門人可期有成者，惟張、吳兩生」，謂裕釗及吳汝綸也。

translations.literal: He once said: "Among my disciples those who may be expected to succeed are only the two students Zhang and Wu," meaning Yuzhao and Wu Rulun.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Among my disciples those who may succeed are only Zhang and Wu," meaning Yuzhao and Wu Rulun.

sentences.zh: 裕釗文字淵懿，歷主江寧、湖北、直隸、陝西各書院，成就後學甚眾。

translations.literal: Yuzhao's writing was profound and refined; he headed academies in Jiangning, Hubei, Zhili, and Shaanxi, achieving many later students.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhao's writing was profound and refined; he headed academies in Jiangning, Hubei, Zhili, and Shaanxi, training many students.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「文以意為主，而辭欲能副其意，氣欲能舉其辭。

translations.literal: He once said: "Writing takes meaning as master, yet diction must be able to match the meaning, and breath must be able to carry the diction.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Writing takes meaning as master, yet diction must match the meaning, and breath must carry the diction.

sentences.zh: 譬之車然，意為之禦，辭為之載，而氣則所以行也。

translations.literal: It is like a carriage: meaning is the driver, diction the load, and breath is what makes it go.
translations.idiomatic: It is like a carriage: meaning is the driver, diction the load, and breath is what makes it go.

sentences.zh: 欲學古人之文，其始在因聲以求氣，得其氣，則意與辭往往因之而益顯，而法不外是矣。」

translations.literal: To study ancient writing, one must begin by seeking breath through sound; obtaining breath, meaning and diction often thereby grow more manifest, and method is nothing outside this."
translations.idiomatic: To study ancient writing, one must begin by seeking breath through sound; obtaining breath, meaning and diction grow more manifest, and method is nothing outside this.

sentences.zh: 世以為知言。

translations.literal: The age considered this knowing speech.
translations.idiomatic: The age considered this penetrating insight.

sentences.zh: 著濂亭文集。

translations.literal: He authored the Lian Pavilion Prose Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Lian Pavilion Prose Collection.

sentences.zh: 裕釗門下最知名者，有范當世、朱銘盤。

translations.literal: Among Yuzhao's disciples the most famed were Fan Dangshi and Zhu Mingpan.
translations.idiomatic: Among Yuzhao's disciples the most famed were Fan Dangshi and Zhu Mingpan.

sentences.zh: 當世，字肯堂，江蘇通州諸生。

translations.literal: Dangshi, styled Kentang, was a student of Tongzhou, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Dangshi, styled Kentang, was a student of Tongzhou, Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 能詩，汝綸嘗歎其奇橫不可敵。

translations.literal: He could write poetry; Rulun once sighed that its bold strangeness was unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: He could write poetry; Rulun once sighed that its bold strangeness was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 著范伯子詩文集。

translations.literal: He authored the Fan Bozi Poetry and Prose Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His Fan Bozi Poetry and Prose Collection survives.

sentences.zh: 銘盤，字曼君，泰興舉人。

translations.literal: Mingpan, styled Manjun, was a provincial graduate of Taixing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mingpan, styled Manjun, was a provincial graduate of Taixing.

sentences.zh: 敘知州。

translations.literal: He was appointed by qualification as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed by qualification as prefect.

sentences.zh: 其學長於史，兼工詩古文。

translations.literal: His learning excelled in history and he was also skilled at poetry and ancient prose.
translations.idiomatic: His learning excelled in history and he was also skilled at poetry and ancient prose.

sentences.zh: 著晉會要一百卷，朝鮮長編四十卷，及桂之華軒詩文集。

translations.literal: He authored one hundred fascicles of Comprehensive Essentials of Jin, forty fascicles of the Korean Long Compilation, and the Guizhihua Studio Poetry and Prose Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Comprehensive Essentials of Jin in one hundred fascicles, the Korean Long Compilation in forty fascicles, and the Guizhihua Studio Poetry and Prose Collection.

sentences.zh: 與裕釗同時者，有楊守敬，字惺吾，宜都人。

translations.literal: Contemporary with Yuzhao was Yang Shoujing, styled Xingwu, a native of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary with Yuzhao was Yang Shoujing of Yidu, styled Xingwu.

sentences.zh: 為文不足躋裕釗，而其學通博。

translations.literal: In writing he did not reach Yuzhao's level, yet his learning was comprehensive and broad.
translations.idiomatic: In prose he did not reach Yuzhao's level, yet his learning was comprehensive and broad.

sentences.zh: 精輿地，用力於水經尤勤。

translations.literal: He was expert in geography and labored especially on the Water Classic.
translations.idiomatic: He was expert in geography and labored especially on the Water Classic.

sentences.zh: 通訓詁，考證金石文字。

translations.literal: He mastered glosses and verified inscriptions on bronzes and stones.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered glosses and verified inscriptions on bronzes and stones.

sentences.zh: 能書，摹鐘鼎至精。

translations.literal: He could write and traced bell and tripod inscriptions with utmost precision.
translations.idiomatic: He could write calligraphy and traced bell and tripod inscriptions with utmost precision.

sentences.zh: 工儷體，為箴銘之屬，古奧聳拔，文如其人。

translations.literal: Skilled at parallel style in admonitions and inscriptions, ancient and lofty, his writing matched the man.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at parallel style in admonitions and inscriptions, ancient and lofty, his writing matched the man.

sentences.zh: 以舉人官黃岡教諭，加中書銜。

translations.literal: As a provincial graduate he served as instructor of Huanggang and was given the rank of Secretariat compiler.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial graduate he served as instructor of Huanggang and was given the rank of Secretariat compiler.

sentences.zh: 嘗遊日本，搜古籍，多得唐、宋善本，辛苦積貲，藏書數十萬卷，為鄂學靈光者垂二十年。

translations.literal: He once traveled to Japan searching ancient books, obtaining many fine Tang and Song editions; painstakingly accumulating funds, his collection numbered several hundred thousand volumes and was the glory of Hubei learning for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled to Japan seeking ancient books, obtaining many fine Tang and Song editions; through painstaking effort his collection numbered several hundred thousand volumes and was the glory of Hubei learning for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十有七。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 著有水經註圖、水經註要刪、隋書地理志考證、日本訪書志、晦明軒稿、鄰蘇老人題跋、望堂金石集等。

translations.literal: His works include Maps of the Water Classic Commentary, Essentials of the Water Classic Commentary, Textual Verification of the Treatise on Geography in the History of Sui, Record of Book-Seeking in Japan, Drafts of the Huiming Studio, Colophons of the Elder from Linsu, and Collected Stone Inscriptions of the Wangtang.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Maps of the Water Classic Commentary, Essentials of the Water Classic Commentary, Textual Verification of the Treatise on Geography in the History of Sui, Record of Book-Seeking in Japan, and Collected Stone Inscriptions of the Wangtang.

sentences.zh: 吳汝綸，字摯父，桐城人。

translations.literal: Wu Rulun, styled Zhifu, was a native of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Rulun, styled Zhifu, was from Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 少貧力學，嘗得雞卵一，易松脂以照讀。

translations.literal: Poor in youth he strove in learning; he once got a chicken egg and exchanged it for pine resin to read by lamplight.
translations.idiomatic: Poor in youth he strove in learning; he once traded a chicken egg for pine resin to read by lamplight.

sentences.zh: 好文出天性，早著文名。

translations.literal: He loved writing by nature and early won literary fame.
translations.idiomatic: He loved writing by nature and early won literary fame.

sentences.zh: 同治四年進士，用內閣中書。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fourth year of Tongzhi, he was appointed Secretariat compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the fourth year of Tongzhi (1865), he was appointed Secretariat compiler.

sentences.zh: 曾國藩奇其文，留佐幕府，久乃益奇之，嘗以漢禰衡相儗。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan marveled at his writing; meeting him later he said: "Have you studied Zeng Gong's prose?" Rulun secretly rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan marveled at his writing; meeting him later he said, "Have you studied Zeng Gong's prose?" Rulun secretly rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 旋調直隸，參李鴻章幕。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Zhili and joined Li Hongzhang's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Zhili and joined Li Hongzhang's staff.

sentences.zh: 時中外大政常決於國藩、鴻章二人，其奏疏多出汝綸手。

translations.literal: At the time major domestic and foreign policies were often decided by Guofan and Hongzhang; their memorials mostly came from Rulun's hand.
translations.idiomatic: At the time major domestic and foreign policies were often decided by Guofan and Hongzhang; their memorials mostly came from Rulun's hand.

sentences.zh: 尋出補深州，丁外內艱。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as magistrate of Shenzhou and mourned father and mother.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to serve as magistrate of Shenzhou and mourned his parents.

sentences.zh: 服除，補冀州。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was made up at Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was made up as magistrate of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 其治以教育為先，不憚貴勢，籍深州諸村已廢學田為豪民侵奪者千四百餘畝入書院，資膏火。

translations.literal: His governance put education first; he did not fear the powerful, registering more than fourteen hundred mu of abandoned school fields in Shenzhou villages seized by local bullies and putting them into the academy to fund stipends.
translations.idiomatic: His governance put education first; he did not fear the powerful, recovering more than fourteen hundred mu of abandoned school fields in Shenzhou villages seized by local bullies for academy stipends.

sentences.zh: 聚一州三縣高材生親教課之，民忘其吏，推為大師。

translations.literal: He gathered talented students from three districts of the prefecture and taught them personally; the people forgot he was an official and acclaimed him as a great master.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered talented students from three districts and taught them personally; the people forgot he was an official and acclaimed him as a great master.

sentences.zh: 會以憂去，豪民至交通御史以壞村學劾奏，還其田。

translations.literal: When he left on mourning, bullies colluded with censors to destroy village schools by memorial, and the fields were returned.
translations.idiomatic: When he left on mourning, bullies colluded with censors to destroy village schools by memorial, and the fields were returned.

sentences.zh: 及蒞冀州，仍銳意興學，深、冀二州文教斐然冠畿輔。

translations.literal: On taking office at Jizhou he still keenly promoted learning; the literary culture of Shen and Ji prefectures flourished foremost in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office at Jizhou he still keenly promoted learning; literary culture in Shen and Ji prefectures flourished foremost in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 又開冀、衡六十里之渠，洩積水於滏，以溉田畝，便商旅。

translations.literal: He also opened a sixty-li canal between Ji and Heng, draining accumulated water into the Fu River to irrigate fields and benefit merchants and travelers.
translations.idiomatic: He also opened a sixty-li canal between Ji and Heng, draining accumulated water into the Fu River to irrigate fields and benefit travel.

sentences.zh: 時時求其士之賢有文者禮先之，得十許人。

translations.literal: He constantly sought worthy men of literary talent and honored them first, obtaining about ten.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly sought worthy men of literary talent and honored them, obtaining about ten.

sentences.zh: 月一會書院，議所施為興革於民便不便，率不依常格。

translations.literal: Once a month he met at the academy to discuss what to undertake or abolish for the people's convenience, mostly not following conventional patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly he met at the academy to discuss reforms for the people's convenience, mostly not following conventional patterns.

sentences.zh: 稱疾乞休。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 鴻章素重其人，延主蓮池講席。

translations.literal: Hongzhang had always valued him and engaged him to head the Lianchi lectureship.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang had always valued him and engaged him to head the Lianchi lectureship.

sentences.zh: 其為教，一主乎文，以為：「文者，天地之至精至粹，吾國所獨優。

translations.literal: In teaching he took writing as the master, holding: "Writing is the utmost essence and purity of heaven and earth; our country alone excels in it.
translations.idiomatic: In teaching he took writing as master, holding, "Writing is the utmost essence and purity of heaven and earth; our country alone excels in it.

sentences.zh: 語其實用，則歐、美新學尚焉。

translations.literal: In practical application, European and American new learning is esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: In practical application, European and American new learning is esteemed.

sentences.zh: 博物格致機械之用，必取資於彼，得其長乃能共競。

translations.literal: The uses of natural history, investigation of things, and mechanics must draw on them; only by gaining their strengths can we compete together.
translations.idiomatic: Natural history, investigation of things, and mechanics must draw on the West; only by gaining their strengths can we compete.

sentences.zh: 舊法完且好，吾猶將革新之，況其窳敗不可復用。」

translations.literal: Old methods complete and good—we would still innovate them; how much more when they are worn out and cannot be reused."
translations.idiomatic: Old methods complete and good—we would still innovate them; how much more when they are worn out and unusable.

sentences.zh: 其勤勤導誘後生，常以是為說。

translations.literal: He diligently guided younger students, always speaking thus.
translations.idiomatic: He diligently guided younger students, always speaking thus.

sentences.zh: 嘗樂與西士遊，而日本之慕文章者，亦踔海來請業。

translations.literal: He delighted in associating with Western scholars, and Japanese admirers of literature also crossed the sea to request instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in associating with Western scholars, and Japanese admirers of literature also crossed the sea to study with him.

sentences.zh: 會朝旨開大學堂於京師，管學大臣張百熙奏薦汝綸加五品卿銜總教務，辭不獲，則請赴日本考學制。

translations.literal: When the court ordered a university established in the capital, Director of Education Zhang Boxi memorialized recommending Rulun with fifth-rank insignia as general superintendent of instruction; unable to decline, he requested to go to Japan to study the school system.
translations.idiomatic: When the court ordered a university in the capital, Zhang Boxi recommended Rulun with fifth-rank insignia as general superintendent; unable to decline, he requested to go to Japan to study the school system.

sentences.zh: 既至其國，上自君、相及教育名家，婦孺學子，皆備禮接款，求請題詠，更番踵至。

translations.literal: Arriving in that country, from the ruler and ministers to famous educators, women and children, all received him with full courtesy; requests for inscriptions and poems came in endless succession.
translations.idiomatic: In Japan, from the ruler and ministers to famous educators, all received him with full courtesy; requests for inscriptions and poems came in endless succession.

sentences.zh: 旋返國，先乞假省墓，興辦本邑小學堂。

translations.literal: Soon returning home, he first requested leave to visit his family's graves and established the local primary school.
translations.idiomatic: Soon returning home, he first requested leave to visit his family's graves and established the local primary school.

sentences.zh: 規制粗立，遽以疾卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: When regulations were roughly set up he suddenly died of illness at sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: When regulations were roughly established he suddenly died of illness at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 汝綸為學，由訓詁以通文辭，無古今，無中外，唯是之求。

translations.literal: Rulun's learning passed through glosses to master literary expression, without regard to ancient or modern, Chinese or foreign—only seeking what was right.
translations.idiomatic: Rulun's learning passed through glosses to literary expression, without regard to ancient or modern, Chinese or foreign—only seeking what was right.

sentences.zh: 自群經子史、周、秦故籍，以下逮近世方、姚諸文集，無不博求慎取，窮其原而竟其委。

translations.literal: From the classics and masters, Zhou and Qin ancient texts, down to the collected works of Fang and Yao of recent times, he sought broadly and chose carefully, tracing origins to ends.
translations.idiomatic: From the classics and masters through Zhou and Qin texts down to Fang and Yao's collected works, he sought broadly and chose carefully, tracing origins to ends.

sentences.zh: 於經，則易、書、詩、禮、左氏、穀梁、四子書，旁及小學音韻，各有​​詮釋。

translations.literal: In the classics he explained the Changes, Documents, Odes, Rites, Zuo Commentary, Guliang, and the Four Books, and also philology and phonology, each with commentary.
translations.idiomatic: In the classics he explained the Changes, Documents, Odes, Rites, Zuo Commentary, Guliang, and Four Books, and also philology and phonology, each with commentary.

sentences.zh: 於史，則史記、漢書、三國志、新五代史、資治通鑑、國語、國策皆有點校，尤邃於史記，盡發太史公立言微旨。

translations.literal: In history he collated the Records of the Grand Historian, History of Han, Records of the Three Kingdoms, New History of the Five Dynasties, Comprehensive Mirror, Discourses of the States, and Strategies of the Warring States, especially penetrating the Records and fully releasing the Grand Historian's subtle intent.
translations.idiomatic: In history he collated the Records, History of Han, Records of the Three Kingdoms, New History of the Five Dynasties, Comprehensive Mirror, Discourses of the States, and Strategies of the Warring States, especially penetrating the Records and releasing the Grand Historian's subtle intent.

sentences.zh: 於子，則老、莊、荀、韓、管、墨、呂覽、淮南、法言、太玄各有評騭，而最取其精者。

translations.literal: In masters he judged Laozi, Zhuangzi, Xunzi, Han Fei, Guanzi, Mozi, Lüshi Chunqiu, Huainanzi, Fayan, and Taixuan, taking the finest.
translations.idiomatic: In masters he judged Laozi, Zhuangzi, Xunzi, Han Fei, and others, taking the finest.

sentences.zh: 於集，則楚辭、文選，漢魏以來各大家詩文皆有點勘之本。

translations.literal: In collections he had collated editions of the Songs of Chu, Wenxuan, and major poets and prose writers from Han and Wei onward.
translations.idiomatic: In collections he had collated editions of the Songs of Chu, Wenxuan, and major writers from Han and Wei onward.

sentences.zh: 凡所啟發，皆能得其深微，整齊百代，別白高下，而一以貫之。

translations.literal: All he opened up could obtain their depth; ordering a hundred generations and distinguishing high and low, he unified them in one thread.
translations.idiomatic: All he opened up reached their depth; ordering a hundred generations and distinguishing high and low, he unified them in one thread.

sentences.zh: 盡取古人不傳之蘊，昭然揭示，俾學者易於研求；

translations.literal: He fully took what the ancients did not transmit, revealing it clearly so scholars could easily pursue it;
translations.idiomatic: He revealed what the ancients did not transmit so scholars could easily pursue it;

sentences.zh: 且以識夫作文之軌範，雖萬變不窮，而千載如出一轍。

translations.literal: and thereby recognized the norms of composition—though ten thousand changes never exhaust it, a thousand years are as one track.
translations.idiomatic: and thereby recognized the norms of composition—though ten thousand changes never exhaust it, a thousand years follow one track.

sentences.zh: 其論文，嘗謂：「千秋蓋世之勳業皆尋常耳，獨文章之事，緯地經天，代不數人，人不數篇，唯此為難。」

translations.literal: Discussing writing he once said: "Merit passing down through the ages is ordinary; only literary affairs span heaven and earth, generation after generation few in men and few in pieces—only this is hard."
translations.idiomatic: Discussing writing he once said, "Merit passing down through the ages is ordinary; only literary affairs span heaven and earth—few men and few pieces per generation—only this is hard.

sentences.zh: 又謂：「中國之文，非徒習其字形而已，綴字為文，而氣行乎其間，寄聲音神采於文外。

translations.literal: He also said: "Chinese writing is not merely learning character forms; stringing characters into text, breath moves between them, lodging sound, spirit, and expression beyond the words.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Chinese writing is not merely learning character forms; stringing characters into text, breath moves between them, lodging spirit beyond the words.

sentences.zh: 雖古之聖賢豪傑去吾世邈矣，一涉其書，而其人之精神意氣若儼立乎吾目中。」

translations.literal: Though ancient sages and heroes are remote from our age, once one enters their books, their spirit and intent seem to stand before one's eyes."
translations.idiomatic: Though ancient sages and heroes are remote, once one enters their books, their spirit seems to stand before one's eyes.

sentences.zh: 務欲因聲求氣，凡所為抗墜、詘折、斷續、斂侈、緩急、長短、伸縮、抑揚、頓挫之節，一循乎機勢之自然，以漸於精微奧之域。

translations.literal: He strove to seek breath through sound; in all turns of elevation, deflection, break, continuity, restraint, expansion, slow and quick, long and short, stretch and contract, suppression, pause, and cadence, he followed the natural momentum of opportunity, gradually approaching the realm of subtlety and mystery.
translations.idiomatic: He strove to seek breath through sound; in every turn of cadence he followed natural momentum, gradually approaching subtlety and mystery.

sentences.zh: 乃有以化裁而致於用，悉舉學問與事業合而為一；

translations.literal: Thus he could transform and bring to use, fully joining learning and career in one;
translations.idiomatic: Thus he could transform and bring to use, fully joining learning and career in one;

sentences.zh: 而尤以瀹民智自強亟時病為兢兢云。

translations.literal: and especially took irrigating popular intelligence and urgent strengthening of the age's ills as his constant care.
translations.idiomatic: and especially took irrigating popular intelligence and strengthening the age as his constant care.

sentences.zh: 著有易說二卷、寫定尚書一卷、尚書故三卷、夏小正私箋一卷、文集四卷、詩集一卷、深州風土記二十二卷，及點勘諸書，皆行於世。

translations.literal: His works include two fascicles of Explanation of the Changes, one fascicle each of Definitive Documents and Ancient Documents, one fascicle of Private Commentary on the Lesser Calendar, four fascicles of prose and one of poetry, twenty-two fascicles of Customs of Shenzhou, and collated books—all circulating.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Explanation of the Changes, Definitive and Ancient Documents, Private Commentary on the Lesser Calendar, prose and poetry collections, Customs of Shenzhou in twenty-two fascicles, and collated books—all circulating.

sentences.zh: 汝綸門下最著者為賀濤，而同時有蕭穆，亦以通考據名。

translations.literal: Rulun's most prominent disciple was He Tao; at the same time Xiao Mu was also famed for comprehensive evidential scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: Rulun's most prominent disciple was He Tao; at the same time Xiao Mu was also famed for evidential scholarship.

sentences.zh: 穆，字敬孚。

translations.literal: Mu, styled Jingfu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Mu, styled Jingfu.

sentences.zh: 縣學生。

translations.literal: A district student.
translations.idiomatic: A district student.

sentences.zh: 其學博綜群籍，喜談掌故，於顧炎武、全祖望諸家之書尤熟。

translations.literal: His learning comprehensively covered many books; he delighted in discussing historical anecdotes and was especially familiar with Gu Yanwu and Quan Zuwang.
translations.idiomatic: His learning covered many books; he delighted in historical anecdotes and was especially familiar with Gu Yanwu and Quan Zuwang.

sentences.zh: 復多見舊槧，考其異同，硃墨雜下。

translations.literal: He also saw many old manuscripts, comparing variants with red and ink mixed.
translations.idiomatic: He also saw many old manuscripts, comparing variants with annotations in red and ink.

sentences.zh: 遇孤本多方勸刻，所校印凡百餘種。

translations.literal: Encountering unique editions he often urged publication; what he collated and printed totaled more than a hundred kinds.
translations.idiomatic: Encountering unique editions he often urged publication; his collations totaled more than a hundred kinds.

sentences.zh: 有敬孚類藁十六卷。

translations.literal: He had sixteen fascicles of the Jingfu Miscellany.
translations.idiomatic: His Jingfu Miscellany runs to sixteen fascicles.

sentences.zh: 濤，字松坡，武強人。

translations.literal: Tao, styled Songpo, was a native of Wuqiang.
translations.idiomatic: He Tao, styled Songpo, was from Wuqiang.

sentences.zh: 光緒十二年進士，官刑部主事。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the twelfth year of Guangxu, he served as secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the twelfth year of Guangxu (1886), he served as secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 以目疾去官。

translations.literal: He left office because of eye disease.
translations.idiomatic: He left office because of eye disease.

sentences.zh: 初，汝綸牧深州，見濤所為反離騷，大奇之，遂盡授以所學，復使受學於張裕釗。

translations.literal: At first, when Rulun was magistrate of Shenzhou, he saw Tao's Counter-Rhapsody on Encountering Sorrow and marveled greatly, thereupon teaching him all he knew and also having him study under Zhang Yuzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Rulun was magistrate of Shenzhou, he saw Tao's Counter-Rhapsody on Encountering Sorrow and marveled, teaching him all he knew and also sending him to study under Zhang Yuzhao.

sentences.zh: 濤謹守兩家師說，於姚鼐義理、考據、詞章三者不可偏廢之說，尤必以詞章為貫澈始終，日與學者討論義法不厭。

translations.literal: Tao strictly maintained both masters' doctrines; on Yao Nai's saying that principle, evidential scholarship, and literary craft must not be neglected, he especially required literary craft to run through from start to finish, daily discussing principles of composition with students without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Tao strictly maintained both masters' doctrines; on Yao Nai's triad of principle, evidential scholarship, and literary craft, he especially required literary craft throughout, daily discussing composition with students without weariness.

sentences.zh: 與同年生劉孚京俱治古文，濤言宜先以八家立門戶，而上窺秦、漢；

translations.literal: With fellow graduate Liu Fujing he both studied ancient prose; Tao said one should first establish the Eight Masters as one's school and look up to Qin and Han;
translations.idiomatic: With fellow graduate Liu Fujing he both studied ancient prose; Tao said one should first establish the Eight Masters as one's school and look up to Qin and Han;

sentences.zh: 孚京言宜先以秦、漢為根柢，而下攬八家，其門徑大略相同。

translations.literal: Fujing said one should first take Qin and Han as foundation and draw in the Eight Masters below—their paths were largely the same.
translations.idiomatic: Fujing said one should first take Qin and Han as foundation and draw in the Eight Masters below—their paths were largely the same.

sentences.zh: 濤有文集四卷。

translations.literal: Tao had four fascicles of collected prose.
translations.idiomatic: Tao's collected prose runs to four fascicles.

sentences.zh: 孚京，字鎬仲，南昌人。

translations.literal: Fujing, styled Haozhong, was a native of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fujing, styled Haozhong, was from Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 有文集六卷。

translations.literal: He had six fascicles of collected prose.
translations.idiomatic: His collected prose runs to six fascicles.

sentences.zh: 生平任俠尚氣節，嫉惡嚴。

translations.literal: Throughout life he was chivalrous and esteemed integrity, stern in hatred of evil.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout life he was chivalrous and esteemed integrity, stern in hatred of evil.

sentences.zh: 見聞有不平，輒憤起，忠懇之誠發於至性。

translations.literal: When he saw injustice he would flare up in anger; loyal sincerity arose from his deepest nature.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw injustice he would flare up in anger; loyal sincerity arose from his deepest nature.

sentences.zh: 念以英主被扼，每述及，常不勝哀痛。

translations.literal: Thinking of the Guangxu Emperor as a brilliant ruler constrained, whenever he spoke of it he could not overcome grief.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking of the Guangxu Emperor as a brilliant ruler constrained, whenever he spoke of it he could not overcome grief.

sentences.zh: 十謁，匍伏流涕。

translations.literal: Ten times he visited the Chongling mausoleum, prostrating himself in tears.
translations.idiomatic: Ten times he visited the Chongling mausoleum, prostrating himself in tears.

sentences.zh: 逢歲祭，雖風雪勿為阻。

translations.literal: At annual sacrifices, though wind and snow he would not be deterred.
translations.idiomatic: At annual sacrifices, wind and snow would not deter him.

sentences.zh: 嘗蒙賜御書「貞不絕俗」額，感幸無極，誓死必表於墓，曰「處士」。

translations.literal: He once received the imperial inscription "Upright yet not cut off from the world" and was infinitely grateful, swearing that at death he must inscribe it on his tomb as "Qing Recluse."
translations.idiomatic: He once received the imperial inscription "Upright yet not cut off from the world" and swore that at death he must inscribe it on his tomb as "Qing Recluse."

sentences.zh: 憂時傷事，一發之於詩文。

translations.literal: Anxiety for the age and sorrow for affairs he released entirely in poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: Anxiety for the age and sorrow for affairs he released entirely in poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 為文宗、。

translations.literal: In writing he took Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan as masters.
translations.idiomatic: In writing he took Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan as masters.

sentences.zh: 少時務博覽，中年後案頭唯有、二疏，、、及、之文，此外則、，無他書矣。

translations.literal: In youth he sought broad reading; after midlife his desk held only the two commentaries on the Odes and Rites, the Zuo Commentary, Records of the Grand Historian, Zhuangzi, and the writings of Han and Ouyang Xiu—besides these only the Shuowen and Guangya, no other books.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he sought broad reading; after midlife his desk held only the two commentaries on the Odes and Rites, the Zuo Commentary, Records of the Grand Historian, Zhuangzi, and the writings of Han and Ouyang Xiu—besides these only the Shuowen and Guangya.

sentences.zh: 其由博反約也如此。

translations.literal: Such was his turning from breadth to restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his turning from breadth to restraint.

sentences.zh: 其論文主意境、識度、氣勢、神韻，而忌率襲庸怪，文必己出。

translations.literal: In discussing writing he took artistic conception, discernment, momentum, and spirit as masters, yet hated slavish imitation, mediocrity, and strangeness; writing must come from oneself.
translations.idiomatic: In discussing writing he took artistic conception, discernment, momentum, and spirit as masters, yet hated slavish imitation and strangeness; writing must come from oneself.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「古文唯其理之獲，與道無悖者，則味之彌臻於無窮。

translations.literal: He once said: "In ancient prose only when principle is attained and nothing contradicts the Way does flavor grow endlessly more refined.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "In ancient prose only when principle is attained and nothing contradicts the Way does flavor grow endlessly more refined.

sentences.zh: 若分畫、、、，加以統系派別，為此為彼，使讀者炫惑莫知所從，則已格其途而左其趣。

translations.literal: If one divides Qin, Han, Tang, and Song and adds schools and factions, making this and that, until readers are dazzled and know not which to follow, one has already blocked the path and perverted the aim.
translations.idiomatic: If one divides Qin, Han, Tang, and Song into schools and factions until readers are dazzled and know not which to follow, one has blocked the path and perverted the aim.

sentences.zh: 經生之文樸，往往流入於枯淡，史家之文則又隳突恣肆，無復規檢，二者均不足以明道。

translations.literal: Classicists' writing is plain yet often flows into dryness; historians' writing is again reckless and unrestrained without rule—both are insufficient to illuminate the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Classicists' writing is plain yet often flows into dryness; historians' writing grows reckless without rule—both are insufficient to illuminate the Way.

sentences.zh: 唯積理養氣，偶成一篇，類若不得已者，必意在言先，修其辭而峻其防，外質而中膏，聲希而趣永，則庶乎其近矣。」

translations.literal: Only by accumulating principle and nurturing breath, occasionally completing a piece as if unable to help it, with intent before words, refining diction and tightening defenses, plain outside and rich within, sound rare and appeal enduring, may one approach it."
translations.idiomatic: Only by accumulating principle and nurturing breath, with intent before words, plain outside and rich within, sound rare and appeal enduring, may one approach it.

sentences.zh: 所作務抑遏掩蔽，能伏其光氣，而其真終不可自閟。

translations.literal: What he wrote strove to suppress and conceal, able to hide his light and breath, yet his truth could never be sealed away.
translations.idiomatic: What he wrote strove to suppress and conceal, hiding his light and breath, yet his truth could never be sealed away.

sentences.zh: 尤善敘悲，音吐淒梗，令人不忍卒讀。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at narrating sorrow; his voice was bitter and choked, making one unable to finish reading.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled at narrating sorrow; his voice was bitter and choked, unbearable to read through.

sentences.zh: 論者謂以血性為文章，不關學問也。

translations.literal: Critics said he wrote with innate nature, not depending on learning.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said he wrote with innate nature, not depending on learning.

sentences.zh: 所傳譯說部至百數十種。

translations.literal: He transmitted translated Western fiction to the number of more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He transmitted more than a hundred translated Western novels.

sentences.zh: 然故不習文，皆待人口達而筆述之。

translations.literal: Yet Shu did not know Western languages; all waited for oral transmission and then wrote them down.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shu did not know Western languages; all relied on oral transmission and then wrote them down.

sentences.zh: 任氣好辯，自新文學興，有倡非孝之說者，奮筆與爭，雖脅以威，累歲不為屈。

translations.literal: Bold in spirit and fond of debate, when new literature arose and some advocated rejecting filial piety, he took up his brush to contend; though threatened, for years he would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Bold in spirit and fond of debate, when new literature arose and some advocated rejecting filial piety, he contended in print; though threatened, for years he would not yield.

sentences.zh: 尤善畫，山水渾厚，冶南北於一爐，時皆寶之。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at painting; landscape was thick and full, blending Northern and Southern schools in one furnace, and the age all treasured it.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled at painting; his landscapes were thick and full, blending Northern and Southern schools, and the age treasured them.

sentences.zh: 講學不分門戶，嘗謂代學術之盛，超越今古，義理、考據，合而為一，而精博過之。

translations.literal: In lecturing he did not divide schools, once saying that Qing scholarly flourishing surpassed past and present, joining principle and evidential scholarship in one yet more refined and broad.
translations.idiomatic: In lecturing he did not divide schools, saying Qing scholarship surpassed past and present, joining principle and evidential scholarship yet more refined and broad.

sentences.zh: 實於學、學以外別創學一派。

translations.literal: Truly beyond Han Learning and Song Learning he created a Qing school.
translations.idiomatic: Truly beyond Han Learning and Song Learning he created a Qing school.

sentences.zh: 時有請立學會者，撫掌稱善，力贊其成。

translations.literal: When some requested establishing a Qing Learning Society, he clapped his hands in approval and strongly supported its completion.
translations.idiomatic: When some requested establishing a Qing Learning Society, he clapped his hands in approval and strongly supported it.

sentences.zh: 甲子秋，卒，年七十有三，門人私諡。

translations.literal: In the jiazi year of autumn he died at seventy-three; disciples privately titled him Master Zhenwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiazi year (1924) he died at seventy-three; disciples privately titled him Master Zhenwen.

translations.literal: He left the Weilu Prose Collection, poetry collection, On Literature, On Painting, and others.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Weilu Prose Collection, poetry collection, On Literature, and On Painting.

sentences.zh: 是時人士漸傾向西人學說，以為自由、平等、權利諸說，由之未嘗無利，脫靡所折衷，則流蕩放佚，害且不可勝言，常於廣眾中陳之。

translations.literal: At the time scholars gradually inclined toward Western doctrines; Fu held that doctrines of liberty, equality, and rights were not without benefit if properly balanced, but without moderation they led to dissipation and harm beyond measure, and he often stated this in public.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars gradually inclined toward Western doctrines; Fu held that liberty, equality, and rights were not without benefit if balanced, but without moderation led to dissipation and harm beyond measure, and he often stated this in public.

sentences.zh: 久以海軍積勞敘副將，盡棄去，入貲為同知，累保道員。

translations.literal: Fu long held naval merit at vice general rank, then abandoned it all, purchased office as subprefect, and was repeatedly promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Fu long held naval merit at vice general rank, then abandoned it, purchased office as subprefect, and was repeatedly promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 元年，海軍部立，特授協都統，尋賜文科進士，充學部總纂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong the Navy Ministry was established; he was specially appointed associate commander-in-chief, soon granted jinshi in letters and made general editor of the Terminology Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuantong (1909) the Navy Ministry was established; he was appointed associate commander-in-chief, soon granted jinshi in letters and made general editor of the Terminology Academy.

sentences.zh: 以碩學通儒徵為資政院議員。

translations.literal: As a profound scholar and Confucian he was summoned as a member of the Political Consultative Council.
translations.idiomatic: As a profound scholar he was summoned as a member of the Political Consultative Council.

sentences.zh: 三年，授海軍一等參謀官。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed first-class naval staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed first-class naval staff officer.

sentences.zh: 殫心著述，於學無所不窺，舉外治術學理，靡不究極原委，抉其失得，證明而會通之。

translations.literal: Fu devoted his heart to writing; in learning there was nothing he did not examine, whether Chinese or foreign methods of governance and principle, exhaustively tracing origins, judging gains and losses, proving and harmonizing them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu devoted himself to writing; in learning there was nothing he did not examine, tracing Chinese and foreign governance and principle, judging gains and losses, proving and harmonizing them.

sentences.zh: 精西文字，所譯書以朅辭達奧旨。

translations.literal: Expert in Western writing, his translations used refined diction to convey profound meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Expert in Western languages, his translations used refined diction to convey profound meaning.

sentences.zh: 其有曰：「之於六藝也，、最嚴。

translations.literal: His preface to Evolution and Ethics says: "Confucius regarding the Six Arts, the Changes and Spring and Autumn are most strict.
translations.idiomatic: His preface to Evolution and Ethics says, "Confucius regarding the Six Arts, the Changes and Spring and Autumn are most strict.

sentences.zh: 曰：『本隱而之顯，推見至隱。』

translations.literal: Sima Qian said: 'The Changes proceeds from the hidden to the manifest; the Spring and Autumn infers the most hidden from what is seen.' These are the most refined words under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian said, 'The Changes proceeds from the hidden to the manifest; the Spring and Autumn infers the most hidden from what is seen.' These are the most refined words under heaven.

sentences.zh: 此天下至精之言也。

translations.literal: This is the most refined speech under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: This is the most refined speech under heaven.

sentences.zh: 始吾以為本隱之顯者，觀像繫辭，以定吉凶而已；

translations.literal: At first I thought 'from the hidden to the manifest' meant observing images and attached phrases to determine fortune and misfortune;
translations.idiomatic: At first I thought 'from the hidden to the manifest' meant observing images and attached phrases to determine fortune and misfortune;

sentences.zh: 推見至隱者，誅意褒貶而已。

translations.literal: Inferring the most hidden meant judging intent in praise and blame.
translations.idiomatic: Inferring the most hidden meant judging intent in praise and blame.

sentences.zh: 及觀西人名學，則見其格物致知之事，有內籀之術焉，有外籀之術焉。

translations.literal: Observing Western logic, I saw that in investigating things to extend knowledge there is inner induction and outer induction.
translations.idiomatic: Observing Western logic, I saw that in investigating things to extend knowledge there is inner induction and outer induction.

sentences.zh: 內籀云者，察其曲而知其全者也，執其微以會其通者也。

translations.literal: Inner induction observes the part to know the whole and grasps the subtle to unite with the general.
translations.idiomatic: Inner induction observes the part to know the whole and grasps the subtle to unite with the general.

sentences.zh: 外籀云者，援公理以斷眾事者也，設定數以逆未然者也。

translations.literal: Outer induction applies public reason to judge many cases and sets constants to anticipate what has not yet occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Outer induction applies public reason to judge many cases and sets constants to anticipate what has not yet occurred.

sentences.zh: 是固吾、之學也。

translations.literal: This is indeed the learning of our Changes and Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: This is indeed the learning of our Changes and Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 所謂『本隱之顯』者外籀也，所謂『推見至隱』者內籀也，二者即物窮理之要術也。

translations.literal: What Qian called 'from the hidden to the manifest' is outer induction; what he called 'inferring the most hidden' is inner induction—both are essential techniques of investigating things to exhaust principle.
translations.idiomatic: What Qian called 'from the hidden to the manifest' is outer induction; 'inferring the most hidden' is inner induction—both are essential techniques of investigating things to exhaust principle.

sentences.zh: 夫西學之最為切實，而執其例可以御蕃變者，名、數、質、力四者之學而已。

translations.literal: Among Western learning what is most practical and whose examples can master manifold change are only the four studies of names, numbers, matter, and force.
translations.idiomatic: Among Western learning what is most practical and whose examples can master change are the four studies of names, numbers, matter, and force.

sentences.zh: 而吾則名、數以為經，質、力以為律，而合而名之曰『易​​』。

translations.literal: Our Changes takes names and numbers as warp and matter and force as woof, combining them and calling it 'Change.'
translations.idiomatic: Our Changes takes names and numbers as warp and matter and force as woof, combining them as 'Change.'

sentences.zh: 大宇之內，質、力相推，非質無以見力，非力無以呈質。

translations.literal: Within the great universe matter and force push each other; without matter force cannot appear, without force matter cannot be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Within the great universe matter and force push each other; without matter force cannot appear, without force matter cannot be displayed.

sentences.zh: 凡力皆乾也，凡質皆坤也。

translations.literal: All force is Qian; all matter is Kun.
translations.idiomatic: All force is Qian; all matter is Kun.

sentences.zh: 動之例三，其一曰：『靜者不自動，動者不自止，動路必直，速率必均。』

translations.literal: Newton's three laws of motion: first, what is at rest does not move itself; what moves does not stop itself; the path of motion must be straight and the rate uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Newton's three laws of motion: what is at rest does not move itself; what moves does not stop itself; the path must be straight and the rate uniform.

sentences.zh: 而則曰：『乾，其靜也專，其動也直。』

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'Qian in stillness is concentrated; in motion is straight.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, 'Qian in stillness is concentrated; in motion is straight.'

sentences.zh: 有者，以天演自然言化，其為天演界說曰：『翕以合質，闢以出力，始簡易而終雜糅。』

translations.literal: Spencer, speaking of evolution by natural change, states in his definition of evolution: 'Contracting to unite matter, expanding to exert force, beginning simple and ending complex.'
translations.idiomatic: Spencer, speaking of evolution, states: 'Contracting to unite matter, expanding to exert force, beginning simple and ending complex.'

sentences.zh: 而則曰：『坤，其靜也翕，其動也闢。』

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'Kun in stillness is contracting; in motion is expanding.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, 'Kun in stillness is contracting; in motion is expanding.'

sentences.zh: 至於全力不增減之說，則有自強不息為之先；

translations.literal: As for the doctrine that total force neither increases nor decreases, there is self-strengthening without cease beforehand;
translations.idiomatic: As for total force neither increasing nor decreasing, there is self-strengthening without cease beforehand;

sentences.zh: 凡動必復之說，則有消息之義居其始。

translations.literal: the doctrine that all motion must return has the meaning of message and decay at the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: the doctrine that all motion must return has the meaning of waxing and waning at the beginning.

sentences.zh: 而『易不可見，乾坤或幾乎息』之旨，尤與熱力平均、天地乃毀之言相發明也。

translations.literal: The point that 'Change cannot be seen; Qian and Kun perhaps nearly cease' especially illuminates heat equilibrium and the saying that heaven and earth will be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The point that 'Change cannot be seen; Qian and Kun perhaps nearly cease' especially illuminates heat equilibrium and the end of heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 大抵古書難讀，為尤。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking ancient books are hard to read, and China especially so.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking ancient books are hard to read, and China especially so.

sentences.zh: 二千年來，士徇利祿，守闕殘，無獨闢之慮，是以生今日者，乃轉於西學得識古之用焉。」

translations.literal: For two thousand years scholars pursued emolument, guarding what was incomplete without independent pioneering thought; therefore those born today turn to Western learning to know the use of antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: For two thousand years scholars pursued emolument, guarding incomplete learning without pioneering thought; therefore those born today turn to Western learning to recover the use of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 凡所譯著，獨得精微皆類此。

translations.literal: All his translations and writings that grasped subtlety were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: All his translations and writings that grasped subtlety were of this kind.

sentences.zh: 世謂以文溝通西文，以西文溝通文，並稱「」。

translations.literal: The age said Shu used Chinese to bridge Western writing and Fu used Western writing to bridge Chinese, both styled "Lin-Yan."
translations.idiomatic: The age said Shu used Chinese to bridge Western writing and Fu used Western writing to bridge Chinese, both styled "Lin-Yan."

sentences.zh: 辛酉秋，卒，年六十有九。

translations.literal: In the xinyou year of autumn he died at sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinyou year (1921) he died at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 著有及譯、、、、、、等。

translations.literal: He authored a prose collection and translations including Evolution and Ethics, Wealth of Nations, Study of Sociology, Mill's Logic, Spirit of Laws, On Liberty, and Principles of Sociology.
translations.idiomatic: He authored a prose collection and translations including Evolution and Ethics, Wealth of Nations, Study of Sociology, Mill's Logic, Spirit of Laws, On Liberty, and Principles of Sociology.

sentences.zh: 同時有，字，人。

translations.literal: At the same time there was Gu Hongming, styled Hongming, a native of Tong'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was Gu Hongming of Tong'an, styled Hongming.

sentences.zh: 幼學於，為博士。

translations.literal: He studied in England in youth and became a doctor.
translations.idiomatic: He studied in England in youth and became a doctor.

sentences.zh: 遍遊、、、諸邦，通其政藝。

translations.literal: He traveled Germany, France, Italy, Austria, and other states, mastering their governance and arts.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled Germany, France, Italy, Austria, and other states, mastering their governance and arts.

sentences.zh: 年三十始返而求學術，窮、之奧，兼涉群籍。

translations.literal: At thirty he returned to seek Chinese learning, exhausting the profundity of the Four Books and Five Classics, also ranging through many books.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty he returned to seek Chinese learning, exhausting the Four Books and Five Classics, also ranging through many books.

sentences.zh: 爽然曰：「道在是矣！」

translations.literal: He said with clarity: "The Way is here!"
translations.idiomatic: He exclaimed with clarity, "The Way is here!

sentences.zh: 乃譯，述大義及禮制諸書。

translations.literal: He then translated the Four Books and expounded the great meaning of the Spring and Autumn and books on ritual institutions.
translations.idiomatic: He then translated the Four Books and expounded the Spring and Autumn and books on ritual institutions.

sentences.zh: 西人見之，始歎學理之精，爭起傳譯。

translations.literal: Westerners, seeing this, first sighed at the refinement of Chinese learning and rose to translate it.
translations.idiomatic: Westerners, seeing this, first sighed at the refinement of Chinese learning and rose to translate it.

sentences.zh: 庚子亂，聯軍北犯，以文草，申大義。

translations.literal: In the gengzi Boxer turmoil, allied armies invaded north; Hongming drafted the Revering the King in English to declare the great principle.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengzi Boxer turmoil, allied armies invaded north; Hongming drafted Revering the King in English to declare the great principle.

sentences.zh: 列強知以禮教立國，終不可侮，和議乃就、

translations.literal: The powers knew China was founded on ritual teaching and could not be insulted; peace was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The powers knew China was founded on ritual teaching and could not be insulted; peace was then settled.

sentences.zh: 皆奇其才，歷委辦議約、濬浦等事。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhidong and Zhou Fu all marveled at his talent and successively entrusted him with treaty negotiations and dredging harbors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhidong and Zhou Fu all marveled at his talent and entrusted him with treaty negotiations and dredging harbors.

sentences.zh: 旋為外務部員外郎，晉郎中，擢左丞。

translations.literal: Soon he served as vice director of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, was promoted to director, and rose to left vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he served as vice director of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, was promoted to director, and rose to left vice minister.
